chapters.title: Chapter 4830: Integrations and Memories I
paragraphs: The area became filled with Immensity and tension as two sides looked at each other.

Power pressed down over everything in the realm of Alfheimr, the crystalline trees bending under the weight of concentrated authority, the rivers of liquid radiance slowing their flow as if even they recognized the significance of this moment.
Elemental’s fury was palpable, a heat that made the air around him shimmer.
Emotive’s smile never wavered, but her eyes held something calculating beneath the manic surface.
And Noah stood between them and his people, an illusory presence that somehow carried more weight than the physical reality around it.
The confrontation hung suspended in time.
Two sides measuring each other.
Two powers determining whether this moment would escalate into something worse.
And then, slowly, with the reluctance of beings who understood now was not the time, THE Living Elemental and THE Living Emotive began to withdraw.
Not because they feared the fight.
Not because they feared!
While such a confrontation unfolded in Alfheimr, while illusory Noah faced down Absolutes with nothing but authority and accumulated weight, another body moved across entirely different territory.
Far from the crystalline forests.
Across The Wastes of THE Fallout.
Noah’s physical body floated through corrupted space alongside Ains and a happy Skoll who bounded through the twisted reality as if it were nothing more than an interesting playground.

The Wastes stretched out around them in all directions, a landscape of collapsed concepts and shattered foundations. Where other regions of Observable Existence held some form of structure, some remnant of what they had been before THE Fallout, this place was pure devastation given form.
Reality twisted in on itself.
Concepts that had no business existing together merged and separated in patterns that defied comprehension.
The very fabric of Existence had been torn apart here, and what remained was something that should not have been able to exist at all.
And yet life persisted.
Of a sort.

Noah navigated through the corrupted Weavings with the ease. His connection to Undifferentiated Fate guided his path, threads of possibility weaving through the chaos to show him where he needed to go.
They arrived near a region of the Wastes that held nothing but twisting corrupted existence.
No landmarks.
No structures.
Nothing that could be used as a reference point.
Just endless corruption folding back on itself in patterns that would have driven lesser minds to madness.
And yet Noah knew this was the place.
He called out calmly, his voice moving across the corrupted space with authority that cut through the ambient chaos.
"Big guy, how did you let something else emerge that does what you do, but countless times deadlier?"
The words hung in the twisted air, a question directed at something that should not have been able to hear them.
They had arrived where the Weavings of Undifferentiated Fate told him Eckert was.
THE Great Usurper!
With Undifferentiated Fate, Noah was able to gain information he had no business knowing, especially if he had a few pieces of information already as Eckert gave him.

So he knew thst currently, Eckert had merged with a Fragment of THE Axiom of Primordial Paradox and become something that existed outside normal classification. The being who had learned to spread his existence through idle contact, to take over the Weavings of others without them even realizing what was happening.

To understand THE Entity a bit better, to find some pathway that might lead to a potential solution against a threat that had claimed multiple Absolutes, one of the approaches Noah had identified was consulting with an entity he knew who could do what THE Entity did.
But at a much smaller scale.
The mechanisms were different, the scale was incomparable, but the fundamental principle of replacing what was there with something else held common ground.

If anyone in Observable Existence might have insight into how such a process worked, how it might be countered, how one might protect against an infection that could claim even Absolutes without them realizing until it was too late, it would be THE Great Usurper.
The corrupted space around them stirred.
Something was responding to Noah’s call.
Something that had been idle, spreading slowly through The Wastes!
Skoll’s ears perked up, his form tensing as he sensed something approaching that registered as neither friend nor foe, but something else entirely.
In front of him, Noah perceived existence silently converging and forming into a humanoid visage.

The corrupted space of The Wastes twisted and folded, reality reshaping itself to accommodate something that existed in ways that defied normal perception. Particles of scattered existence drew together like iron filings responding to a magnet, coalescing into a shape that grew more defined with each passing moment.
Eckert.
THE Great Usurper.

When one thought of such a title, they might imagine an ancient being weathered by eons of existence. Something gnarled and powerful, holding the weight of countless devoured lives in every aspect of its form.
But what materialized in front of Noah was the image of a young man in his twenties.

The visage was colorless, an illusory humanoid shape with no pigmentation beyond shades of gray and white. His features were handsome in a casual way, relaxed and unburdened. His smile was easy, genuine, the expression of someone greeting an old friend rather than one of the most dangerous beings in Observable Existence.
It was deceptive.

Because Noah knew this being had devoured the existences and memories of countless others. Every smile, every casual gesture, every aspect of that youthful appearance was built upon the consumed foundations of beings who no longer existed.
The young man’s form stabilized completely, his colorless eyes finding Noah’s with recognition and something like relief.
And then he did something unexpected.
Eckert moved forward with easy confidence, his hand coming up in a gesture of familiarity rather than the formal greetings.
He...dapped Noah up!
Noah raised his brows but went along with it. His hand met Eckert’s in a clasp!
"Man."
Eckert’s voice came out with exhaustion.
"I’ve been going nuts trying to figure out the extent of change across Observable Existence."
He shook his head.
"What’s this about someone doing what I can do at a crazy scale?"

chapters.title: Chapter 4831: Integrations and Memories II
paragraphs: The question hung in the corrupted air between them.

It was time to catch up and learn more about Eckert and what he could do, to understand the mechanisms of his unique methodology, and to compare it to THE Entity to see how one might go against a threat that had already claimed multiple Absolutes.
Because if anyone understood the process of replacing what was there with something else, of spreading through existence itself to consume and become, it would be THE Great Usurper!
And right now, understanding was the most valuable weapon Noah could acquire.
While all of this occurred across The Wastes, a part of him continued to pay attention to the major changes unfolding within THE Infiniverse.
His Civilization was growing exponentially.

The connection between himself and THE Infiniverse meant that every advancement he achieved fed directly into the realm that served as the heart of everything he’d built. And now, as it assimilated an entire Primordial Realm into itself, that growth was accelerating beyond anything he’d previously experienced.
At this moment.

In the sandy Early Veiled Shore at the center of THE Infiniverse, Noah had another body moving alongside his mother as the two of them harvested sacred herbs he’d brought over from the Shore of THE Creature.

The herbs glowed with soft luminescence, each one a treasure that would’ve caused wars among lesser beings. Yet here they grew in abundance, nurtured by conditions that existed nowhere else in Observable Existence.
His mother moved with practiced ease, her presence a grounding force that reminded Noah of who he’d been before all of this.
Existence was wild and ridiculous, but he could always make time to spend it with the important people in his life.

Many others moved all over the Early Veiled Shore. In the distance, he could see his son Henry surrounded by two women as he cooked marine lifeforms in a Wok filled with sacred water. Steam rose in patterns that spoke of culinary mastery applied to ingredients that transcended normal food.
Off to the side, the bald figure of Bob watched like a hawk. Little Bobby!

His attention was fixed on his daughter Liora, who was laughing beside Henry with easy joy. Bob’s protective gaze never wavered, the concern of a father who’d been through too much to ever truly relax.
After all, this man had burned entire Wheels of Existence for his daughter! Not to mention Thauron. He missed that guy!
Barbatos, Adelaide, Athena, and all the other Queens of THE Infiniverse moved about with their own busyness and tasks.
None of them knew whatever grand enemy now stood above them. None of them knew about THE Entity, about the infection that had claimed multiple Absolutes.
And they didn’t have to worry about this.
Because Noah would shoulder everything to protect those under his Civilization.

Even further in the distance, he could see the Sanctuaries of Inevitabilities. Tens of millions of Primus Inevitabilities moved around like an army, each one a being of tremendous potential being cultivated under his authority.
The day when he could turn these millions into Surface Depth entities, have an army at the first Scale of Existence, all specialized into unique professions...
That was the day when it would be game over for many.
But as of now, it was still a distant future away.
At this time, Noah began to feel the golden sands trembling beneath his feet.

A hint of red permeated the air above, mixing with streams of blue. The influence of Muspelheim being devoured was becoming extremely strong, its essence bleeding into THE Infiniverse as the integration progressed toward completion.
Prompts bloomed.
|Integration Milestone Achieved|
|More than half of Muspelheim has been integrated into THE Infiniverse|
|Unique Musings of Existence have been discovered|
|I spent an embarrassing amount of processing power analyzing why Muspelheim produced so many THE classification entities when other realms struggled to produce a few|
|The answer, it turns out, was not some grand mystery|
Unique Musings of Existence.
Noah stopped where he was on the plot of farmland. He closed his eyes and allowed the Immensity of THE Weaver of Existence to spread outward.

The First Tongue erupted from him in a low hum. The Derivative Civilizations of Hunger and Undifferentiated Fate stirred within his foundations, ready to consume and process whatever information emerged.
|Primordial Realm Analysis|
|Muspelheim functioned as a pivotal convergence of immense Weavings of The First Tongue, similar to Ginnungagap|
|Over the eons, countless Corrupted Growths were drawn toward this Primordial Realm like it was some kind of drain|
|These corrupted elements were cleansed, and the pure Civilizational Authority that resulted simply... accumulated|
|This explains why so many Muspeli Lifeforms achieved THE classification|
|They were being fed concentrated purity while everyone else had to earn advancement the hard way|
|Fragment Discovery|
|Multiple Fragments of Axioms have been sensed and obtained|
|Currently being catalogued|
|Infiniverse Transformation|
|As integration proceeds, THE Infiniverse is transforming to become a unique component of Observable Existence|
|Corrupted Growths will begin to naturally be drawn toward THE Infiniverse|
|With these Growths being cleansed automatically, all the pure Civilizational Authority that blooms will feed back into your home|
|This creates a feedback loop of glorious proportions|
|Most beings spend eons trying to establish something like this|
|You stumbled into it while eating a Primordial Realm|
|Collaborative Analysis|
|THE Infiniverse and I are designing similar Musings of Existence to THE Agora of Primordial Judgment and THE Vaults of Ginnungagap|
|Purpose: To better understand the positions of Primordial Realms in relation to Observable Existence|
|This is genuinely complex work|
|Population Influx|
|Muspeli Lifeforms are beginning to be drawn into THE Infiniverse|
|A not-so-insignificant number are at the first Scale of Existence|
|This increases the infinite potential of the Harvest you draw for all those under your Civilization|
|All of this continues feeding your growing Foundation|
|Foundation Status|
|THE Surface Depth: Approaching theoretical perfection|
|THE Intermediate Depth: Approaching theoretical perfection|
|THE Fundamental Depth: Slowly, slowly, slowly creeping toward what THE Creature and THE Primordial Chaos achieved in the distant past|
|Slowly, even though measuring your progress against beings who had eons feels unreasonable|
|You’ve had hours as this really isn’t slow. Even if it was days, it would still be considered an impossibility.|
Can you imagine it? If his progression actually took him days or weeks to go from Surface to Intermediate Depth?
Or if he needed years to attain Fundamental Depth or Absolute? Because normally, others took thousands and millions of years!
He shivered just thinking of such a possibility!

chapters.title: Chapter 4832: Integrations and Memories III
paragraphs: Noah read through the prompts with his eyes closed.
And he saw it.
Murky Corrupted Growths converging toward THE Infiniverse as if drawn by forces beyond their understanding. They painted over the barrier outside like a disease seeking entry.
But as soon as they touched those boundaries, a silent glow of heavy Depth emerged.
The Corrupted Growths were rapidly dissipated, dissolved like shadows before dawn. What had been twisted and wrong became clean and pure, transformed into golden light that flowed into his home.
Was this why THE Vaults of Ginnungagap were so grand? Why THE Agora of Primordial Judgment held so many THE classification entities and four Absolutes?

They’d been cleansing Corrupted Growths for eons, accumulating the pure Civilizational Authority that resulted. They’d become stronger through the natural process of serving as nodes that attracted and purified corruption.
And now THE Infiniverse was beginning to do the same.
His home was becoming a Primordial Realm in truth, not just in name.
More prompts bloomed.
|Absolute Everything Generation|
|Progress toward next Absolute Everything: 10%|
|In conjunction with your personal cleansing and what THE Infiniverse now does automatically, another Absolute Everything will be ready soon? Soon|
|Potential applications:|
|- Take another Half-Step Absolute toward Absolute|
|- Assuming they’re all as grand as THE Big Stepper, which is admittedly a high bar|
|- Other purposes as you determine|
Many things were coming up as possibilities.
His progression proceeded steadily, foundations being reinforced with every passing moment, every cleansed Corrupted Growth, every piece of harvested authority flowing into his Civilization.
And there was still so much more to do.

In addition to pursuing information about THE Entity through Eckert, he now knew the locations of The Shelters of THE Loom from obtaining Undifferentiated Fate. The places where THE Living Paradox’s forces gathered. The strongholds that had seemed unreachable before.
He wanted to pay a visit to them.

And alongside that, there were the memories of THE Weavers themselves. He’d sent another part of his consciousness toward their Absolute Existential Palace to sift through what remained of their accumulated understanding.
If he had more information, more knowledge, he could move through Existence even grander than before. After all, knowing the right things was everything.

He even had his own personal growth to consider. The continued nurturing of the 27 Absolute Seals. The Archai he’d formed...Perpetual Harvest, Cheating Architect, Undifferentiated Mana...each holding new avenues to express his power as he neared Absolute.
There was much to be done.
So much to be done!
In Observable Existence, there is a creature calledTHEMnemonic Leviathan.

It dwells in the spaces between Primordial Realms, its body composed entirely of accumulated information.Every secret whispered across eons, every truth discovered and forgotten, every piece of knowledge that ever existed flows through its endless form. It knows everything.
And... it has never done anything.

THE Mnemonic Leviathandrifts through Existence, bloated with understanding it cannot apply, suffocating under the weight of wisdom it cannot wield. It knows how Absolutes fall. It knows how Civilizations rise. It knows...the weaknesses of Absolutes that others dont know.
It knows, and it watches, and it does nothing at all.

Those who have witnessed eons say that knowledge alone is the most useless currency in Observable Existence. They have seen beings accumulate libraries of understanding only to be collapsed by someone who knew a single truth and acted upon it without hesitation. They have watched empires built not by the most informed, but by those who treated every scrap of knowledge as a weapon demanding immediate use.
Because in the end, knowledge hoarded is knowledge wasted.
But knowledge applied is transformation itself.
The gap between knowing and doing is where most beings live their entire existences, comfortable in their accumulation, paralyzed by their wisdom, convinced that understanding is the same as power.
It is not.
Power belongs to those who learn one truth and move before the lesson has finished settling in their minds.
Knowledge was everything, so Noah proceeded to go and seek it.

There was knowledge to be gained in THE Agora of Primordial Judgment and whatever secrets it might hold that made THE Secretive Eon refuse to enter. There were answers waiting to be found, protections waiting to be understood, weapons waiting to be claimed.
And then there was the Absolute Existential Palace of THE Weavers.

His consciousness was already walking through its halls once more, moving through corridors that seemed to shift and breathe with the remnants of three minds that had once shared a single existence. The architecture was strange here, walls that curved in ways that suggested different perspectives overlapping, doorways that appeared different depending on which angle you approached them from.
He entered a region filled with multiple golden doors.

Dozens of them. Hundreds. Each one sealed with locks and chains that pulsed with residual authority, the final protections of beings who had accumulated secrets across eons of service to powers that shaped Observable Existence itself.
Doorways to memories of THE Weavers.
To access any of them, one would have to expend a tremendous amount of power and Depth. Even in death, THE Weavers wanted to be tricky fuckers.
They had woven protections into their own memories, ensuring that anyone who sought their knowledge would pay dearly for every scrap of understanding they obtained.
Noah walked across the hall filled with golden doors as he utilized Undifferentiated Fate to lead him forward toward the best possible result he could find at this moment.
The Derivative Civilization stirred within his foundations, its authority spreading outward like ink dropped into water.

Tendrils of golden-blue light swirled around him, emerging from his existence like extensions of his will made manifest. They moved with purpose that transcended conscious direction, reaching out like hands toward each of the doors around him. They pressed against locks, brushed against chains, tested seals that had held for eons.
Checking.
Affirming.
Reading the threads of fate and destiny that connected each door to potential futures.

Some tendrils recoiled from doors that held nothing of value. Others lingered on doors that contained useful but not critical information. A few pressed harder against doors that held secrets worth the cost of opening.
But eventually, many of them gathered on one inconspicuous golden door.
It wasn’t the largest door. It wasn’t the most ornately decorated. It sat between two grander entrances as if trying not to be noticed, its chains slightly less imposing than those on its neighbors.
The tendrils of Undifferentiated Fate wrapped around it with certainty that brooked no doubt.
This one.
Noah nodded and floated toward it.

He put his hand on the locks and chains surrounding the door, feeling the weight of protections that THE Weavers had laid down across countless years. They pushed back against him, testing his authority, questioning whether he had the right to access what lay within.
In the next moment, he leaned forward.
He pressed the ridiculous Immensity of the weight of his entire existence into these chains.

The foundation that approached what THE Creature and THE Primordial Chaos had built across eons. The 27 Seals of Absolute Tongue burning with concentrated authority. The Claim on The First Tongue itself, the linguistic foundation of reality pressing against protections that had never been designed to withstand such weight.
CRACK!
The chains cracked and fell down, clattering against the floor of the hallway with sounds that echoed through the empty palace.
The golden door began to open in front of him.
Noah stepped through.

Existence began to turn hazy all around him, reality losing its definition as memory replaced perception. The hallway faded. The palace faded. Everything that was now faded into everything that had been then.
And he blinked.
Shockingly, he found his consciousness split into three.

He was looking through the eyes of three people simultaneously, three perspectives that somehow merged into a single experience. It was disorienting , his sense of self fragmenting across multiple viewpoints that moved and thought and felt as one.
In this memory, it was like Noah was living through the eyes of THE Weavers themselves!

The Corrupted Growths were rapidly dissipated, dissolved like shadows before dawn.
What had been twisted and wrong became clean and pure, transformed into golden light that flowed into his home.
Was this why THE Vaults of Ginnungagap were so grand?
Why THE Agora of Primordial Judgment held so many THE classification entities and four Absolutes?
They’d been cleansing Corrupted Growths for eons, accumulating the pure Civilizational Authority that resulted.
They’d become stronger through the natural process of serving as nodes that attracted and purified corruption.
And now THE Infiniverse was beginning to do the same.
His home was becoming a Primordial Realm in truth, not just in name.
More prompts bloomed.
|Absolute Everything Generation|
|Progress toward next Absolute Everything: 10%|
|In conjunction with your personal cleansing and what THE Infiniverse now does automatically, another Absolute Everything will be ready soon?
Soon|
|Potential applications:|
|- Take another Half-Step Absolute toward Absolute|
|- Assuming they’re all as grand as THE Big Stepper, which is admittedly a high bar|
|- Other purposes as you determine|
Many things were coming up as possibilities.
His progression proceeded steadily, foundations being reinforced with every passing moment, every cleansed Corrupted Growth, every piece of harvested authority flowing into his Civilization.
And there was still so much more to do.
In addition to pursuing information about THE Entity through Eckert, he now knew the locations of The Shelters of THE Loom from obtaining Undifferentiated Fate.
The places where THE Living Paradox’s forces gathered.
The strongholds that had seemed unreachable before.
He wanted to pay a visit to them.
And alongside that, there were the memories of THE Weavers themselves.
He’d sent another part of his consciousness toward their Absolute Existential Palace to sift through what remained of their accumulated understanding.
If he had more information, more knowledge, he could move through Existence even grander than before.
After all, knowing the right things was everything.
He even had his own personal growth to consider.
The continued nurturing of the 27 Absolute Seals.
The Archai he’d formed...Perpetual Harvest, Cheating Architect, Undifferentiated Mana...each holding new avenues to express his power as he neared Absolute.
There was much to be done.
So much to be done!
In Observable Existence, there is a creature calledTHEMnemonic Leviathan.

It dwells in the spaces between Primordial Realms, its body composed entirely of accumulated information.Every secret whispered across eons, every truth discovered and forgotten, every piece of knowledge that ever existed flows through its endless form.
It knows everything.
And... it has never done anything.
THE Mnemonic Leviathandrifts through Existence, bloated with understanding it cannot apply, suffocating under the weight of wisdom it cannot wield.
It knows how Absolutes fall.
It knows how Civilizations rise.
It knows...the weaknesses of Absolutes that others dont know.
It knows, and it watches, and it does nothing at all.
Those who have witnessed eons say that knowledge alone is the most useless currency in Observable Existence.
They have seen beings accumulate libraries of understanding only to be collapsed by someone who knew a single truth and acted upon it without hesitation.
They have watched empires built not by the most informed, but by those who treated every scrap of knowledge as a weapon demanding immediate use.
Because in the end, knowledge hoarded is knowledge wasted.
But knowledge applied is transformation itself.
The gap between knowing and doing is where most beings live their entire existences, comfortable in their accumulation, paralyzed by their wisdom, convinced that understanding is the same as power.
It is not.
Power belongs to those who learn one truth and move before the lesson has finished settling in their minds.
Knowledge was everything, so Noah proceeded to go and seek it.
There was knowledge to be gained in THE Agora of Primordial Judgment and whatever secrets it might hold that made THE Secretive Eon refuse to enter.
There were answers waiting to be found, protections waiting to be understood, weapons waiting to be claimed.
And then there was the Absolute Existential Palace of THE Weavers.
His consciousness was already walking through its halls once more, moving through corridors that seemed to shift and breathe with the remnants of three minds that had once shared a single existence.
The architecture was strange here, walls that curved in ways that suggested different perspectives overlapping, doorways that appeared different depending on which angle you approached them from.
He entered a region filled with multiple golden doors.
Dozens of them.
Hundreds.

Each one sealed with locks and chains that pulsed with residual authority, the final protections of beings who had accumulated secrets across eons of service to powers that shaped Observable Existence itself.
Doorways to memories of THE Weavers.
To access any of them, one would have to expend a tremendous amount of power and Depth.
Even in death, THE Weavers wanted to be tricky fuckers.
They had woven protections into their own memories, ensuring that anyone who sought their knowledge would pay dearly for every scrap of understanding they obtained.
Noah walked across the hall filled with golden doors as he utilized Undifferentiated Fate to lead him forward toward the best possible result he could find at this moment.
The Derivative Civilization stirred within his foundations, its authority spreading outward like ink dropped into water.
Tendrils of golden-blue light swirled around him, emerging from his existence like extensions of his will made manifest.
They moved with purpose that transcended conscious direction, reaching out like hands toward each of the doors around him.
They pressed against locks, brushed against chains, tested seals that had held for eons.
Checking.
Affirming.
Reading the threads of fate and destiny that connected each door to potential futures.
Some tendrils recoiled from doors that held nothing of value.
Others lingered on doors that contained useful but not critical information.
A few pressed harder against doors that held secrets worth the cost of opening.
But eventually, many of them gathered on one inconspicuous golden door.
It wasn’t the largest door.
It wasn’t the most ornately decorated.
It sat between two grander entrances as if trying not to be noticed, its chains slightly less imposing than those on its neighbors.
The tendrils of Undifferentiated Fate wrapped around it with certainty that brooked no doubt.
This one.
Noah nodded and floated toward it.
He put his hand on the locks and chains surrounding the door, feeling the weight of protections that THE Weavers had laid down across countless years.
They pushed back against him, testing his authority, questioning whether he had the right to access what lay within.
In the next moment, he leaned forward.
He pressed the ridiculous Immensity of the weight of his entire existence into these chains.
The foundation that approached what THE Creature and THE Primordial Chaos had built across eons.
The 27 Seals of Absolute Tongue burning with concentrated authority.
The Claim on The First Tongue itself, the linguistic foundation of reality pressing against protections that had never been designed to withstand such weight.
CRACK!
The chains cracked and fell down, clattering against the floor of the hallway with sounds that echoed through the empty palace.
The golden door began to open in front of him.
Noah stepped through.
Existence began to turn hazy all around him, reality losing its definition as memory replaced perception.
The hallway faded.
The palace faded.
Everything that was now faded into everything that had been then.
And he blinked.
Shockingly, he found his consciousness split into three.
He was looking through the eyes of three people simultaneously, three perspectives that somehow merged into a single experience.
It was disorienting , his sense of self fragmenting across multiple viewpoints that moved and thought and felt as one.
In this memory, it was like Noah was living through the eyes of THE Weavers themselves!

chapters.title: Chapter 4833: Integrations and Memories IV
paragraphs: He raised his hands to see the fair hands of three women, slender fingers that had woven the fates of countless beings across eons of existence. All of them wore obsidian-gold robes that flowed like liquid night, waves of golden hair cascading past their shoulders in styles that were similar but not identical.
Three bodies.
One memory that he was now experiencing from the inside.
The region around them slowly came into focus.

They stood on the stair steps of a massive obsidian temple, a structure so vast that its upper reaches disappeared into darkness that seemed to exist beyond normal space. The stairs were wide enough for armies to march upon, each step carved from stone that held the weight of ages.
Pillars of twisted obsidian rose on either side, their surfaces inscribed with symbols that hurt to look at directly.
And at the very center of this temple, at the apex of those endless stairs, a single aura waited.
THE Weavers walked toward this entity.
With each step, Noah felt the veneration that pulsed through their shared existence. The respect. The devotion. The absolute certainty that they approached something heavy.
The entity came into Noah’s vision.
And he felt like he was looking at the eye of a paradoxical storm.
Because he was.
This was...THE Primordial Paradox.

Yes, the memory was clearly telling him that this was THE Primordial Paradox.Not THE Living Paradox. The original holder of that Claim, the being who had stood among THE Four since before The Infinite Unfurling.

THE Primordial Paradox looked like a massive obsidian entity, his form towering above THE Weavers with presence that made reality itself seem uncertain. He was muscular in ways that spoke of power beyond physical strength, yet he also carried the bearing of a scholar.
His eyes held the weight of contradictions resolved and unresolved, of truths that could be simultaneously real and unreal.
He was everything THE Living Paradox pretended to be.
And he was something more.

In the memory, THE Weavers felt a sense of veneration as they bowed toward this being. Their three bodies moved in perfect synchrony, heads lowering, golden hair falling forward like curtains of loyalty.
THE Primordial Paradox waved his hands dismissively.
The gesture was casual, almost paternal. The wave of a master who had long since ceased to require formal acknowledgment from those who served him.
In the next moment, the aura of something heavy and Absolute emanated from him.

THE Primordial Paradox produced a black cube that floated toward their master, its surface perfectly smooth, its edges perfectly defined. It held weight that seemed to press against the fabric of memory itself.
Absolute!
THE Primordial Paradox was already an Absolute. His authority saturated everything around him, his Claim on Paradox itself woven into the very structure of Observable Existence.
So how did THE Living Paradox ever manage to consume both this entity and the Claim they laid on one of the oldest aspects of Existence?
The question burned through Noah’s consciousness even as the memory continued to unfold.
THE Primordial Paradox spoke, and his voice was grand and imposing and authoritative!
"My daughters."
The words settled over THE Weavers like a blessing.
"Something has anchored itself onto my Absolute authority and Claim. It is slowly eating away at me, and I cannot stop it for now."
Noah felt the shock that rippled through THE Weavers at these words. Their master, admitting vulnerability.
"This is a critical part of me that is unaffected, which I am giving to you."
The black cube floated toward THE Weavers, and they received it with hands that trembled slightly despite their best efforts at composure.
"Take it and keep it safe. You will know when to open it in the future."
THE Primordial Paradox paused, his contradictory eyes growing distant.

"The enemy is a terrifying one. I have to approach them differently compared to all others. I wish I could go to THE Creature and get his help on this, as he was always more knowledgeable than I am. But I must contain this myself at this moment."
His gaze refocused on THE Weavers.
"You will take this part, and you will-"
The sound of steps echoed through the temple.
Someone else was entering.
THE Weavers turned, and Noah turned with them, seeing through their eyes as another entity appeared at the entrance of the obsidian temple.
The newcomer moved with confidence that spoke of deep familiarity with this place. Their aura burned at THE Fundamental Depth of Absolute Sovereignty, power that was immense but not yet Absolute.
And when Noah sensed them, when he truly perceived who had just arrived...
He knew instantly.
THE Living Paradox.
Before he became what he was now. Before he devoured his master. Before he took the Claim that had never been meant for him.

He was younger in this memory, his features less defined, his presence less overwhelming. But the core of who he would become was already visible in the way he carried himself, in the ambition that lurked behind eyes that had not yet learned to fully mask their hunger.
THE Primordial Paradox looked at THE Living Paradox with an expression that held no suspicion. Only trust. Only the fondness of a master for a disciple who had served faithfully across eons.
"Erwin."
THE Living Paradox of course had a name. A real name. Not a title, not a classification, but a name that spoke of origins far humbler than his current status.
"You have been with me since you were nothing but a peasant. I give you another part of me to keep safe and put away in the location that I have sent to your memories."

Another obsidian black cube floated toward THE Living Paradox, toward Erwin, who received it with solemnity that seemed genuine. His hands cradled the cube as if he would guard it with his life, his expression one of devoted loyalty that showed no hint of the betrayal that would eventually come.

THE Primordial Paradox looked at THE Weavers and THE Living Paradox with a gaze that held regret. Something he wished he could change but could not. Something he hoped would not come to pass but feared might.
"Do not worry."
His voice remained grand and authoritative, but beneath it, Noah could hear the strain of someone fighting a battle on multiple fronts.
"Your master will get past this. What I have given to you are just contingencies."
He straightened, his form seeming to grow even larger as he reasserted his dominance over the moment.
"After I figure out what exactly has been invading my Weavings without me even knowing, I will extinguish it. I will show it how it cannot overcome that which is Paradoxical."
His eyes swept over his disciples one final time.
"Now go. Fulfill my orders. Fulfill your duty."
BOOM!
The memory shattered.
Reality fractured like glass struck by a hammer, fragments of the past scattering into the void as Noah’s consciousness was violently expelled from the experience.
He found himself back in the hallway of the Absolute Existential Palace, his mind buzzing with knowledge and possibilities.
THE Primordial Paradox had been infected by something.
Something that anchored itself onto his authority without him knowing. Something that ate away at him slowly, that he couldn’t stop, that he had to approach differently than any other enemy.
It sounded pretty fucking similar to...THE Entity.
It had to be THE Entity, or something connected to it! An...older form of it?
The methodology was identical. The invisible invasion. The consumption from within. The replacement that occurred before the victim even realized they were under attack.
And THE Living Paradox...
Erwin!
He was the one to do this as he eventually ate THE Primordial Paradox!
But he wasn’t part of THE Entity at this moment as THE Entity wanted to consume him too, yes?
Also...
Where were those black cubes now?
THE Weavers had been given one. They were dead, their Palace now in Noah’s possession. Was it here somewhere? Was it still waiting to be opened at the right moment?
And the one given to Erwin...
Did THE Living Paradox still have it?
Or had he already used whatever power it contained?
Noah’s eyes blazed with blue-gold light as understanding and uncertainty warred within his foundations.
He had come seeking knowledge.
And knowledge, as always, had given him more questions than answers.
But now he knew something that perhaps no one else or very few in Observable Existence understood.
THE Entity...may not be entirely new!

chapters.title: Chapter 4834: What Is Known And Unknown I
paragraphs: Noah came across a curious finding as uniquely, there was some connection between the origin of THE Entity and THE Living Paradox.
Something that was always buzzing in the back of his mind was the question of how THE Living Paradox had managed to devour THE Primordial Paradox.
Whatever approach he used had to have something that connected to what Noah currently knew as THE Entity.
But uniquely, it didn’t seem like THE Living Paradox himself, or even his followers within THE Loom, were affected this whole time.
Because only THE Living Dimensional and THE Living Quantum were just recently infected in Jotunheim, with THE Living Temporal currently running for his life across time itself.

What he was thinking about as well were the items that had been given by THE Primordial Paradox to THE Weavers and THE Living Paradox. The item given to Erwin was likely already utilized or devoured by him in his ascension to Absolute. But the cube that THE Weavers had received...
If he could go through their memories and find exactly where that was, if THE Weavers hadn’t offered it to THE Living Paradox after their master’s fall...
This may also hold some answers.
THE Primordial Paradox had stated that he was giving them a part of himself.
His mind buzzed with possibilities.
|Hypothetical Analysis|
|Whatever weapon or unique Weaving of Existence that THE Living Paradox utilized against THE Primordial Paradox has grown and emerged as THE Entity after THE Fallout|
|This would explain the similar methodology of invisible infection and replacement|
|What is not known:|
|- Whether THE Entity and THE Living Paradox have any form of relationship|
|- Whether THE Living Paradox knows the extent of what THE Entity is doing|
|- Whether THE Living Paradox can control THE Entity or if it has evolved beyond his influence|
|There is not sufficient knowledge to come to a definitive conclusion|
|Recommendation: Affirming whether the cube THE Weavers received still exists and locating it would be ideal|
|Secondary Recommendation: Raids on The Shelters of THE Loom may need to commence to obtain even more information on Paradox and his methodologies|
Noah looked over the prompts for a moment before he looked out at the other doorways all around him.
Maybe the answers were in the memories of THE Weavers. Maybe they weren’t. But he would continue looking until he found what he needed or exhausted every possibility this Palace contained.

Tendrils of blue-gold light extended from him again, emerging from his existence like serpents made of concentrated fate. They moved around the hallway with purpose, sliding past golden doors, pressing against locks and chains, seeking another entrance that would provide him with pertinent information.
Some doors rejected the touch of Undifferentiated Fate entirely.
Others responded with faint glimmers that suggested useful but not critical contents.
The search continued!
As he was doing all of this, his body in THE Agora of Primordial Judgment was moving with a happy Lumivara and Glossikos as he sought to understand this vast and unpredictable domain better.

They had been moving silently through corridors that seemed to exist in states of permanent philosophical debate, the very walls inscribed with arguments and counterarguments that had played out across eons.
At this moment, they stood before the entrance ofTHE Mouseion of Fated Artifacts.
The Museum of Destiny.

It sat inside THE Villa Dei Boscoreale, past THE Thermae of Cyclic Refinement where Noah had undergone his brutal Katharsis. The entrance was marked by columns of white stone that seemed to shimmer with potential, as if the artifacts within were already reaching out to those who might claim them.
The dryad visage of Glossikos turned to him, her bark-like features settling into an expression that held weight beyond simple conversation.
"We didn’t get a chance before, so you can enter and see what fated artifact you will obtain from here."
Her voice was measured and professional.
"Afterwards, the last place in the Villa is THE Bibliotheca of Primordial Wisdom. The Library of Origins. It contains all the knowledge regarding THE Agora of Primordial Judgment and more."
Oh?
Noah’s eyes twinkled at those words.
He would have rather gotten started there with how much he craved knowledge right now. A library containing everything about THE Agora...
But everything came in due time.
Even this place that would have a potentially unique artifact wasn’t something to say no to. Who knew what fate had waiting for him behind those shimmering columns?
So he gave a light nod.
"Let’s go."

The figure of Glossikos looked at him with a stern gaze that stopped him before he could take a step forward. Her eyes, ancient and filled with the weight of linguistic mastery she had pursued across eons, fixed on him with intensity that demanded acknowledgment.
"We aren’t even going to talk about you collapsing THE Weavers?"
Her voice held an edge now.
"What THE Living Paradox will do in response? Or are you like the rest of THE Four who only do what you must and allow the rest of us to pick up the pieces?"
She said such words with the coldness of someone who had watched THE Four play their games while other existences suffered the consequences!
Noah met her gaze without flinching.
"What is there to say about it?"
His voice was calm, unbothered.
"If you have anything to ask, I am here to listen. Until then, let’s get me whatever artifact is in here and then to that library."
Glossikos stared at him for a long moment before....
She turned without another word.
And with that, they delved into the museum.
Around the same time that Noah delved into memories of THE Weavers and further into THE Agora of Primordial Judgment, prompts bloomed in his consciousness with unexpected urgency.
|Master, we have found something rather unexpected|
|As we finish the integration of Muspelheim, in the space where this Primordial Realm used to exist, a unique aura of a lifeform has been discovered|
|This lifeform is not a Muspeli Lifeform|
|It does not match any classification in our current database|
|The situation does not currently seem dangerous, but your input is required|
|I say "does not seem dangerous" with the caveat that I genuinely have no idea what we’re looking at|

It sat inside THE Villa Dei Boscoreale, past THE Thermae of Cyclic Refinement where Noah had undergone his brutal Katharsis.
The entrance was marked by columns of white stone that seemed to shimmer with potential, as if the artifacts within were already reaching out to those who might claim them.
The dryad visage of Glossikos turned to him, her bark-like features settling into an expression that held weight beyond simple conversation.
"We didn’t get a chance before, so you can enter and see what fated artifact you will obtain from here."
Her voice was measured and professional.
"Afterwards, the last place in the Villa is THE Bibliotheca of Primordial Wisdom.
The Library of Origins.
It contains all the knowledge regarding THE Agora of Primordial Judgment and more."
Oh?
Noah’s eyes twinkled at those words.
He would have rather gotten started there with how much he craved knowledge right now.
A library containing everything about THE Agora...
But everything came in due time.
Even this place that would have a potentially unique artifact wasn’t something to say no to.
Who knew what fate had waiting for him behind those shimmering columns?
So he gave a light nod.
"Let’s go."
The figure of Glossikos looked at him with a stern gaze that stopped him before he could take a step forward.
Her eyes, ancient and filled with the weight of linguistic mastery she had pursued across eons, fixed on him with intensity that demanded acknowledgment.
"We aren’t even going to talk about you collapsing THE Weavers?"
Her voice held an edge now.
"What THE Living Paradox will do in response?
Or are you like the rest of THE Four who only do what you must and allow the rest of us to pick up the pieces?"
She said such words with the coldness of someone who had watched THE Four play their games while other existences suffered the consequences!
Noah met her gaze without flinching.
"What is there to say about it?"
His voice was calm, unbothered.
"If you have anything to ask, I am here to listen.
Until then, let’s get me whatever artifact is in here and then to that library."
Glossikos stared at him for a long moment before....
She turned without another word.
And with that, they delved into the museum.
Around the same time that Noah delved into memories of THE Weavers and further into THE Agora of Primordial Judgment, prompts bloomed in his consciousness with unexpected urgency.
|Master, we have found something rather unexpected|
|As we finish the integration of Muspelheim, in the space where this Primordial Realm used to exist, a unique aura of a lifeform has been discovered|
|This lifeform is not a Muspeli Lifeform|
|It does not match any classification in our current database|
|The situation does not currently seem dangerous, but your input is required|
|I say "does not seem dangerous" with the caveat that I genuinely have no idea what we’re looking at|

chapters.title: Chapter 4835: What Is Known And Unknown II
paragraphs: Noah heard the voice of Ruination echoing in his mind with such words as he quickly focused, his Absolute Seals of Fortune and Potential buzzing as if they sensed a grand possibility.
He quickly took control of his body that Ruination had been piloting in Muspelheim.
The transition was seamless, his consciousness settling into flesh and bone and authority that had been moving through the remnants of a Primordial Realm.
And he saw what surrounded him.

His massive blue-gold pillar, the monolith that had been devouring everything, stood grandly and tyrannically alone in the void. Fiery crimson-gold light of the Primordial Realm continued to sink into it from afar like rivers delving into an endless drain. The authority of Muspelheim, the accumulated weight of eons, all of it flowing into THE Infiniverse through this point of consumption.
And all around the monolith was blank collapsed space where the Primordial Realm used to sit.
Empty.
Dark.
The absence of something that had existed for longer than most beings could comprehend.
And yet, at this moment, this region did not have the calmness it should have held.

Because of their actions, they had actually uncovered a form of life that literally seemed like it had been slumbering in the region of space beneath Muspelheim. Waiting in the void between realms as if the Primordial Realm itself had been a blanket covering something ancient beyond measure.
With him taking hold of his body, Noah moved toward this unique finding.
He felt a sense of apprehension that he couldn’t explain.
HUUM!
And as he approached, whatever that slumbering lifeform was began to rouse.
Heavy Depths of Immensity began to radiate all around, pressing against Noah’s existence with weight that made him pause and truly assess what he was perceiving.
He was astonished.
The Depth didn’t fit into Surface or Intermediate or Fundamental. And yet he also couldn’t say that it fit in the Absolute, as he had now met multiple Absolutes and they didn’t feel this way.
It wasn’t that the aura he currently felt was grander or heavier than someone like THE Primordial Chaos. It simply felt different. Ancient in ways that transcended the normal understanding of age!
But the heaviness and Immensity no doubt made him feel as if the lifeform was an equivalent of an Absolute.

In the region of space where a Primordial Realm used to sit, darkness and white light intertwined and clashed. Short bursts of authority made it feel like sparks of black and white were meeting all around, illuminating the surroundings in flashes that stretched out for many miles.
Reality itself seemed uncertain about how to process what was waking up.
And the slumbering thing that Noah had woken up due to his devouring of a Primordial Realm opened its eyes at this moment.
What Noah saw defied easy description.

The creature’s form was that of an ancient aquatic being, something that looked like it had swum through the primordial waters of Existence itself before concepts like water or swimming had meaning. Its body stretched for miles, yet the concept of size for it wasn’t really warranted. It could just as well be gigaparsecs large. Scale seemed to be a suggestion rather than a rule for this entity.

It shone with a hazy stellar crimson-pink light that made its entire body look ethereal and almost see-through. Not ghostly, but existing in a state between physical and conceptual that normal perception couldn’t properly categorize.

Crimson-pink wings spread above it, vast membranes of light that pulsed with inner luminescence. They weren’t wings for flying. They were likely extensions of its existence that served purposes Noah couldn’t begin to guess.

And across its entire form, shimmering pages floated and drifted. Countless pages filled with words of The First Tongue, sentences and paragraphs and entire treatises written in the linguistic foundation of reality itself. They moved around the creature like schools of fish, like leaves in an eternal wind, like thoughts given physical form.
Noah was astounded to look upon such a creature.
The calm and ancient eyes of this being opened and stared back at him, pupils that held depths beyond normal comprehension. And within them, Noah could feel and see...boundless Everythings.
Not power in the conventional sense.
Information.
Pure, crystallized information accumulated across time spans that made eons seem like moments.
As he was staring at it, a booming ancient feminine voice echoed out across the void between realms.
"You have disturbed my slumber."
The words weren’t accusatory, they were simply factual.
"But you are also the first to do so since The Earliest Folds."
A pause that seemed to stretch across centuries.
"For this, I shall grant you the chance to ask a single question."
Noah’s eyes opened wide at this moment as prompts bloomed with information that made his foundations pulse with recognition.
|Information obtained through connection with The First Tongue|
|You have been granted a question by THE Mnemonic Leviathan, Pebanista Yacuruna|
|THE Mnemonic Leviathan dwells in the spaces between Primordial Realms|
|Its body is composed entirely of accumulated information|
|Every secret whispered across eons, every truth discovered and forgotten, every piece of knowledge that ever existed flows through its endless form|
|It knows almost everything|
|And it has never done anything|
|The Mnemonic Leviathan drifts through Existence, bloated with understanding it cannot apply|
|It is a docile creature of Existence, unbothered by the endless Weavings playing out across it|
Noah looked at the massive entity that stared at him with ancient eyes.
One question.
A single question to a being that knew almost everything that had ever been known.

His mind raced through possibilities, weighing the value of each potential question against the others. What did he need most? What would give him the greatest advantage? What knowledge would transform him most completely?
The Mnemonic Leviathan waited with patience born of existing between realms since before The Infinite Unfurling.
It was an ancient thing few knew of, and it had all the time in Observable Existence.
It always had.

chapters.title: Chapter 4836: What Is Known And Unknown III
paragraphs: He had an unbelievable finding just from the action of devouring a Primordial Realm.
Something utterly surreal!

A creature that felt like it had the Immensity of an Absolute, and yet at the same time, it wasn’t. The classification didn’t fit. The parameters didn’t align. It existed in a space between definitions that Noah hadn’t even known was possible.
The Mnemonic Leviathan looked at him with ancient patience as it asked once more.
"What question do you have?"
The voice was filled with Immensity that pressed against reality itself.
Noah’s eyes flashed sharply as he replied.
"I am not yet ready to give my question."
His words came calm and imperious.
"I am interested in learning more about you before I give my question. I do not even know how to categorize you, and I have met many across Existence."
This was actually a new finding that made him rather excited. Something outside the scope of what he knew about THE Creature and THE Living Paradox and all others.
What was it?
Where did it come from?
How did it fit into the grand weavings of Observable Existence?
As he was thinking about all of this, THE Mnemonic Leviathan initially looked at him in silence.
And then she eventually spoke.
"Primordial Realms. Shores. Folds. Wheels. Renowned Existences."
Her voice boomed across the void between realms.
"All that which you may have been exposed to in Observable Existence does not mean that is all there is in Observable Existence."
BOOM!
The words landed with weight that made nearby space tremble.
"THE Creature is not everything. Chaos or Paradox are not everything. THE First Tongue is not everything across Observable Existence."
Her ancient eyes held something that might have been amusement at his limited perspective.
"Observable Existence is vast, mighty, and filled with wonders. Some cannot even be perceived by entities less than Absolute. And some... even Absolutes are not privy to."
She paused, letting that truth settle.
"That is Existence. Many stray when they believe they know everything and have seen everything."
Her form pulsed with crimson-pink light.
"Now. What do you wish to know?"
The words of THE Mnemonic Leviathan were ridiculously heavy as Noah listened.

This entity held more knowledge than many, but she didn’t seem to want to talk too much. She answered what was asked and nothing more. No elaboration. No tangents. No freely given wisdom that might help him understand the broader context.
And he loved to meet old things that loved to talk.
They freely gave the most information without even realizing it. A rambling ancient being could reveal secrets in casual asides that would take years to discover otherwise.
But this one was different.
She wanted her question and nothing more.
If she really wanted a question to keep talking...
Noah’s eyes flashed with tyranny as he nodded, as if he’d arrived at his answer.
"What do I need to do in order to stand above everyone in power in Observable Existence in the shortest amount of time?"
BOOM!
He didn’t ask about THE Entity.
Instead, he asked a question that would be pertinent to him for the foreseeable future.
A question whose answer could guide his path for eons to come.
And...
THE Mnemonic Leviathan frowned.
She silently looked at him with those ancient eyes, her massive form going still in ways that suggested genuine surprise.
As if she was asking... dude, what the fuck kind of question was that?
The pages floating around her body slowed their eternal dance.
The crimson-pink light dimmed slightly.
After a while, the ancient voice replied.
"Ask another question."
Noah frowned.
"Don’t you know almost everything?"
His voice held challenge now.
"You do not have an answer to this question?"
THE Mnemonic Leviathan looked at him with something that might have been exasperation filtered through eons of patience.
"I know almost everything."
Her voice was flat.
"And the question you asked cannot be feasibly answered."
She paused.
"Okay. Those are two questions answered. That concludes and even exceeds your granted question, O Claimer of THE First Tongue."

Noah’s eyes flashed sharply as the radiant light around this creature began to intensify. Her form started to shimmer, the pages swirling faster, the crimson-pink wings spreading wider as if she was about to descend back into whatever space between realms she called home!
She was leaving!
Yet she stopped moments later, her ancient eyes finding his once more.
"I do not like to be bothered."
The words held weight that portrayed eons spent in peaceful slumber, undisturbed by the petty conflicts of Absolutes and THE Four and all the other beings who thought their struggles mattered.
"So. Just ask another question."
Noah’s eyes became stern.
If she didn’t want to answer his heavy question about ultimate power, he’d ask something more immediate.
"What is everything I need to know to overcome THE Entity that has already overtaken Jotunheim and THE Secretive Eon?"
BOOM!
Since this entity didn’t want to answer his first question, he asked another.
One that addressed the most pressing danger he currently faced.
And this time...
The eyes of THE Mnemonic Leviathan flashed.

The pages around her body moved faster, words of The First Tongue rearranging themselves as if searching through accumulated knowledge that spanned all of Observable Existence. Information older than THE Fallout. Truths that had been forgotten by every living being except this one creature who remembered everything.
She was contemplating his question.
And then she replied.
"The solution to your victory in the present is tied to events in the past."
Her voice was cryptic and measured.
"The way and answer you seek lies in the Weavings of what happened all those years ago with THE Primordial Paradox."
"Understanding the origin shall grant understanding of how to end it. These are the coordinates in time where you can find your solution."
This... this fucking fraud wasn’t giving him straight answers at all!
Events in the past? Understanding the origin? Coordinates in time?
She was basically telling him to figure it out himself while providing the vaguest possible guidance!
But a blinding crimson light did flow from her massive form, streaming toward his body like a river of concentrated information.
Actual coordinates in time. Not a place in space, but a when.
A specific moment in the past where the answers he sought could be found.
|Information Received|
|Temporal coordinates have been embedded into your existence|
|These coordinates point to a specific moment during or before The Infinite Unfurling|
|Reaching these coordinates would require Temporal Traversal of significant magnitude|

chapters.title: Chapter 4837: What Is Known And Unknown IV
paragraphs: He received coordinates burning in his foundations, temporal markers pointing toward a moment in the past that could unravel everything he needed to know about THE Entity.
But as he thought about this unique lifeform and what they represented, he didn’t want to let them go so easily.
A being that knew almost everything.
A creature that had slumbered beneath Primordial Realms since who knew when!
Something that existed at a level equivalent to Absolute while not fitting any normal classification.
And she was about to leave, to descend back into whatever space between realms she called home, to continue her eternal existence of knowing and watching and doingnothingat all.
Noah looked at THE Mnemonic Leviathan as she began to fade, her form becoming more ethereal, more see-through, the crimson-pink light dimming as reality prepared to forget she had ever been here.
"Wait."
His voice cut through the void.
THE Mnemonic Leviathan paused, those ancient eyes finding his with something that might have been mild irritation at being delayed.
"What I know of you is that you do not like to be bothered, and you slumber in the spaces beneath Primordial Realms."
Noah’s voice came calm and measured.
"I have a very nice Primordial Realm. Much like Muspelheim here."
He gestured toward the monolith that continued to devour the remnants of the realm she had slumbered beneath.
"Hasn’t it been comfortable, you slumbering here all these years? Come slumber and relax some more in my Primordial Realm."
"Unlike any Primordial Realms out there, mine isn’t filled with chaos and upheavals. You won’t be disturbed. It would fit with your nature."
The fading light from THE Mnemonic Leviathan stabilized.
She looked at Noah with those ancient eyes, her massive form hovering in the void as if she was genuinely considering something for the first time in eons.
The pages of The First Tongue that drifted around her slowed their eternal dance.
"The home of THE Genesis Monarch is not known much by others across Existence."
Her voice was contemplative rather than dismissive.

"The only time it was revealed was after the collapse of Transcendent Folds to Living Existences right before THE Fallout. It is the least known out of all Primordial Realms, if it even qualifies as a Primordial Realm."
She paused, her ethereal form pulsing with crimson-pink light.
"But I am an imperturbable existence and disdain actions by nature. You will likely disturb me. I have knowledge, but I do not act on it."
Her ancient eyes held something that looked almost like regret.
"That is my nature."
Her voice was heavy as she said this, the weight of eons of deliberate inaction pressing against every word.
Noah nodded, understanding what she was saying but not willing to accept it as the final answer.
"Anytime now, THE Entity might spread themselves from Jotunheim to other Primordial Realms."
His voice remained calm, reasonable.
"Or THE Living Paradox will send more of his forces to Alfheimr or other Primordial Realms. The conflicts that are brewing will touch every corner of Observable Existence eventually."
He tilted his head slightly.
"Whatever you choose, will it really be better than my Primordial Realm that nobody knows about?"
A pause.
"Do you even know where my Primordial Realm is?"
The question hung in the void between them.
THE Mnemonic Leviathan, who knew almost everything, who held every secret whispered across eons, who contained every truth discovered and forgotten...
Was silent.
For a long moment, she simply looked at him with those ancient eyes, and Noah could see the calculations happening behind them.
"Okay."
The word came simple and final.
"But you...must not bother me."
Noah smiled devilishly internally and nodded calmly with innocence!
"Of course. The most I may do is ask a question every now and then. I would never ask you to act out of your nature."
He gestured toward the void around them.
"Come. The journey will take a bit long since I now have another entity to move from here and take across The Wastes."
The moment he said this, THE Mnemonic Leviathan shook her massive head, the pages around her form rustling with what might have been amusement.
"There are faster ways."
WAA!
Noah’s eyes sharpened at those words.
Faster ways?

Through The Wastes of THE Fallout, where corrupted existence made travel treacherous and slow and teleportation impossible? Where even his immense foundations had to carefully navigate the twisted remnants of what Observable Existence had been?
"There are pathways."
THE Mnemonic Leviathan’s voice took on a weight.
"In the spark between Observable and Unobservable Existence, inside those spaces between spaces where reality hesitates before deciding what can be perceived, there are passages."
Her crimson-pink light pulsed brighter.
"The Interstices."
The word landed with significance that made Noah’s foundations pulse.

"They connect all points of Existence while existing in none of them. When Observable Existence was first differentiated, not everything was cleanly sorted. Some spaces fell into neither category. These spaces connected to each other naturally, forming a lattice of pathways that exist in a state of perpetual uncertainty. Neither fully real nor fully unreal."
Her massive form shifted, ancient eyes holding his with intensity that demanded attention.

"Even most Absolutes do not know of them. THE Creature likely knows and moves through them. THE Primordial Chaos has brushed against their edges. But true knowledge of The Interstices was removed from common understanding long before what you call Observable Existence differentiated."
She paused, letting that sink in.

"The Interstices are moments of existential hesitation. Places where reality paused before deciding what something would become. These pauses connected across Observable Existence like synapses in a vast neural network, forming routes that bypass normal spatial relationships entirely."

Her voice grew heavier still as Noah’s existence buzzed with a mixture of excitement. This was it- an old thing who was talking on and on! He had poked and probed until THE Mnemonic Leviathan was now freely breaking off into long asides!
"Travel through The Interstices doesn’t move you through space. It moves you through definition. You step out of being defined in one location and step back into being defined in another."
Noah’s mind raced as he processed what she was describing.
Pathways that existed in the gap between what could be observed and what could not. Routes that bypassed corrupted space entirely. A network that even most Absolutes didn’t know existed.
"Through The Interstices, The Wastes mean nothing."
THE Mnemonic Leviathan continued with the patience of a being who had all the time in Existence.
"Corrupted Existence means nothing. Distance and time bend to intent."
Her ancient eyes held something that might have been significance.
"Even the coordinates I have given you can be reached easier through there."
Noah’s eyes blazed with interest.
The pages of The First Tongue swirled around her form with increasing speed, as if responding to the weight of knowledge being shared.
"To even perceive The Interstices, one must be able to comprehend the boundary between Observable and Unobservable."
Her voice held warning now.

"The Interstices are not safe. They are filled with things that have accumulated in the spaces between definition. Corrupted Growths drawn to the edges of perception. Slumbering Undisturbed Existences like myself who prefer the quiet of undefined space. Attentions that should not be drawn."
She began to rise slightly, her ethereal form pulling toward a point in space that seemed to fold inward on itself.
"But they are faster than anything else in Existence."
"One way to open them, relating to masters of The First Tongue, would be to first know of them. Be capable of perceiving them."
Her ancient eyes locked onto his.
"And then speaking a word that has no definition. A Phoneme that describes something that doesn’t exist yet. This forces reality to acknowledge the undefined, creating passage."
She settled back, her form becoming more solid again.
"I know all of this. But I don’t act."
The faintest hint of something that might have been self-deprecation touched her voice.
"So you do it. And we can get there in an instant."
BOOM!
Noah looked at this creature with marvel.
She had all the knowledge one could ask for. Every secret. Every truth. Every methodology for accomplishing anything that could be accomplished in Observable Existence.
And she was a lazy bum who didn’t want to do anything.

This was her nature! But she did say something interesting. The Interstices! Something that should make his Temporal Traversal possible again! And one of the ways to reach them after knowing of them...
A word that described something that didn’t exist yet.
A word with no definition.
He was THE master of The First Tongue. He held 27 Seals of Absolute Tongue. He had claimed linguistic authority over reality itself.

His foundations stirred as he reached into his understanding of The First Tongue. The 27 Core Phonemes that formed the building blocks of linguistic reality. The Logos he had mastered. The Philologies and Archai.
All of them described things that existed.
Things that were defined.
Things that reality had already decided upon.
But The Interstices were places where reality hadn’t decided yet.
So he needed to speak something that reality hadn’t decided yet either.
Noah closed his eyes.
He reached past the Phonemes, past the established Logos, past everything that had been codified and understood across eons of linguistic mastery.
He reached for the space between words.
The pause before meaning.
The hesitation before definition.
And he opened his mouth and spoke something that had never been spoken before. Basically...gibberish!
A sound that wasn’t quite a sound.
A word that wasn’t quite a word.
HUUM!
Reality shuddered and space folded.
And in front of Noah, Existence opened up to reveal wonder. It couldn’t even be called or a tear or portal.
It was simply a place where space forgot to be solid.
A moment of existential hesitation made manifest.
An entrance to The Interstices!
THE Mnemonic Leviathan looked at the passage with ancient eyes that held something almost like approval.
"Good."
The single word was the highest praise she seemed capable of giving!

chapters.title: Chapter 4838: The Interstices I
paragraphs: It was a marvelous thing to see.

Once again, knowledge was extremely critical. He had to know about The Interstices first, had to understand that they existed before he could perceive them. And then he needed to know how to open up a doorway into these pathways that extended out across Existence.
Spaces of pathways that existed in a state of perpetual uncertainty.
Pathways between what was Observable and Unobservable.

The shimmering doorway hung before him, a fold in reality that didn’t look like a portal or a tear or any conventional form of spatial manipulation. It simply looked like a place where space had forgotten to be solid. A hesitation made manifest.
As he looked at it, Noah couldn’t help but ask.
"What are the methods to enter The Interstices? This space between definitions?"

The question was practical. If he was going to use these pathways, he needed to understand all the ways they could be accessed. The Phoneme method THE Mnemonic Leviathan had described worked, but were there others?
WAA!
The massive form of THE Mnemonic Leviathan shifted.

Her miles-long body compressed in an instant, stellar crimson-pink light folding inward as she reduced herself to barely two meters. The pages of The First Tongue that had swirled around her vast form now orbited a figure that could float comfortably at Noah’s side.
She came to hover at his right, her ethereal body still see-through, still shimmering with that hazy stellar glow.
Her ancient eyes found his with the patience of something that had seen everything and found most of it uninteresting.
"Each entity once powerful enough can utilize their own methods. There isn’t anything universal."
Her voice remained grand despite her reduced size, ancient authority compressed into a smaller vessel.
"Someone much more powerful than you can utilize the method of The Moment Between Breaths to create an entry point into The Interstices."
She paused, and Noah could have sworn he saw something like amusement in those ageless eyes.

"In the instant after exhaling and before inhaling, when the body holds neither old air nor new, neither old authority nor new authority, a being of sufficient awareness can slip sideways into undefined space."
"That easy. You just aren’t there yet."
Noah smiled as he looked at Pebanista Yacuruna.
At THE Mnemonic Leviathan.

She was giving him a sidelong glance as she said this, and he recognized the expression. It was the look of someone who had just told you that walking through walls was simple if you were strong enough, and you very clearly were not strong enough.
He filed the information away.
The Moment Between Breaths. A method for beings more powerful than him. Something to work toward.
But right now, he was too curious about The Interstices themselves to dwell on what he couldn’t yet do. The doorway shimmered before him, reality’s hesitation waiting to be stepped through.
He took a step forward and entered.
And...
|Entry Confirmed|
|You have entered the space between spaces|
|The space between definitions|
|You are arriving in the Primary Veins|
|More information is being obtained by The First Tongue as your consciousness extends into this place|
|This is not a place that forgives inattention|
Noah’s eyes flashed sharply as he looked around him to see something that defied easy description.
He was standing on top of a massive gray pillar.

The pillar extended downward into darkness so complete that it seemed less like absence of light and more like presence of nothing. There was no bottom that he could perceive, no foundation that these structures rested upon. They simply existed, rising from an abyss that felt hungry.

Other pillars rose around him, forming a corridor of sorts. A pathway that extended into the distance, each pillar spaced just far enough apart that one could leap between them if one was foolish enough to risk the darkness below.
The floor beneath his feet was Primordial Gray.

Not gray as in the color between black and white. Gray as in the color that existed before colors were differentiated. The shade that reality wore before it decided what things would look like. It felt stable beneath him, but that stability was a choice rather than a certainty.
And the ceiling...
The ceiling didn’t exist in a fixed position.

Noah looked up and saw darkness that simply continued until his perception decided "up" stopped having meaning. There was no roof. No boundary. Just the point where his mind refused to process any further and declared that direction closed for consideration.
The entire area felt like a corridor built from concepts that had never finished forming.
|Primary Veins Analysis|
|You have arrived in the main arterial pathways of The Interstices|
|Wide corridors that connect major nodes of Observable Existence|
|Relatively stable, with consistent rules|
|Travel through them compresses distance by a factor of approximately 10,000|
|A journey of billions of gigaparsecs becomes a walk of seconds|
|This is as efficient as travel gets|
And he didn’t even have to close his eyes.
He didn’t have to look with The First Tongue or reach out with Undifferentiated Fate to perceive what filled this place.
Every single surface.
Every nook and cranny.
Every inch of the Primordial Gray pillars and the darkness between them...man oh man, it was filled with Corrupted Growths!

They clung to the pillars like moss on ancient stones, layers upon layers of twisted existence that had accumulated across eons of neglect. They floated in the spaces between pathways, drifting through the undefined air like dust motes made of wrong. They clustered in the corners where pillars met darkness, feeding on the residual potential that flowed through these forgotten routes.
To the eyes of others, it might feel like absolutely nothing.
Invisible and undetectable!
But to Noah, with his Civilization that had begun automatically purifying Corrupted Growths through THE Infiniverse itself...
They were so dense that he couldn’t help but wave his hand!

A blue-gold glow extended from his palm, spreading outward like ripples in water, reaching toward the edges of his perception in this undefined space. The light touched everything. The pillars. The darkness. The accumulated corruption that had been gathering here since who knew how long.
HUUM!
The Corrupted Growths shriveled instantly and completely.

Where his authority touched them, they collapsed inward, their twisted forms unraveling as the corruption was stripped away and only purity remained. They turned into golden glows that flowed back into the surrounding existence, some of these glows streaming toward Noah himself, sinking into his foundations with warmth.
The space around him cleared.

Primordial Gray pillars that had been obscured by eons of corruption now stood clean and defined. The darkness between them seemed less hungry, less absolute. The pathway ahead looked almost welcoming compared to what it had been moments before.
|Purification Complete|
|You have purified a space without definition|
|Your authority has spread to places that you do not even know far from here|
|Be careful as there are many unknowns in The Interstices|
|But the number of Corrupted Growths cleansed was collectively more than you have cleansed before|
|Few have walked in the place you are currently in|
|Fewer still have bothered to clean up after themselves|
|An Absolute Everything is forming within your existence|
BOOM!
