chapters.title: Chapter 4839: The Interstices II
paragraphs: Noah felt it!
A heavy and glorious weight coalescing inside of him. The Absolute Everything took shape within his foundations, pure Civilizational Authority compressed into a form!
This was from just stepping into The Interstices.
From one wave of his hand. From cleaning up a single stretch of pathway that no one had bothered to maintain!
If he continued traveling to other areas of this place...
If he explored the full extent of these forgotten routes...
How many Absolute Everythings could he accumulate?
How much pure authority was waiting to be claimed in spaces that even most Absolutes didn’t know existed?

Noah looked at this space between definitions that he was in, his mind racing with possibilities. He wanted to explore. Wanted to travel every pathway. Wanted to cleanse every Corrupted Growth and claim every scrap of authority that had been accumulating here across eons.

He looked toward THE Mnemonic Leviathan, who had appeared beside him on the Primordial Gray pillar. Her reduced form floated serenely, those ancient eyes taking in the cleansed pathway with something that might have been mild interest.
"What if I want to spend a bit more time in this place and not cross it within an instant?"
If The Interstices compressed distance so dramatically, if a billion gigaparsecs became seconds, then how did one slow down? How did one linger in a place that was designed to be passed through?
Pebanista Yacuruna turned her ethereal gaze toward him.
"You can do so in your own time."
Her voice held the patience of ages.
"The Interstices are pathways where one moves by definition. We are defined here at this moment. You need a legible method through your Civilization to define us before your Primordial Realm."
She paused.
"And when we step out, we will be there."
The nature of this unique entity remained the same even now.
She knew and explained everything. Yet she did nothing.
Noah didn’t want to push her too much. She had already agreed to slumber beneath THE Infiniverse, had already shared knowledge of The Interstices that even most Absolutes didn’t possess.
So at this moment, he simply created a sentence.
A Philology.

He put together Phonemes of The First Tongue, linguistic building blocks arranged into meaning that he imposed around them both. The words weren’t spoken aloud. They were simply declared, authority made manifest through the foundational language of reality itself.
A declaration!
|We are outside of my Infiniverse.|
HUUM!
It didn’t look like anything had changed when he said this.
The Primordial Gray pillars remained. The darkness between them remained. The pathway stretched out in both directions as if nothing had occurred.
But Pebanista Yacuruna spoke out at this moment.
"Entering this place is nearly impossible for many. But leaving it, or at least this region, is fairly easy. You simply make the intent or the definition that you are taking a step to leave."
Noah nodded.
He understood.

The Interstices moved by definition. You defined where you were, and then you stepped out of being defined in one location and into being defined in another. The pathways themselves were just the space between those definitions.
He had defined them as being outside THE Infiniverse.
Now he just had to take a step.
Noah moved forward.
One step towards another pillar, and...

The glimmering allure of The Primary Veins faded around him, the Primordial Gray pillars dissolving like mist before morning sun. The darkness receded. The space between definitions released its hold on his existence.
And shockingly, he saw the flickering corrupted Wastes around him.

The twisted remnants of THE Fallout stretched out in all directions, corrupted existence folding back on itself in patterns that would drive lesser minds to madness. But directly before him, separated from the chaos by a barrier of concentrated authority...
The blue-gold barrier of a miniaturized Infiniverse.
His home.
One step to enter the space without definition.
A single intent to define themselves in another location.
And then one additional step.
He had crossed unfathomable depths in that short period of time, bringing back a heavy and ethereal entity to his abode.
THE Mnemonic Leviathan floated beside him, her reduced form taking in THE Infiniverse with ancient eyes that had seen more wonders than most beings could imagine.
"This will do."
Three words.
The highest praise she seemed capable of giving!
And with that, she began to drift toward the barrier, toward the Primordial Realm that would become her new slumbering ground!
The entry into THE Infiniverse for Pebanista Yacuruna was a simple one really.

THE Infinite Loom and its ever-changing barrier simply opened as Noah and she floated in. The concentrated authority that kept his home protected from the chaos of THE Fallout recognized his presence and parted without resistance, allowing the ancient entity passage into a realm that few had ever seen.
This was the first external entity he was bringing into his home.
And he did so without fear after measuring all possibilities.

The region he brought her to had surroundings shining crimson-gold, an earthen floor of Muspelheim forming down below to give off a sense of familiarity for her. The integration of the Primordial Realm was nearly complete now, and he could shape its essence however he wished within THE Infiniverse.

All around them, rivers of Dreams flowed in lazy spirals. Streams of Prana pulsed with life-giving energy. Currents of Avalon and Helios and many other components of THE Infiniverse floated through the air while holding Logos and Philologies that defined them.
And as she entered, Pebanista Yacuruna spoke.
"It is a pure and quiet place."
Her ancient voice held something that might have been approval.
"I will slumber and move around here so long as I am not bothered. I..."
She paused.
"Oh?"
The dolphin-like creature blinked, her ethereal form going still as she looked in front of Noah.

The visage of a humanoid manifestation was forming from the very essence of THE Infiniverse itself. A woman of blue-gold light, her features regal and stern, her presence radiating the weight of an entire Primordial Realm given consciousness.
Beside her, the figure of another blue-gold illusory manifestation formed.
RUINATION.
The two of them stared at Pebanista Yacuruna with eyes that held calculation and curiosity in equal measure.
THE Mnemonic Leviathan looked at them as if adding new information into her database, those ancient eyes flickering with recognition of something she had not expected.
"There are many oddities in Existence."
Her voice was contemplative.
"The Early Veiled Shore of THE Creature is simply that. It does not have a consciousness that can apply itself like so."
She paused, studying the manifestations before her.
"For you to have managed to do this with your Primordial Realm is... different."
Out of everything THE Infiniverse could have been called,odditywas a unique one.

chapters.title: Chapter 4840: The Hollow Echo! I
paragraphs: Noah’s eyes flashed as he gave her a look.

The grand and imposing visage of THE Infiniverse floated toward Pebanista Yacuruna, her blue-gold form radiating authority that spoke of vast domains and countless resources accumulated across Noah’s journey.
"This place is vast."
Her voice held welcome that was also assessment.
"Let us choose a location that fits you the most."

Noah had already communicated with THE Infiniverse for them to extract as much information as they could from this ancient entity. Every secret she held. Every truth she had accumulated. Every piece of knowledge that might prove useful in the conflicts to come.
While he...
He was about to make his return to The Interstices.
There was much he wanted to do.
So he looked toward RUINATION and THE Infiniverse.
"Get her settled. I may have a trip... across time."
Pebanista Yacuruna floated ahead before she turned around and glanced at Noah one last time.
"Pathways without definitions will have many things."
Her ancient voice held warning now.

"But even Absolutes are the least of your worries. There are Undefined Lifeforms from before THE Infinite Unfurling. There are The Watchers, Hollow Echoes. And you run the risk of Definition Collapse."
She paused, letting those words settle.

"Spending too long in The Interstices causes the traveler’s own definition to weaken. The space between Observable and Unobservable doesn’t want defined things in it. It constantly pressures travelers to become undefined."
Her ancient eyes held his.
"It is not a place to explore and play around in. Go to the point in time that has your answers, and treat The Interstices as just that... passages to get you places you otherwise could not go to."
Noah’s eyes shone brightly.
Was this ancient creature actually going out of her way to look out for him? Or simply trying to make sure her new landlord didn’t die too quickly?
Whichever it was, he nodded with a smile.

In the next moment, Pebanista Yacuruna began enlarging in size again. Her ethereal form expanded, becoming thousands of miles long as afatancient aquatic beast materialized fully within THE Infiniverse. The pages of The First Tongue swirled around her vast body, crimson-pink light painting the surrounding existence in stellar hues.
She began floating forward as THE Infiniverse and RUINATION moved alongside her.
The latter sent a prompt to Noah.
|Don’t worry, Master|
|We will wring this dolphin dry of all the knowledge it has|
|The more she becomes exposed to your First Tongue here, the more information I can extract|
|I know the assignment|
RUINATION knew what needed to be done.
Noah nodded with a smile as he alone remained in this region of THE Infiniverse with its forming landscapes of Muspelheim.
He breathed out and got ready.
The process was familiar now.
Noah reached past the known Phonemes, past the established Logos, past everything that had been codified and understood across eons of linguistic mastery. He reached for the space between words.
And he opened his mouth and spoke utter gibberish.
Reality shuddered. Space folded. And in front of him, another entrance to The Interstices opened, that familiar moment where space simply forgot to be solid.
He stepped through.
When he entered this time, the prompts that bloomed were different.
|Entry Confirmed|
|You did not arrive in the Primary Veins of The Interstices this time|
|You have entered the Capillary Threads|
|Narrow passages that branch off Primary Veins|
|Lead to more specific locations|
|Less stable, with rules that fluctuate|
|Distance compression varies wildly here, sometimes greater, sometimes lesser|
|It is very easy to get lost in|
The Capillary Thread he found himself in looked nothing like the Primary Veins.

Where those had been vast corridors of Primordial Gray pillars rising from endless darkness, this was narrow. Confined. The pathway beneath his feet was barely wide enough for two beings to walk abreast, and even that width seemed to fluctuate as if the passage itself couldn’t decide how large it wanted to be.
Murky mist covered the distant areas behind and in front of him. The mist swirled and shifted, making it impossible to perceive anything beyond a few dozen meters in either direction.
Darkness pressed in from the sides, hungry and patient.
He could be walking toward salvation or oblivion, and he wouldn’t know until he arrived.
And when Noah looked around, he sensed the overflowing Corrupted Growths.
They were everywhere.

Denser than in the Primary Veins. More concentrated. As if the narrowness of these passages had compressed the corruption that accumulated here, packing eons of twisted existence into spaces that could barely contain it.
Even though it carried a level of danger, Noah still waved his hand.
He sent his Immensity out, exerting himself to cleanse everything within his perception.
HUUM!

Invisible silent golden waves flowed through the surrounding existence. The Corrupted Growths shriveled and collapsed, their twisted forms unraveling as purity replaced corruption. Golden light streamed back toward him, sinking into his foundations.
|Purification Complete|
|Another Absolute Everything is forming within your existence|
|At this rate, you could establish a factory here|
BOOM!
The weight of another Absolute Everything coalesced inside of him!
Two now.
From just walking through The Interstices.
But while it formed, Noah felt his existence buzzing.
A foreboding sensation flared.
His gaze changed as 27 Seals of Absolute Tongue instantly bloomed behind him, manifesting in a corona of blue-gold authority that surrounded his form with concentrated power.
BOOM!
Something heavy smashed onto his back.
His entire existence vibrated with impact that should have sent him flying across The Interstices. But because he was an Absolute Immovable Object, he stayed still.
His Seals, however...
He was stern to realize they bent.
Creaked.
Strained under weight that they should not have had to bear.
And behind him was...
Noah was astonished to see an illusory gray hollow-like humanoid figure of an entity surrounded by gray flames.

Gray billowing flames spilled out of the nose and mouth of this humanoid entity, corrupted fire that felt wrong in ways that transcended normal wrongness. The figure was massive, towering above Noah with presence that pressed against reality itself.
And Noah recognized it.
It looked exactly like the form of THE Creature he had seen in Ginnungagap. That same humanoid shape. That same overwhelming presence. That same sense of Existence given form.
But where THE Creature had been surrounded by multicolored flames and the Immensity of all Existence...
This one felt vile.
Hollow.
Like corrupted existence wearing a face it had no right to wear!

chapters.title: Chapter 4841: The Hollow Echo! II
paragraphs: |You have caught the attention of The Hollow Echo of THE Creature|
|A segment of a lost definition of THE Creature when he passed through this region from an unknown time|
|It was drinking from the Corrupted Growths you purified|
|Its Immensity is unkno-|
BOOM!
The prompts couldn’t even finish.
Noah saw the Hollow Echo move fast, faster than anything that size should have been able to move. Its fist came down not toward him directly, but toward the space around him.
Because he was an Immovable Object.
So the Hollow Echo didn’t target him.
It punched the entire area around him instead.
And the surrounding environment of The Interstices...
That was not Immovable.
BOOM!
The entire region Noah was in shattered!

The Capillary Thread broke apart like glass struck by a hammer, fragments of undefined existence scattering in all directions. And even though Noah himself couldn’t be moved, the space he was standing on could be.
He was flung across The Interstices, riding a piece of shattered pathway through murky darkness as his Seals creaked and buzzed as if bearing a pressure they were never designed to withstand!
|The Immensity and weight of your Foundation is the only reason your existence has not shattered|
|You are bearing the weight of a Hollow Echo from an unknown time|
|This is not a fight you can win|
|This is barely a fight you can survive|
Noah’s eyes pulsed with Immensity.
He couldn’t let this continue. Couldn’t let himself be thrown around like debris in a storm while his Seals cracked under pressure that shouldn’t have been possible!
He moved his hand like a hammer.
A heavy Declaration emerged from it, words of The First Tongue blazing with authority that he forced into reality through sheer weight of existence.
|I! Am! Immovable!|
BOOM!
It began as a Declaration.
But uniquely, due to his Immensity and weight, due to the foundations he had built across a journey that defied normal progression, it became something more.
A Partial Embodiment.

Everything around him stabilized instantly. The shattered fragments of the Capillary Thread froze in place. The murky darkness stopped pressing inward. Even the corrupted existence that permeated this region became anchored, held in place by a definition that Noah had imposed through sheer force of authority.
Immovable.
Everything was Immovable.
But even before he could get his bearings...
WOOSH!
The Hollow Echo was already in front of him.

It had crossed the distance in less than a heartbeat, its corrupted form materializing from the stabilized darkness with speed that mocked his attempts at control. Its mouth opened, gray corrupted existence spilling out like vomit from a dying fold.
And a heavy ancient voice boomed out!
"DISCOMBOBULATE."
BOOM!
An Embodiment.
With a single word.
A single fucking word, and all of surrounding existence began to melt.

Noah’s definition of Immovable warped and twisted as a superior definition overwrote it. The fragments he had stabilized became unstable again, but worse now, they lost coherence entirely, turning to mush and paste as reality forgot what shape things were supposed to be.
The Hollow Echo brought its giant hand down like a hammer.
Everything in this region of The Interstices turned to formless nothing!
And Noah’s Seals began to crack!
At such a time...
Blue-gold flames wrapped around Noah’s figure.

His mouth and nose leaked lava-like blue-gold fire as something inside him ignited. He raised his head toward the Immensity of the Hollow Echo, toward the corrupted definition of THE Creature that was about to erase him from existence.
And he spoke.
"FUCK. YOU."
BOOM!
|An Absolute Everything has been utilized fully|
|From your existence, an Embodiment blooms at a heavy cost!|
The 27 Seals around Noah blazed with the light of an Embodiment.
The cracks healed. The strain eased. Power that he had accumulated through cleansing The Interstices poured into a definition that he imposed upon reality with everything he had.
He raised his hands and bellowed out, holding against the Immensity of the palm descending to collapse everything around him.
Two Embodiments clashed in The Interstices.
Two heavy definitions pressing against each other with weight that made space itself groan in protest.
DISCOMBOBULATE versus FUCK YOU.
Dissolution versus Defiance.
And...
BOOM!
A gray fracture erupted between them.

The space where two Embodiments met couldn’t contain the contradiction of their definitions. Reality cracked down the middle, a fissure of pure uncertainty splitting the Capillary Thread in ways that shouldn’t have been possible!
All around them, the definitions of existence became distorted.
And akin to a nuclear explosion, the existence between Noah and the Hollow Echo melted and detonated.
The blast flung them in different directions of definition, hurling them through The Interstices along vectors that had nothing to do with physical space and everything to do with meaning itself.
|Two Embodiments imposed different definitions and have caused an unnatural reaction in The Interstices|
|You have been thrown in different directions|
Different directions.
Noah breathed as he felt the strain on his existence, as he felt his Seals buzzing as if they were screaming that they couldn’t bear this weight.
It was a shocking thing.
He didn’t feel any fear.
He felt a sense of exhilaration.
His existence felt bright. Heavy. Unfathomably grand at being able to simply survive a few femtoseconds against a mere Hollow Echo of THE Creature that may have been the weakest version of him.
If a lost definition, a fragment of corrupted memory, could nearly collapse him...
What would the real THE Creature be like at full power?
The thought made him hungry!

And as he felt the countless other Corrupted Growths all around him, as he sensed the accumulated corruption of The Interstices pressing against his tumbling form, he smashed his fist out and cleansed.
HUUM!
Golden waves flowed outward even as he was thrown through undefined space.
Corrupted Growths shriveled and died, their essence purified into authority that flowed back into his foundations.
|Another Absolute Everything forming|
He wanted to continue.
Wanted to cleanse more. Accumulate more. Push further into The Interstices and see what other echoes and corruptions waited to be purified.
But his existence felt the heavy fucking strain.
His Seals were still buzzing with residual stress. His foundations, while intact, had been pushed to limits he hadn’t known existed. Another encounter with something like that Hollow Echo...
He might not survive.
Noah shook his head and pulled upon his Atlas.
His Foundation. His Immensity. His Grimoire of Infinite Lexicons. His Way.
He activated Temporal Traversal!
In the past, Towers had acted as lighthouses to illuminate the way. He didn’t even have Stanchions at this moment.
But he had 27 Seals.

His Seals illuminated the way forward, burning with blue-gold light that cut through the murky uncertainty of The Interstices. His figure began to be wrapped in the light of temporal passage, reality bending around him as he prepared to move not just through space, but through time itself.
He put a new definition out there.

The coordinates that Pebanista Yacuruna had given him were exerted, temporal markers pointing toward a specific moment in the past when THE Primordial Paradox first encountered the infection that would eventually consume him.
Temporal Traversal that may not have been possible due to THE Fallout unfolded.
Noah’s figure warped out of existence, disappearing from this region of The Interstices as he began to float toward a different region.
At a different time.
The moment he disappeared from that area, an instant later...
The Hollow Echo of THE Creature tore apart existence to arrive there.
Its corrupted form materialized from the shattered remains of the Capillary Thread, gray flames billowing from every orifice as it looked around with hollow eyes that held only hunger.
It searched.
It sought.
It did not find the puny existence that wasn’t collapsed by its Immensity.
The Hollow Echo stood in the empty space for a long moment, corrupted flames spilling into the void as it processed the absence of its prey.
Then, slowly, it began to drift back into the murky darkness of The Interstices.

And even though Noah himself couldn’t be moved, the space he was standing on could be.
He was flung across The Interstices, riding a piece of shattered pathway through murky darkness as his Seals creaked and buzzed as if bearing a pressure they were never designed to withstand!
|The Immensity and weight of your Foundation is the only reason your existence has not shattered|
|You are bearing the weight of a Hollow Echo from an unknown time|
|This is not a fight you can win|
|This is barely a fight you can survive|
Noah’s eyes pulsed with Immensity.
He couldn’t let this continue.
Couldn’t let himself be thrown around like debris in a storm while his Seals cracked under pressure that shouldn’t have been possible!
He moved his hand like a hammer.
A heavy Declaration emerged from it, words of The First Tongue blazing with authority that he forced into reality through sheer weight of existence.
Am!
Immovable!|
BOOM!
It began as a Declaration.
But uniquely, due to his Immensity and weight, due to the foundations he had built across a journey that defied normal progression, it became something more.
A Partial Embodiment.
Everything around him stabilized instantly.
The shattered fragments of the Capillary Thread froze in place.
The murky darkness stopped pressing inward.
Even the corrupted existence that permeated this region became anchored, held in place by a definition that Noah had imposed through sheer force of authority.
Immovable.
Everything was Immovable.
But even before he could get his bearings...
WOOSH!
The Hollow Echo was already in front of him.
It had crossed the distance in less than a heartbeat, its corrupted form materializing from the stabilized darkness with speed that mocked his attempts at control.
Its mouth opened, gray corrupted existence spilling out like vomit from a dying fold.
And a heavy ancient voice boomed out!
"DISCOMBOBULATE."
BOOM!
An Embodiment.
With a single word.
A single fucking word, and all of surrounding existence began to melt.
Noah’s definition of Immovable warped and twisted as a superior definition overwrote it.
The fragments he had stabilized became unstable again, but worse now, they lost coherence entirely, turning to mush and paste as reality forgot what shape things were supposed to be.
The Hollow Echo brought its giant hand down like a hammer.
Everything in this region of The Interstices turned to formless nothing!
And Noah’s Seals began to crack!
At such a time...
Blue-gold flames wrapped around Noah’s figure.
His mouth and nose leaked lava-like blue-gold fire as something inside him ignited.
He raised his head toward the Immensity of the Hollow Echo, toward the corrupted definition of THE Creature that was about to erase him from existence.
And he spoke.
"FUCK.
YOU."
BOOM!
|An Absolute Everything has been utilized fully|
|From your existence, an Embodiment blooms at a heavy cost!|
The 27 Seals around Noah blazed with the light of an Embodiment.
The cracks healed.
The strain eased.
Power that he had accumulated through cleansing The Interstices poured into a definition that he imposed upon reality with everything he had.
He raised his hands and bellowed out, holding against the Immensity of the palm descending to collapse everything around him.
Two Embodiments clashed in The Interstices.
Two heavy definitions pressing against each other with weight that made space itself groan in protest.
DISCOMBOBULATE versus FUCK YOU.
Dissolution versus Defiance.
And...
BOOM!
A gray fracture erupted between them.
The space where two Embodiments met couldn’t contain the contradiction of their definitions.
Reality cracked down the middle, a fissure of pure uncertainty splitting the Capillary Thread in ways that shouldn’t have been possible!
All around them, the definitions of existence became distorted.
And akin to a nuclear explosion, the existence between Noah and the Hollow Echo melted and detonated.
The blast flung them in different directions of definition, hurling them through The Interstices along vectors that had nothing to do with physical space and everything to do with meaning itself.
|Two Embodiments imposed different definitions and have caused an unnatural reaction in The Interstices|
|You have been thrown in different directions|
Different directions.
Noah breathed as he felt the strain on his existence, as he felt his Seals buzzing as if they were screaming that they couldn’t bear this weight.
It was a shocking thing.
He didn’t feel any fear.
He felt a sense of exhilaration.
His existence felt bright.
Heavy.
Unfathomably grand at being able to simply survive a few femtoseconds against a mere Hollow Echo of THE Creature that may have been the weakest version of him.
If a lost definition, a fragment of corrupted memory, could nearly collapse him...
What would the real THE Creature be like at full power?
The thought made him hungry!

And as he felt the countless other Corrupted Growths all around him, as he sensed the accumulated corruption of The Interstices pressing against his tumbling form, he smashed his fist out and cleansed.
HUUM!
Golden waves flowed outward even as he was thrown through undefined space.
Corrupted Growths shriveled and died, their essence purified into authority that flowed back into his foundations.
|Another Absolute Everything forming|
He wanted to continue.
Wanted to cleanse more.
Accumulate more.
Push further into The Interstices and see what other echoes and corruptions waited to be purified.
But his existence felt the heavy fucking strain.
His Seals were still buzzing with residual stress.
His foundations, while intact, had been pushed to limits he hadn’t known existed.
Another encounter with something like that Hollow Echo...
He might not survive.
Noah shook his head and pulled upon his Atlas.
His Foundation.
His Immensity.
His Grimoire of Infinite Lexicons.
His Way.
He activated Temporal Traversal!
In the past, Towers had acted as lighthouses to illuminate the way.
He didn’t even have Stanchions at this moment.
But he had 27 Seals.
His Seals illuminated the way forward, burning with blue-gold light that cut through the murky uncertainty of The Interstices.
His figure began to be wrapped in the light of temporal passage, reality bending around him as he prepared to move not just through space, but through time itself.
He put a new definition out there.

The coordinates that Pebanista Yacuruna had given him were exerted, temporal markers pointing toward a specific moment in the past when THE Primordial Paradox first encountered the infection that would eventually consume him.
Temporal Traversal that may not have been possible due to THE Fallout unfolded.
Noah’s figure warped out of existence, disappearing from this region of The Interstices as he began to float toward a different region.
At a different time.
The moment he disappeared from that area, an instant later...
The Hollow Echo of THE Creature tore apart existence to arrive there.
Its corrupted form materialized from the shattered remains of the Capillary Thread, gray flames billowing from every orifice as it looked around with hollow eyes that held only hunger.
It searched.
It sought.
It did not find the puny existence that wasn’t collapsed by its Immensity.
The Hollow Echo stood in the empty space for a long moment, corrupted flames spilling into the void as it processed the absence of its prey.
Then, slowly, it began to drift back into the murky darkness of The Interstices.

chapters.title: Chapter 4842: Helheim!
paragraphs: He was being flung across Existence, but it was not even a traversal of space and time.
It seemed to be a traversal of definitions!

Where he was defined before to be in the era where THE Fallout had just occurred, at this moment, he was defining himself to be in a different era entirely. And he could only reach it by passing through spaces between spaces, between what was Observable and what was not.
This time around, he had specific coordinates.
Temporal markers burning in his foundations, guiding his passage through The Interstices toward a moment that had occurred eons before his birth.
|Temporal Traversal Analysis|
|The Weavings of your existence are passing through innumerable definitions across The Interstices|
|You have crossed past what is defined as THE Earliest Folds|
|You have crossed past what is determined to be THE Infinite Unfurling|
|Current trajectory: defining yourself toward the definition of a time extremely early within THE Infinite Unfurling, when things were in their early stages of differentiation|
|The coordinates Pebanista Yacuruna provided are aligning with remarkable precision|
|Take a step and you shall leave The Interstices to the new era|
|One note: I have no data on this time period. We’re operating blind|
Noah felt uniquely how the Weavings of Existence had changed even though he was still in The Interstices.

The murky darkness that had surrounded him in the Capillary Threads was gone. The Primordial Gray pillars of the Primary Veins were absent. Instead, when he looked around, he found himself funneling through a path of great brilliance.
Light that wasn’t light.
Meaning that wasn’t meaning.

Definition in its purest form, unfiltered by the corruption and complexity that eons of Existence had accumulated. It felt clean here. Ancient. As if he was passing through the moment before everything became complicated.
He steadied himself.
And took a single step.

The moment he did, he exerted a new definition. The spaces between spaces faded. What was Observable and Unobservable separated around him like curtains being drawn back. He anchored himself into a new era with authority that burned through his 27 Seals.
HUUM!
The moment he stepped out of The Interstices, what he felt was immense coldness as he was shooting down at high speeds!

He smashed like a meteor onto a riverbank filled with obsidian frost, his arrival carving a massive crater into a frozen landscape that seemed to reject the very concept of warmth. The cold was so penetrating that even with his Foundation, even with the weight and Immensity he had accumulated across his journey, he felt it seeping into his existence.
The cold of endings. The cold of finality. The cold of a realm that existed to receive those who had nowhere else to go.

Noah placed his hands on the lands around him, feeling obsidian ice that burned with temperatures that shouldn’t have been possible. His Seals circulated around his body, their blue-gold light pushing back against the encroaching frost. The First Tongue began to permeate all around him, linguistic authority reaching out to gather information from an era that predated everything he knew.
Information rapidly began forming in his mind.
He heaved as he felt the strain on his existence calming down.
He breathed out while feeling as if his muscles had just withstood tremendous weight.

His 27 Seals were all shining brilliantly as they healed from being bent by the weight of a mere Hollow Echo. The micro-fractures were sealing themselves, authority flowing through channels that had been stressed to their limits and were now recovering in this frozen landscape.
As his awareness spread, Noah rose from the crater and looked upon where he had arrived.

An expanse of obsidian sky stretched above him, filled with mist and coldness that seemed to have weight. There were no stars here. No sun. No source of light that he could identify. And yet he could see, as if the darkness itself had learned to illuminate in ways that defied normal perception.
He could hear the sounds of a heavy rushing river nearby.

The water, if it could be called water, moved with a terrifying force that made his foundations buzz just from proximity. This was not a river that could be swum. This was not a river that could be crossed by normal means!
The current alone felt like it could crush Fundamental Depth entities, grinding them down to nothing through sheer relentless pressure.
|Location Analysis Complete|
|You have arrived at a unique point in time in the distant past of THE Infinite Unfurling|
|Cross-referencing available data with First Tongue here|
|This location is deemed to be the Primordial Realm: Helheim|
|The Weavings of an ancient type of Paradox permeate all around|
|Specific coordinates place you at the riverbanks ofGjöll|
|Historical context: Gjöll is recorded as one of the boundary rivers of Helheim, separating the realm of endings from the rest of Existence|
Helheim.
Noah’s eyes twinkled as his existence buzzed with Immensity.
He began to rise up from that crater, obsidian frost falling from his form as he took in the full scope of where temporal traversal had deposited him.
The landscape stretched out in all directions with a beauty that was terrible to behold.

Massive glaciers of black ice rose in the distance, their surfaces carved with symbols. The ground beneath his feet was permafrost that had never known thaw, obsidian earth frozen solid since before differentiation had finished sorting Existence into its current categories.
Skeletal trees dotted the riverbank, their branches bare and reaching toward the lightless sky like the fingers of the dead grasping for something they could never reach.
They weren’t truly trees, Noah realized. They were concepts. Ideas of trees that had wandered here and become trapped, taking root in soil that accepted all things that had ended.

Mist rolled across the frozen plains in waves, each bank of fog carrying whispers that might have been voices or might have been the sound of Existence itself mourning what had been lost. The whispers spoke in languages he didn’t recognize, tongues that had been forgotten before THE Infinite Unfurling had given shape to what Observable Existence would become.
And the river Gjöll...

It roared beside him with fury that felt personal. The waters were not water but something else entirely. Liquid endings. Flowing finality. The current carried fragments of things that had once been, grinding them down to their base components before depositing them somewhere deeper in this realm of conclusion.

Bridges of bone spanned the river at distant intervals, their arches constructed from the remains of beings who had attempted to cross and failed. They served as warnings and pathways both, monuments to the price of passage through a realm that demanded payment in collapse.
It was an utterly surreal experience to be observing all of this.

A Primordial Realm from the early stages of THE Infinite Unfurling, preserved in a moment of time that Noah had no right to be witnessing. The cold. The darkness. The weight of endings pressing against his existence from every direction.
And yet his awareness quickly locked onto something that was here that should not be here.
An ancient-looking ship sat at the edges of the rough river Gjöll...calmly.

It was paradoxically appearing and disappearing, flickering in and out of definition as if it couldn’t decide whether it existed or not. One moment it was fully manifest, its hull carved from wood that had never grown on any tree. The next moment it was translucent, barely there, a ghost of a vessel that refused to fully commit to presence.

The ship was massive, easily large enough to carry armies across waters that would destroy anything less. Its sails were furled, fabric woven from shadows and silence. Its prow was carved into the shape of something that might have been a serpent or might have been a concept that had never been given a name.
And on its deck, a single aura could be felt.

The being stood at the helm of that impossible ship, his presence radiating authority that made the frozen landscape seem small by comparison. He was a regal and majestic humanoid obsidian entity, his form carved from the same material as the glaciers that rose in the distance.
A massive obsidian crown floated and spun above his head, rotating slowly with weight that spoke of dominion over things that most beings couldn’t comprehend. His robes shone obsidian-gold.
The aura he radiated was that of an Absolute.
But not just any Absolute.

This was the weight of someone who had stood among THE Four. Someone who had held a Claim on one of the oldest aspects of Existence itself. Someone whose authority had shaped what Paradox meant before THE Living Paradox had ever existed.
This was another being that Noah recognized.

The ancient entity smiled, his obsidian features shifting into an expression that held warmth despite the frozen realm around them. He opened his mouth, and when he spoke, his voice carried across the river Gjöll with authority that made the rushing waters seem quiet by comparison.
"I have been waiting across time for thee, my friend."
The words were archaic! Spoken in a cadence that belonged to an era before modern speech had been differentiated from the primordial expressions of meaning.
"Come aboard. We have far too much to accomplish, and the Weavings tell me that things have grown corrupted."
His obsidian eyes held knowledge that spanned eons.
"Thus, we possess little time to do what must be done."
BOOM!
Noah stared ahead with a sense of incredulity.
He was currently looking at what he remembered from the memory of THE Weavers to beTHE Primordial Paradox.
The original holder of that Claim.
The being who had been consumed by Erwin, by THE Living Paradox, in an act of betrayal that had reshaped the hierarchy of THE Four.
The entity who had given pieces of himself to his disciples before the end, hoping that contingencies might somehow save what could not be saved.
And he had been waiting across time for...him?

chapters.title: Chapter 4843: THE Primordial Paradox I
paragraphs: Many beings believed in fate and destiny.

Many beings cling to it with desperate fervor. They believe that the Weavings of Existence have already determined what will occur, that every moment has been preordained since before THE Infinite Unfurling gave shape to reality. They find comfort in this notion. If one’s destiny is set, then failure is not truly failure. Success is not truly earned. Everything simply is what it was always meant to be.
The significant majority hold this belief.
The significant majority are wrong.

Those who have witnessed eons say that even with immense Weavings of fate and destiny, nothing is ever truly fated or destined. They have watched beings defy prophecies that seemed absolute. They have seen futures that were "certain" unravel because someone chose differently than the Weavings predicted. They have observed the most intricate weavings of destiny torn apart by a single decision made in a single moment.
Because all that there is, in the end, ischoices.
Choices stir everything across Existence.

A being who believes in destiny surrenders their agency to comfortable inevitability. A being who understands choice recognizes that every moment is a crossroads, every breath a decision, every action a thread that rewrites what comes next.
Destiny is the story the powerful tell the powerless to keep them passive. Fate is the lie the fearful tell themselves to avoid responsibility for their own existence.
But choice is truth.
And those who wield choice with full understanding of its weight become the ones who write destiny for others.
Noah remained floating in the cold air of Helheim as he looked at the imposing Absolute entity on the ship.
Many thoughts were running across his mind. Questions about temporal mechanics. Concerns about paradoxes. Calculations regarding what his presence here might mean.
But he didn’t give them much space.
He simply voiced out what he was thinking.
"Are you sure that you have the right person?"
His voice carried across the frozen riverbank with authority that refused to be diminished by the presence of an Absolute.
"Do you even know who I am?"
Yes.
He did not know THE Primordial Paradox.

And THE Primordial Paradox, who existed within these Weavings, should not have known anything about him. This was the first time that Noah was arriving here. The first moment of contact between two beings separated by eons of history.
The past was the past.
What Noah already knew had occurred would not change. This was something he had discovered when he first returned from Ginnungagap, when temporal manipulation had shown him its fundamental rules.

So regardless of what happened here, THE Primordial Paradox would still be overcome by THE Living Paradox. His Claim would still be stolen. The betrayal that had reshaped THE Four would still occur exactly as it had always occurred.
Noah would not be able to change this.
This was the closed temporal loop.
Him traveling to the past did not change the past and would not change history because his actions were already, and had always been, part of that past. He simply did not know it yet.

When he awakened Mana more than three years ago, he didn’t know that his existence had already traversed eons backward before that point in time. And before he met THE Mnemonic Leviathan, he didn’t know that his temporal traversal would be taking him to THE Primordial Paradox.
This was the issue with time and its manipulation.
It was very messy.

THE Primordial Paradox smiled on the deck of his impossible ship, the expression carrying warmth that seemed at odds with the frozen realm around them. He shook his head slowly, his obsidian crown rotating with measured grace above his brow.
"No, I do not know who you are."
His voice was precise, each word enunciated with the careful diction of someone for whom language was a craft to be respected.
"Or rather, I did not know who you are until I met you just now."
He studied Noah with eyes that held the weight of eons.
"From observing you at this moment, I can perceive that the one who may paradoxically be capable of assisting me is, quite uniquely, someone I did not even know existed."
He paused, letting that sink in.
"Because at this point in time, The First Tongue has not been claimed. And yet, here you are. The Claimer of The First Tongue."
His smile deepened.
"From the authority that you do not trouble yourself to conceal, I can discern your distinction to be that of THE Genesis Monarch."
The obsidian entity folded his hands behind his back with the bearing of someone accustomed to commanding attention simply by existing.

"I must confess, I am rather surprised. I had anticipated that perhaps THE Creature might be the one capable of rendering assistance. Or even THE Primordial Chaos, though he and I have our disagreements."
His eyes held something that might have been amusement.
"I most certainly did not expect someone such as yourself."
As he said all of this, Noah looked at this being emanating waves of Absolute authority into the frozen skies of Helheim.
He should already be infected by THE Entity.

Even though it should not be the same Entity that Noah knew at this moment in time, whatever its origin was, the infection that THE Primordial Paradox had described to THE Weavers in that memory had already begun. Something had anchored itself onto his authority and Claim. Something was slowly eating away at him.
And yet he stood here with the dignity of someone who had accepted his fate while refusing to surrender to it.
Noah floated down from the frozen air.

His feet touched the deck of the ship, and the moment they did, he felt something extraordinary beneath him. The surface was solid. Fuckin sturdy! It didn’t just resist pressure. It rejected the very concept of being damaged.
|Ship Analysis Complete|
|Structural composition identified: The backbone of this vessel is forged from Helheim itself|
|Not materials from Helheim. Helheim itself. A fragment of the Primordial Realm compressed into nautical form with Absolute Depth|
|Classification: Indestructible Object|
|Defensive capability: Can withstand the full might of an Absolute without structural compromise|
|Vessel designation discovered through First Tongue: Naglfar|
|Historical context: Naglfar is recorded in ancient Weavings as the ship that sails between endings, carrying those who have business with finality itself|

They have seen futures that were "certain" unravel because someone chose differently than the Weavings predicted.
They have observed the most intricate weavings of destiny torn apart by a single decision made in a single moment.
Because all that there is, in the end, ischoices.
Choices stir everything across Existence.
A being who believes in destiny surrenders their agency to comfortable inevitability.
A being who understands choice recognizes that every moment is a crossroads, every breath a decision, every action a thread that rewrites what comes next.
Destiny is the story the powerful tell the powerless to keep them passive.
Fate is the lie the fearful tell themselves to avoid responsibility for their own existence.
But choice is truth.
And those who wield choice with full understanding of its weight become the ones who write destiny for others.
Noah remained floating in the cold air of Helheim as he looked at the imposing Absolute entity on the ship.
Many thoughts were running across his mind.
Questions about temporal mechanics.
Concerns about paradoxes.
Calculations regarding what his presence here might mean.
But he didn’t give them much space.
He simply voiced out what he was thinking.
"Are you sure that you have the right person?"
His voice carried across the frozen riverbank with authority that refused to be diminished by the presence of an Absolute.
"Do you even know who I am?"
Yes.
He did not know THE Primordial Paradox.
And THE Primordial Paradox, who existed within these Weavings, should not have known anything about him.
This was the first time that Noah was arriving here.
The first moment of contact between two beings separated by eons of history.
The past was the past.
What Noah already knew had occurred would not change.
This was something he had discovered when he first returned from Ginnungagap, when temporal manipulation had shown him its fundamental rules.
So regardless of what happened here, THE Primordial Paradox would still be overcome by THE Living Paradox.
His Claim would still be stolen.
The betrayal that had reshaped THE Four would still occur exactly as it had always occurred.
Noah would not be able to change this.
This was the closed temporal loop.
Him traveling to the past did not change the past and would not change history because his actions were already, and had always been, part of that past.
He simply did not know it yet.
When he awakened Mana more than three years ago, he didn’t know that his existence had already traversed eons backward before that point in time.
And before he met THE Mnemonic Leviathan, he didn’t know that his temporal traversal would be taking him to THE Primordial Paradox.
This was the issue with time and its manipulation.
It was very messy.
THE Primordial Paradox smiled on the deck of his impossible ship, the expression carrying warmth that seemed at odds with the frozen realm around them.
He shook his head slowly, his obsidian crown rotating with measured grace above his brow.
"No, I do not know who you are."
His voice was precise, each word enunciated with the careful diction of someone for whom language was a craft to be respected.
"Or rather, I did not know who you are until I met you just now."
He studied Noah with eyes that held the weight of eons.
"From observing you at this moment, I can perceive that the one who may paradoxically be capable of assisting me is, quite uniquely, someone I did not even know existed."
He paused, letting that sink in.
"Because at this point in time, The First Tongue has not been claimed.
And yet, here you are.
The Claimer of The First Tongue."
His smile deepened.
"From the authority that you do not trouble yourself to conceal, I can discern your distinction to be that of THE Genesis Monarch."
The obsidian entity folded his hands behind his back with the bearing of someone accustomed to commanding attention simply by existing.
"I must confess, I am rather surprised.
I had anticipated that perhaps THE Creature might be the one capable of rendering assistance.
Or even THE Primordial Chaos, though he and I have our disagreements."
His eyes held something that might have been amusement.
"I most certainly did not expect someone such as yourself."
As he said all of this, Noah looked at this being emanating waves of Absolute authority into the frozen skies of Helheim.
He should already be infected by THE Entity.

Even though it should not be the same Entity that Noah knew at this moment in time, whatever its origin was, the infection that THE Primordial Paradox had described to THE Weavers in that memory had already begun.
Something had anchored itself onto his authority and Claim.
Something was slowly eating away at him.
And yet he stood here with the dignity of someone who had accepted his fate while refusing to surrender to it.
Noah floated down from the frozen air.
His feet touched the deck of the ship, and the moment they did, he felt something extraordinary beneath him.
The surface was solid.
Fuckin sturdy!
It didn’t just resist pressure.
It rejected the very concept of being damaged.
|Ship Analysis Complete|
|Structural composition identified: The backbone of this vessel is forged from Helheim itself|
|Not materials from Helheim.
Helheim itself.
A fragment of the Primordial Realm compressed into nautical form with Absolute Depth|
|Classification: Indestructible Object|
|Defensive capability: Can withstand the full might of an Absolute without structural compromise|
|Vessel designation discovered through First Tongue: Naglfar|
|Historical context: Naglfar is recorded in ancient Weavings as the ship that sails between endings, carrying those who have business with finality itself|

chapters.title: Chapter 4844: THE Primordial Paradox II
paragraphs: Noah stood on such a thing as he looked at the glorious visage of THE Primordial Paradox.

The ancient Absolute still maintained a heavy sense of majesty despite everything. His eyes held no fear or worry. Not even a sense of urgency pressed against his bearing. He didn’t look like someone who knew that their Claim was under attack.
He looked like someone who had made peace with what was coming and was now focused entirely on what could still be done.
"I also did not expect you...as you are now anyways."
Noah’s voice came measured, direct.
"I came here seeking to understand a bit more about the thing currently attacking you. And to understand the one responsible for it."
He met those obsidian eyes without flinching.
"You do know who is responsible for this assault on you, right?"
At such words, THE Primordial Paradox sighed.

It was a sound that held the weight of betrayal processed and accepted. His profound gaze of immense dignity and power never wavered, but something behind it shifted. Something that spoke of trust that had been violated in ways that cut deeper than any physical wound.
"Of course."
His voice remained precise, controlled.
"My dearest disciple Erwin initiated all of this. But even he may not understand what he has truly done."
The name hung in the frozen air between them.
"And I have come to realise that it is unstoppable. I can only make preparations."
He turned slightly, gesturing toward the rushing waters of Gjöll that roared beside them.
"My Claim over Paradox informed me that there would be someone who might potentially assist me in these preparations if I sailed across my river. But truly, time is not on our side."
His obsidian features settled into something that might have been wry acceptance.
"Even though I was waiting here for my own aims and goals, you appear to have similar ones based upon the enemy attacking me."
He faced Noah fully.
"So. Can we get started?"
He said such words gloriously and imperiously, the bearing of an Absolute who had chosen to spend his final preparations with efficiency rather than lament.
Noah looked at this being and asked the question that mattered most.
"What exactly needs to be done?"
THE Primordial Paradox smiled at such words.
It was the smile of someone who had been waiting for that precise question.
"I have already commenced my preparations. I have isolated and hidden parts of myself in different areas throughout Helheim."
He paused, and something darker crossed his features.
"I have come to realise that even these parts of myself, stretched out across my realm, will be claimed in the end as well."
His hands clasped behind his back once more.

"In waiting here, I had thought I would come across THE Creature or THE Primordial Chaos and secure their aid in locking a part of myself away in Alfheimr or Jotunheim. Somewhere beyond immediate reach. It has to stay and persist in this time as it is a piece of Absolute. A Piece of the Claim of Paradox as it cannot be carried across time, otherwise I would hand it to you and say our goodbyes. So it needs a place to remain until it can be safe to unveil."
He looked at Noah with eyes that held the weight of paradox itself.
"And it appears that, quite paradoxically, it was neither of the two I expected."
His smile returned.
"It is instead the one with the Claim to The First Tongue."
He gestured with one obsidian hand toward the frozen expanse beyond the ship.
"So you tell me, Genesis Monarch."
"Where exactly are we heading? Ginnungagap? Muspelheim?"
BOOM!
The words landed with weight.
THE Primordial Paradox was asking him to choose.
To decide where a fragment of an Absolute, a piece of one of THE Four themselves, would be hidden away!
THE Primordial Paradox asking him such a question was ridiculous in itself.
Where to hide a piece of an Absolute across time? Where to place a fragment of one of THE Four that would remain concealed from THE Living Paradox and even THE Entity across eons of searching?
But Noah was nothing if not adaptable.

He thought about the answers he had come to find here. As the first existence to be infected by whatever THE Entity used to be, THE Primordial Paradox would be among the few that would know more than everyone else. His knowledge of the infection’s origin, its methodology...
But first, he had to answer this question.

So after he thought about it for a moment, on exactly where a part of THE Primordial Paradox could be hidden that others would not be able to gain access to, his mind couldn’t help but wander to an area that had a complex set of rules.
An area that held four Absolutes, or really, would in the future.
An area that THE Entity was not capable or willing to go into!

The place where THE Secretive Eon had refused to enter even when her Disciple was inside. The place that had somehow cleansed or blocked the infection from Noah’s followers. The place that held protections that even THE Entity respected.
If a fragment of THE Primordial Paradox was hidden there, within THE Vaults of Ginnungagap that connected to THE Agora...
His eyes shone with realization.
"Definitely Ginnungagap."
HUUM!
The moment he said these words, the vast ship below them trembled with resonance of of ancient engines stirring to life.
THE Primordial Paradox smiled.

He tapped his feet lightly against the deck of Naglfar, and the massive ship shot out like a sliver of obsidian light. The acceleration was beyond anything Noah had experienced, multiple times faster than Skoll at full sprint, crossing the heavy waves of the river Gjöll as if the crushing current was nothing more than a gentle stream.
The frozen banks of Helheim blurred past them.
The skeletal trees became smears of darkness against the obsidian sky.
And the roar of the river faded behind them as Naglfar carved its path toward whatever destination would eventually lead to Ginnungagap.

chapters.title: Chapter 4845: THE Primordial Paradox III
paragraphs: As this process began, THE Primordial Paradox waved his hands with casual authority.

Two obsidian thrones rose from the deck of the ship, positioned opposite each other at the center of the vessel. They grew from the Helheim-forged wood like natural extensions of the ship itself, their surfaces carved with symbols of ancient Paradox.
An extended crystalline obsidian table bloomed in front of them.

The table buzzed with an ancient type of Paradox that made Noah’s foundations resonate. Its surface became filled with obsidian-gold sacred herbs and crystals, treasures that radiated authority and weight that spoke of tremendous value.

THE Primordial Paradox motioned for Noah to sit on the opposing throne as he settled onto his own with the ease of someone who had done this countless times before. He waved his hands and began to eat from the wonders on the table, consuming items that would have been priceless treasures in Noah’s era as if they were casual refreshments.
Noah glanced down at the spread before him.

His eyes found the throne opposite THE Primordial Paradox, and he moved to take his seat. When he reached out to grab an obsidian-gold gem shaped like a cube, information immediately flooded his consciousness through The First Tongue.
|Item Analysis|
|Designation: Gjöll Pressure Crystal|
|A paradoxical crystal found at the bottom of the river Gjöll|
|Has been battered by the river’s crushing pressure for approximately one billion years|
|The sustained force has compressed trace amounts of Absolute authority into its structure|
|A single crystal contains slight Weavings of Absolute within it|
|Consumption recommendation: Immediate|
|These don’t exist in your era. The river Gjöll was altered during THE Infinite Unfurling’s later stages|
Noah’s eyes flashed brilliantly at this.
Without a second thought, he chucked the crystal toward his mouth and began to chew.

The sensation was extraordinary. Cold that burned. Pressure that expanded. Authority that seeped into his foundations like water into parched earth. The crystal dissolved against his teeth, its billion years of accumulated weight releasing into his existence with each bite.
|Foundation Enhancement Detected|
|The Immensity and weight of your Foundation at the comparative Fundamental Depth has increased by 0.1%|
It seemed that there were many wonders and opportunities here.

Noah focused on the items laid out on this brilliant table and began to consume them one after another. Obsidian fruits that tasted like concentrated endings. Golden herbs that burned with paradoxical warmth. Crystalline waters that flowed upward when swallowed.
Each one added to his foundations in ways that would have taken time to achieve.
THE Primordial Paradox watched him with a smile. He had in his hand an obsidian glass filled with vibrant golden liquid that he was drinking calmly.
"How are things later on in the future?"
His voice was casual, conversational.
"Does Erwin get into more trouble?"

He asked such a question as if he was inquiring about someone who did not fully concern him. As if the disciple who was currently eating away at his Absolute authority was merely a distant acquaintance whose exploits were mildly interesting rather than existentially threatening.
Noah found another unique item to consume, a sphere of compressed frost that held the weight of countless endings within it. He looked at THE Primordial Paradox as he bit into it.
"If you know about him and what he is currently doing to you, and even now as you talk about him..."
He chewed thoughtfully.
"Why do you view him with such nonchalance? Even if you are unable to stop the process, why treat him how you are right now? As if you don’t know?"
THE Primordial Paradox smiled at his words.
It was the smile of someone who had made peace with circumstances that would have driven lesser beings to rage or despair.
"I respect his grind."
The words came with genuine appreciation.
"A peasant with grand ambitions. He simply does not know how immense and grand Existence truly is."
He took another sip of his golden liquid.

"If he possesses the ambition to do what he is doing to me at this very moment, he shall not stop there. He will always seek for more and more, and his actions will lead to things he cannot even imagine."
His obsidian eyes held ancient wisdom.
"More often than not, those with tremendously high ambition bring more trouble to themselves than they can possibly anticipate. It is paradoxical, and it is grand."
The obsidian crown above his head churned and spun with heaviness and Immensity that pressed against reality itself.
"And I know more about Paradox than anyone can imagine. I was born and entrenched in it."
As he spoke, the air of a terrifying Absolute radiated from him.

Noah compared this stifling sensation to the Hollow Echo he had met in The Interstices. That fragment of THE Creature’s lost definition, which had nearly shattered his Seals and forced him to expend an Absolute Everything just to survive...
It wasn’t even a hundredth comparable to the aura that he felt from THE Primordial Paradox before him.
Not even close.
It was just that ridiculously different between them.
The gap between an Echo and the real thing was vast beyond comprehension.
At this time...
THE Primordial Paradox lost his smile.
He frowned, his obsidian features shifting as his attention turned toward the sky above them. Noah also turned and sensed what had drawn the Absolute’s attention.
The auras of two radiant Absolutes in the far distance approaching fast!
"These would be one of the reasons why we did not have time."
THE Primordial Paradox’s voice remained composed, but an edge had entered it.
"They have been camping and waiting to observe exactly what has kept me here this entire time. Whatever I am interested in, my enemies desire even more."
His enemies?
Noah’s eyes flashed brilliantly as he processed this information.
What else would be the enemies of THE Primordial Paradox? He was one of THE Four. He held a Claim on one of the oldest aspects of Existence itself

As if he could sense Noah’s unspoken question, THE Primordial Paradox lounged back on his throne. The auras of two incoming Absolutes didn’t seem to concern him in the slightest. He swirled the golden liquid in his glass with the casual air of someone discussing small talk rather than imminent conflict.
"There are boundless possibilities when Existence is first differentiating."
His voice held the weight of someone who had witnessed things that no longer occurred.
"What is impossible now was the daily occurrence back then. My enemies are those that failed to claim Paradox before THE Infinite Unfurling fully established itself."
WAA!

chapters.title: Chapter 4846: THE Primordial Paradox IV
paragraphs: THE Primordial Paradox took another sip.
"And even now, they remain desperate to do so. Erwin was never the first to attempt taking my Claim from me."
His smile returned as it was thin and knowing.
"He was only the one who managed to succeed. Even though he is nowhere near the most powerful among those who tried."
He set his glass down on the crystalline table.
"And that glimmer of Paradox within him, that capacity to achieve the impossible through methodology rather than raw power... that is at least what made him worthy of attempting this."
His gaze turned over to Noah, shifting from the approaching threats to more immediate concerns.
"Oh, by the way."
His tone became businesslike.
"As big a fan as I am of continuum paradoxes, what I am attempting would have to be very covert. Others cannot really know about the one who helped me."
He studied Noah with eyes that saw more than surface appearances.
"Could you alter yourself or change your identity a little bit? This way, your Weavings can be kept a secret across time."
THE Primordial Paradox actually suggested such a thing.
Noah looked at him while continuing to consume the items laid out on this brilliant table. Another crystal. Another fruit. Another sip of liquid that tasted like finality given form.
He knew that his distinction as the Claimer of The First Tongue was a heavy one.

When he didn’t have sufficient power, it could also bring endless trouble. And the matter right now was a sensitive one. He was trying to grasp more knowledge of the past to understand how to defeat an enemy in the future. If his presence here became known, if his identity was discovered across time...
The complications would be immense.
His existence shone with decision.
His visage began to alter and change.

His figure became wider and taller, expanding from his normal form into something more imposing. Shimmering blue-gold wings erupted from his back, spreading wide with feathers that seemed to be made of crystallized language itself.
Above his head, a crown formed.
But not the crown of 27 Seals that normally accompanied his authority.

This crown looked like a stack of books burning with the light of only 18 Phonemes of The First Tongue. The 18 Core Phonemes that were known at this point in time, before the additional 9 he had forged.

Overall, he looked like a small titanic entity surrounded by what many at this time still knew The First Tongue to be. Powerful. Knowledgeable. But limited to the linguistic understanding of this era rather than the expanded mastery of the future.
THE Primordial Paradox looked at this scene and nodded slowly.
"Your distinction is reined in for the most part."
His voice held approval, but also caution.
"But if others at the level of THE Creature or Chaos take a good look at you, they would still be able to discern the truth."
He tapped his fingers against the arm of his throne.

"So here is just a little assistance from me. To mask what you are, you would have to impose another identity upon yourself. Since it will be impossible not to display your brilliance with The First Tongue, you could be someone who is very proficient in it."
His obsidian eyes twinkled.
"Let me see... how do you like the title of THE Tongue Whisperer?"
BOOM!
As he said such words, THE Primordial Paradox tapped out with one finger.
Waves of Absolute Immensity surged from him, wrapping around Noah with authority that far exceeded anything he came across recently. But the intent was not hostile. The power was not attacking!
The waves coalesced into a physical object that materialized in front of Noah.
A medallion.

Obsidian-gold metal formed into the shape of a river flowing into itself, an endless loop of current that had no beginning and no end. The paradox of a river that was its own source and its own destination, perfectly captured in metal that held Absolute authority within every atom.

|Classification: Absolute Artifact|
|Designation: The Medallion of Infinite Current|
|Function: Veils the signature of one’s power to only be discerned as an Absolute known as THE Tongue Whisperer|
|Creator: THE Primordial Paradox|
|This artifact imposes a false identity at the Absolute level of authority|
|While wearing it, your true distinction will be completely masked|
|Others will perceive you as THE Tongue Whisperer, an Absolute of unknown origin with mastery over The First Tongue|
Noah looked at this medallion in his hands with shining eyes.
THE Tongue Whisperer.
He had heard that name before!
When he last visited Ginnungagap, names had been mentioned as he moved with Ul’moreth. THE Creature. THE Primordial Paradox. THE Living Paradox. THE Secretive Eon.
And among them, spoken with the same weight and reverence...
THE Tongue Whisperer.

After that Temporal Traversal, he had never come across anything else relating to THE Tongue Whisperer. It was as if the entity had simply vanished from history, leaving behind nothing but a name whispered in the oldest places of Existence.
He had wondered, briefly, who THE Tongue Whisperer had been and whether he would meet them like he came across THE Secretive Eon in the future!
And now...
Now he was looking at a medallion that would make him THE Tongue Whisperer.
He was the fucking Tongue Whisperer?
The mysterious Absolute mentioned alongside the greatest beings in Observable Existence during the early stages of THE Infinite Unfurling?
Oh!
The closed temporal loop revealed another layer of its complexity!
Time.
It was so fucking messy.

Noah placed the medallion around his neck, and the moment the obsidian-gold metal touched his chest, he felt his identity shift. His aura changed. His signature transformed. The weight of THE Genesis Monarch, Claimer of The First Tongue, one of THE Four...
All of it became something else.
THE Tongue Whisperer.
An Absolute of unknown origin and master of The First Tongue in ways that defied easy explanation.
THE Primordial Paradox smiled as he observed the transformation complete itself.
"Much better."
His voice held satisfaction.
"Now then, THE Tongue Whisperer..."
The approaching auras of two enemy Absolutes grew stronger, closer, more immediate.
"Let me swat a few gnats away and even teach a lesson. I can be considered a Senior among THE Four so I can always be a little kinder to our Youngest of THE Four. Do you know about Apophasis?"

Erwin was never the first to attempt taking my Claim from me."
His smile returned as it was thin and knowing.
"He was only the one who managed to succeed.
Even though he is nowhere near the most powerful among those who tried."
He set his glass down on the crystalline table.
"And that glimmer of Paradox within him, that capacity to achieve the impossible through methodology rather than raw power... that is at least what made him worthy of attempting this."
His gaze turned over to Noah, shifting from the approaching threats to more immediate concerns.
"Oh, by the way."
His tone became businesslike.

THE Primordial Paradox actually suggested such a thing.

Another fruit.
Another sip of liquid that tasted like finality given form.
He knew that his distinction as the Claimer of The First Tongue was a heavy one.
When he didn’t have sufficient power, it could also bring endless trouble.

If his presence here became known, if his identity was discovered across time...
The complications would be immense.
His existence shone with decision.
His visage began to alter and change.
His figure became wider and taller, expanding from his normal form into something more imposing.
Shimmering blue-gold wings erupted from his back, spreading wide with feathers that seemed to be made of crystallized language itself.
Above his head, a crown formed.

This crown looked like a stack of books burning with the light of only 18 Phonemes of The First Tongue.
The 18 Core Phonemes that were known at this point in time, before the additional 9 he had forged.
Overall, he looked like a small titanic entity surrounded by what many at this time still knew The First Tongue to be.
Powerful.
Knowledgeable.
But limited to the linguistic understanding of this era rather than the expanded mastery of the future.

chapters.title: Chapter 4847: Apophasis! I
paragraphs: Apophasis.
Noah knew of this ancient expression of power for Absolutes.
It operated differently from Declarations or Embodiments, existing in a space of negation rather than assertion!
But he had never seen it demonstrated by someone who truly understood it.
So for now, he shook his head lightly, wanting to see how THE Primordial Paradox expressed Apophasis!
THE Primordial Paradox set down his obsidian glass and regarded Noah with a measured gaze.
THE Primordial Paradox then leaned back on his throne, his obsidian crown spinning slowly above his head.
"Most expressions of power operate through positive declaration. One states what they are, what they can do, what authority they hold. This is effective, certainly. But it is also limiting."
His fingers traced patterns in the air that left trails of paradoxical light.
"To declare ’I am immortal’ binds you to a concept of immortality. You have defined yourself, and in defining yourself, you have created parameters. Parameters can be exploited. Countered. Overcome."
He paused, letting those words settle.
"Apophasis operates through the opposite principle. Negation. One defines what something is by declaring what it is not."
His obsidian eyes held weight that pressed against reality.

"Consider the difference. ’I am immortal’ creates a definition that can be attacked. But ’I am not subject to death’ eliminates the concept entirely. You have not declared yourself anything. You have simply removed the constraint."
Noah’s eyes shone with understanding as he absorbed this.
"Each negation removes a fundamental limitation until the entity exists outside normal parameters entirely. They have not declared themselves free. They have simply removed the chains."
THE Primordial Paradox smiled.

"At its highest expression, Apophasis renders an entity nearly unassailable. There is nothing to attack because nothing has been declared. The only counter is to negate the negation itself, but this...oh, this creates paradoxes that can destabilize local Existence. And I love paradoxes, and I....thrive on paradoxes."
His smile widened!

Noah’s eyes shone with calm light as he listened while continuing to eat. It was a grand expression of power, one that aligned perfectly with the nature of the being explaining it. Who better to wield negation than someone whose very Claim was built upon contradiction?
He wouldn’t mind seeing it in action!
As if Existence itself had heard that thought, the skies above them rumbled.
The auras of two Absolutes descended.
And they were grand!

What Noah saw were oddities of nature, beings that defied easy categorization even among the already impossible classification of Absolute. They had clearly existed since the early stages of THE Infinite Unfurling, their forms shaped by an era when reality was still deciding what shapes power could take.
The first was a creature ofshadow and wing.

Its form was that of a massive bat-like entity, but wrong in ways that made the eyes struggle to process. A single enormous eye dominated its face where two should have been, burning with crimson light that seemed to see through multiple layers of reality simultaneously.

Its wings stretched wide enough to cast shadows across Naglfar’s deck, membranes of darkness that absorbed light rather than reflecting it. Its body was muscular and twisted, limbs that bent at angles that shouldn’t have supported movement but clearly did.
|Entity Analysis|
|Designation: Popobawa, THE Singular Eye|
|Classification: Absolute|
|Civilization: The Paradox of Perception|
|Way of Perception: That which is seen from one angle does not exist from another|
|Foundation: Built upon the contradiction between observation and reality|
|Historical context: One of the failed claimants to Paradox before THE Infinite Unfurling established its current parameters|
|Threat assessment: Significant, but currently maybe outclassed by present company?|
The second was a bird of lightning and hunger.

Its form was avian but terrible, feathers that crackled with contained storms, eyes that held the hollow emptiness of something that fed on life itself. Electricity arced between its wings with each movement, and its beak was curved and cruel, designed for tearing rather than pecking. Its talons gripped nothing but air, yet somehow it perched upon that emptiness as if it were solid ground.
|Entity Analysis|
|Designation: Impundulu, THE Storm That Hungers|
|Classification: Absolute|
|Civilization: The Paradox of Consumption|
|Way of Consumption: That which feeds grows stronger, yet that which grows stronger must feed more|
|Foundation: Built upon the contradiction between sustenance and starvation|
|Historical context: Another failed claimant to Paradox, allied with Popobawa in their continued attempts|
|Threat assessment: Significant, currently radiating hostile intent|
|Note: Both of these entities have been pursuing THE Primordial Paradox’s Claim since before you were born, Master|
|They have failed every time|

Their bodies radiated an air of archaic might, power that had been accumulated across eons of existence in an era when such accumulation was simpler than it had become. They descended toward Naglfar with the confidence of predators who had finally cornered their prey.
The moment they arrived, Impundulu opened its crackling beak.
"Paradox! For too long you have-"
"Shh."
THE Primordial Paradox did not rise from his throne.
He did not even shift his posture.

He simply raised one finger, and an instant later, the mouth of the talking Impundulu closed. The Absolute’s beak snapped shut with a sound like thunder being strangled, and its eyes widened with shock as it discovered something impossible.
It could not speak.
It could not express itself.
The words it had prepared, the threats it had crafted, the Embodiments it had intended to make...
All of it was gone.
"You are not capable of expression."
THE Primordial Paradox’s voice was calm, almost bored.
"Your words are not heard. Your intent is not communicated. Your voice is not present in this space."
BOOM!

The Apophasis settled over Impundulu like chains made of absence, each negation removing something fundamental from its existence. It hadn’t been silenced. Silence implied the potential for sound. It had simply been removed from the category of beings capable of making themselves understood!
THE Primordial Paradox looked at Noah as if an older brother was explaining something unique to the youngest member of the family.
"Sometimes, when you permit others to live because they provide you with fond memories, they mistake it for weakness."
His obsidian eyes held ancient amusement.
"So an example has to be made to remind them why they lost in the first place."
