chapters.title: Chapter 4865: Looking For A Local! I
paragraphs: What was an Infinite Everything?

It was a heavy question that pressed against his mind with weight that demanded answers. An Absolute Everything could elevate a Half-Step Absolute to full Absolute status if their foundation was heavy enough. It was the pinnacle of Civilizational Authority compressed into a single resource.
But an Infinite Everything?
What could something infinite do that something merely Absolute could not?
He wanted to explore this question, wanted to understand what had changed within him and how he could use it to further his goals. The question burned in his mind!
But it didn’t seem like he would be given the chance to explore and ask.
Because THE Undivided One, Bazuman, who had looked startled for the first time in its existence...
Was no longer startled.

The massive being with countless eyes began to dance with horror-inducing excitement, its form shifting and expanding as if the challenge of prey that could escape had awakened something primal within it. Joy radiated from its crimson eyes. Anticipation leaked from its jagged jaws. For the first time in eons, it had found something interesting.
Something that might actually be fun to hunt.

The many eyes across its form began to glow with concentrated light, and then they differentiated that light into beams of obsidian brilliance that surged toward Noah with speed that exceeded anything he had encountered since arriving in THE Prima Indifferentia.
|Attack Analysis|
|Designation: Rays of Undifferentiated Annihilation|
|These beams carry both Depth and the light of undifferentiation simultaneously|
|Being hit with them is instant annihilation for anything below Absolute|
|Your Infinite nature may provide resistance to the undifferentiation aspect|
|You might survive a blast or two|
|You will not survive sustained bombardment|
|Recommendation: Do not get hit|
The prompts were menacing ones that left no room for optimism or cleverness.
Noah didn’t tarry.

He flared his infinities once more, releasing the blue-gold light that burned within his existence outward into the surrounding proto-matter. The undefined substance responded to his infinity with eagerness that he hadn’t expected, churning and gathering around him as if it wanted to be part of whatever he was becoming.

A storm of proto-matter erupted around his form, denser and more violent than the one that had carried him here. The beams of obsidian light charging toward him struck this storm and became distorted, their trajectories bending as the proto-matter interfered with their ability to maintain definition long enough to hit their target.

Noah silently gave direction to his infinities, and the storm of proto-matter didn’t just emerge but began to move. His existence became a flicker of blue-gold light that shot away from THE Undivided One at speeds that the storms themselves enhanced, carrying him deeper into THE Prima Indifferentia and away from a creature that had never lost prey before and clearly didn’t intend to start now!
Running away was never a bad thing.
Especially when the enemy seeking to collapse you was levels above anything you could currently handle.

Behind him, Bazuman’s screech of excitement echoed across the undefined expanse, and Noah could feel the creature beginning to pursue. Its million eyes tracked his trajectory. Its countless mouths opened in anticipation. Its entire existence oriented itself toward the hunt!
But Noah had something that Bazuman couldn’t undifferentiate.
Surviving alone was arduous enough as it was.
He had to find a solution in a place filled with dangers and opportunities, had to locate THE Primordial Paradox or find his own way back to the Crack of Observable Existence!
The storm of proto-matter carried him forward, away from the horror behind him and toward whatever waited ahead!
In THE Prima Indifferentia, there were no safe directions.
But some directions were less dangerous than others.
Well, hopefully anyways!
In another region of THE Prima Indifferentia near The Crack of Observable Existence.

THE Primordial Paradox stood amidst the churning expanse of proto-matter with a frowning expression, his eyes closed as if he were trying to sense something that refused to be sensed. His obsidian form remained perfectly defined despite the constant pressure of undifferentiation that would have eroded lesser beings, his very nature as the holder of the Paradox Claim creating a bubble of stability in a place that rejected stability as a concept.

Around him, proto-matter weaved and bent as if his paradoxical existence made it impossible to be undifferentiated. The undefined substance couldn’t seem to decide whether he was part of it or separate from it, whether he belonged here or didn’t, and that confusion protected him.
But as he couldn’t find what he wanted, he shook his head and sighed with exhaustion.
He had brought THE Youngest here.

And now the being who carried The First Tongue had been swept away by storms of proto-matter that THE Primordial Paradox should have anticipated and prevented. It seemed the infection was grabbing more of him than he expected.

He raised his hand and tapped the area in front of him, and a crack opened in the undefined space that had nothing to do with the Crack of Observable Existence. This was something else entirely, a communication method that transcended normal spatial relationships, forming into an illusory screen that pulsed with unique authority connecting two points across Existence regardless of the distance between them.
Moments later, an image formed on this screen.

The entity that appeared was shrouded in multicolored flames, his body fully drenched with fires of Existence that burned in every color simultaneously. These weren’t flames that consumed but flames that simply were, the visual manifestation of pure being given form. His entire figure couldn’t be fully observed because observing it would have required definition, and this entity existed at a level where definition was something he chose to wear rather than something imposed upon him.
He was presence incarnate!
He was THE Creature.
THE Primordial Paradox looked at this being, and without even an introduction or pleasantries, he spoke directly.
"Would you happen to be in THE Prima Indifferentia right now? I may need the assistance of a local."

At such words, the figure on the illusory screen stared back at THE Primordial Paradox with eyes that couldn’t be seen but could definitely be felt. When he replied, his voice boomed with resonance that seemed to echo out from the screen and cause the proto-matter in the surroundings to churn wildly before settling down respectfully, as if this voice was soothing and one that demanded acknowledgment simply by existing.
"You know I am not a local there."
THE Primordial Paradox waved his hand dismissively.
"Yes, yes, you keep mentioning Alfheimr. But I am in a bind here as I lost someone, and I need to find them rather quickly."
The expression of THE Primordial Paradox was calm as he said all of this.

The figure surrounded by flames of Existence remained stoic and grand on the illusory screen, his presence pressing against the communication channel with weight that made even this distant projection feel overwhelming.
"You have been masking yourself actively from Existence and everything else for quite some time now."
THE Creature’s voice held observation rather than accusation.
"Even I have had no idea who is around you. I was only able to learn about the distinction of THE Tongue Whisperer."
The multicolored flames flickered with something that might have been curiosity.
"Is this the one that you lost?"

chapters.title: Chapter 4866: Looking For A Local! II
paragraphs: At such words, THE Primordial Paradox nodded lightly.
He didn’t elaborate on who THE Tongue Whisperer was or why he had brought someone with mastery over The First Tongue into THE Prima Indifferentia.
THE Creature on the illusory screen was silent for a moment, his flames shifting through patterns of consideration and calculation occurring behind eyes that couldn’t be perceived.
"I am not in THE Prima Indifferentia right now."
His voice carried finality regarding that particular option.
"But a local from there should be able to help you."
A local from here.
These words alone caused THE Primordial Paradox to frown. The proto-matter around him churned in response to his emotional state, reflecting his unease with increased agitation.

"Any locals here apart from you are either mad or out for Existence itself. THE Undivided Ones cannot be reasoned with, THE Formless Terrors seek only to undifferentiate others, and everything else that has survived here long enough to be called local has done so by becoming something that should not be trusted."
THE Creature on the illusory screen waved his hands in a dismissive manner, the multicolored flames trailing after his movements like loyal attendants.
"If you want my assistance, that is the extent of it."
His voice held no room for argument.
"Call out his name until he finds you as you move across THE Prima Indifferentia. Simply call for Jack."
Jack?

THE Primordial Paradox tilted his head at this name, his obsidian crown spinning with confusion that he didn’t bother to hide. The designation seemed too casual, too mundane for something that could survive as a local in a place where Absolutes became Formless Terrors and THE Undivided Ones hunted anything with definition.
With his display of confusion evident, THE Creature on the illusory screen clarified.
"Jack. Jokul. He prefers to be alone and unbothered, but he owes me a favour."
The multicolored flames shifted with something that might have been fondness.
"Whoever you lost in there, Jack should be able to find them."
A pause.
"Unless you did something as reckless as bringing someone that was not Absolute into THE Prima Indifferentia."
The flames darkened slightly.
"If they are away from you for just a matter of seconds, they may already be undifferentiated."

The words felt like a heavy and somber warning, the kind that only someone who truly understood THE Prima Indifferentia’s dangers could give. THE Creature had spent more time here than any other member of THE Four, had explored regions that even THE Primordial Paradox had never ventured toward, and his caution was not given lightly.
THE Primordial Paradox smiled and shook his head.
"I do not think so. Not this one, anyway."
"But what will this cost me?"
Nothing between THE Four was ever truly free, and favours owed to THE Creature were not things to be accumulated carelessly.
THE Creature’s flames stilled on the illusory screen, becoming almost solid for a moment as he considered his price.
"You can tell me what is happening with you."
His voice lost its casual edge, becoming something more serious.
"Do I need to be worried?"
Did he need to be worried?

The entity shrouded by multicolored flames of Existence, the being that THE Primordial Paradox had reached out to for help, THE Creature himself, was asking about the state of THE Primordial Paradox with concern!
And THE Primordial Paradox smiled with the expression of someone who had made peace with circumstances that others would have raged against.
"It is nothing major."
His voice held acceptance rather than defeat.
"I shall simply be going to sleep for a little while, as someone else would likely take my place."
He paused, considering his next words carefully.
"They will not be as entertaining as I am, but observe whether they are worthy or even capable of progressing toward the Second Scale. I am curious myself, after all of this."
THE Primordial Paradox said such foreboding words with a casual air.
THE Creature in the illusory screen looked out silently without a reply.
His multicolored flames burned with intensity that made the proto-matter around THE Primordial Paradox tremble, responding to the emotional weight of what had just been shared.
An immense silence settled across the communication channel, neither of them speaking as the weight of the moment pressed against them both.
Eventually, THE Creature spoke.
"It seems that you have found yet another hardship to overcome."
His voice was measured and heavy.
"If the adversity is tremendous enough, it may just be sufficient fuel for you to take a step toward the second Scale. After all, The Vakochev Scales demand hardship..."
The multicolored flames flickered with something ancient.
"Very well. But be careful."
His voice grew deeper.
"One can plan and plan endlessly, but you never truly know what Existence has in store. None of us know."
HUUM!
"None of us will ever truly know."
The surrounding proto-matter trembled at the words of THE Creature with a sense of fear and reverence.
THE Primordial Paradox listened silently before he nodded with the weight of farewell hidden behind his composed features.
He waved his hands.
The illusory screen portraying THE Creature disappeared, the communication channel closing and leaving THE Primordial Paradox alone once more in the churning expanse of THE Prima Indifferentia.
He stood there for a moment, allowing himself a breath.
Then he straightened his obsidian form and looked around at the undefined expanse surrounding him.
He had a Tongue Whisperer to find.
And he had limited time before the infection within him progressed to stages that would make movement impossible.

THE Primordial Paradox began to walk through THE Prima Indifferentia, his voice calling out across the undefined space with authority that pressed against the proto-matter and forced it to carry his words further than they should have been able to travel.
"Jokul!"
The name echoed across churning storms and pillars of undefined potential.
"Jack!"
He called again, moving deeper into the expanse while searching for both a being he had never met and the one he had lost!

THE Creature in the illusory screen looked out silently without a reply.
His multicolored flames burned with intensity that made the proto-matter around THE Primordial Paradox tremble, responding to the emotional weight of what had just been shared.
An immense silence settled across the communication channel, neither of them speaking as the weight of the moment pressed against them both.
Eventually, THE Creature spoke.
"It seems that you have found yet another hardship to overcome."
His voice was measured and heavy.
"If the adversity is tremendous enough, it may just be sufficient fuel for you to take a step toward the second Scale.
After all, The Vakochev Scales demand hardship..."
The multicolored flames flickered with something ancient.
"Very well.
But be careful."
His voice grew deeper.
"One can plan and plan endlessly, but you never truly know what Existence has in store.
None of us know."
HUUM!
"None of us will ever truly know."
The surrounding proto-matter trembled at the words of THE Creature with a sense of fear and reverence.
THE Primordial Paradox listened silently before he nodded with the weight of farewell hidden behind his composed features.
He waved his hands.
The illusory screen portraying THE Creature disappeared, the communication channel closing and leaving THE Primordial Paradox alone once more in the churning expanse of THE Prima Indifferentia.
He stood there for a moment, allowing himself a breath.
Then he straightened his obsidian form and looked around at the undefined expanse surrounding him.
He had a Tongue Whisperer to find.
And he had limited time before the infection within him progressed to stages that would make movement impossible.

THE Primordial Paradox began to walk through THE Prima Indifferentia, his voice calling out across the undefined space with authority that pressed against the proto-matter and forced it to carry his words further than they should have been able to travel.
"Jokul!"
The name echoed across churning storms and pillars of undefined potential.
"Jack!"
He called again, moving deeper into the expanse while searching for both a being he had never met and the one he had lost!

chapters.title: Chapter 4867: Undifferentiation!
paragraphs: Even moving and breathing felt tough at this moment for Noah.

With every breath he took, even though he didn’t need to take a breath, he felt like he was breathing in all of himself and breathing out all of himself simultaneously. The infinity that had bathed his existence wasn’t something he could simply possess and move on from!

He felt like with every passing moment he was breathing in infinity and expelling infinity, his lungs becoming conduits. It was a unique sensation to have, both exhilarating and terrifying in equal measure.
It would have been ideal to have at least a few minutes to acclimate to the immense changes across his existence.
But he was being forced to do all of this acclimation while being chased by a monstrous creature who could decimate Absolutes with the casual ease of a child crushing insects.

The only reason that he was surviving as long as he was came down to a single factor: the Immensity of Bazuman that could undifferentiate so many things was not working on him because it couldn’t undifferentiate his infinity.
But this creature also held a terrifying Depth.

So the beams of incandescent light chasing after him, those Rays of Undifferentiated Annihilation, would only take one or two direct hits before this body would be crumbled and this temporal traversal would come to an end.

The proto-matter storms around him churned with increasing violence as Noah pushed them to move faster, his infinities directing their flow while he rode their currents like a leaf in a hurricane. Behind him, Bazuman’s countless crimson eyes tracked his trajectory with interest that had transformed into genuine excitement, the horror of a million jaws opening and closing with anticipation as if they were a predator on a particularly enjoyable hunt.
But with every passing instant, Noah acclimated more and more to his existence and the Immensity that it currently carried.
"Oh?"
He asked himself this question as if he didn’t believe what he was perceiving to be true, as he came to grasp something about himself that he tried right away.
Because with infinity bathing everything, it also bathed his Seals of Absolute Tongue that represented his Way and Civilization.
They weren’t just seals anymore.

At this moment, as his figure burning with blue-gold light shot out toward one direction while surrounded by storms of proto-matter, the beams that could collapse and undifferentiate were bypassing more and more of the storm. The proto-matter could only distort their trajectories so much before the weight of Bazuman’s Depth forced them through, and they were about to reach him with devastating impact.
At such a time, Noah flung his arm back.
He threw out asingleAbsolute Seal of Infinity.
And utmost brilliance ensued right after.
|Existential Observation|
|The Absolute Seals representing your Civilization are now Infinite|
|They have no limit to their number|
|They have no constraint on their manifestation|
|You threw one|
|Infinity responded|
BOOM!

Even though Noah had thrown out a single seal of infinity, in the next moment, a flood of endless seals bloomed out like radiant blue-gold flowers unfurling across the undefined space of THE Prima Indifferentia.

The seals emerged from that single point of release and multiplied endlessly, each one spawning more and more until the entire region behind Noah became a garden of linguistic authority made manifest. They looked like countless blue-gold plum blossoms emerging from his existence, their petals formed from concentrated Phonemes and their centers burning with the weight of his Civilization.

A unique sound bloomed out with the emergence of infinite seals of infinity, a resonance that was simultaneously a whisper and a roar, the sound of one becoming many becoming infinite. The proto-matter around them responded with awe!

The sheer number of the seals was so overwhelming that the terrifying and perilous beams of light stemming from THE Undivided One became covered entirely, their trajectories intersecting with petal after petal after petal of blue-gold authority. They smashed into these seals with force that should have shattered anything below Absolute, and the seals did shatter, breaking apart into motes of linguistic light.
But for every seal that broke, infinity provided another.
And another.
And another.

Momentarily, the entire region looked like a beautiful scene filled with blue-gold scattered plum blossoms, a garden of impossible flowers blooming in a place where gardens had never existed and flowers had never been differentiated. The seals resisted undifferentiation because they were born from infinity, and infinity couldn’t be made less than it was, so they overcame the terrifying light released by THE Undivided One through sheer inexhaustible presence.
But because the Depth of this being was still there, and the density and weight of Noah’s seals was nowhere as immense as this terrifying entity chasing after him...
BOOM!
The beams that had been distorted were reinforced by something far more direct.

Millions of tentacles erupted from Bazuman’s ever-shifting form, each one ending in jaws that gnashed with hunger that transcended normal appetite. They surged through the garden of infinite seals, tearing through the blue-gold blossoms with physical force rather than undifferentiation, using raw Depth to accomplish what conceptual attack could not.
The many crimson eyes of THE Undivided One seemed to show more and more interest toward Noah, gleaming with excitement that made the proto-matter around them tremble with sympathetic dread.
"Little one."

The voice that emerged from Bazuman was wrong in ways that transcended description, coming from everywhere and nowhere simultaneously, formed from concepts that hadn’t fully differentiated into sound.
"Do not struggle."
The tentacles pressed forward, crushing seals by the thousands even as thousands more bloomed to replace them.
"Just let me have a taste."
HUUM!

Noah looked back with a calm and solemn gaze even as seals continued to flood from his hand like an endless tide of flower petals. The Immensity of THE Undivided One still drew near despite his infinite defense, the tentacles and jaws closing the distance through brute force that his seals couldn’t fully resist.
He searched inside of his existence for something more.

He hadn’t yet pulled upon the Infinite Everything that had formed within him, choosing to give his existence a chance to break it down and understand what it truly was before utilizing it. Because everything was new at this moment, and being in this region of THE Prima Indifferentia caused RUINATION to constantly fight an influx of undifferentiation, the analysis was taking longer than usual.
But it was still his existence, and the things that weren’t new were rapidly becoming clear to him.
Right now, when he considered how he could overcome something so much stronger than him to survive, another infinity bloomed and blazed with light within his foundations.
His main Civilization allowed for him to burn with this light of infinity, but he wasn’t alone in that burning.
There were Derivative Civilizations under him.

THE Civilizational Authority of Infinite Hunger stirred within his existence, the endless appetite that had consumed THE Paradox of Consumption and reached Half-Step Absolute as a result. THE Civilizational Authority of Infinite Undifferentiated Fate stirred alongside it, the connection to destiny that touched upon the very nature of this place.
Both of them permeated into all of the seals of infinity that he was releasing.

The vibrant blue-gold petals endlessly raging all around him took on shades of crimson from the Hunger and even more gold from the Undifferentiated Fate. They transformed from defensive flowers into something else entirely, their edges becoming sharper, their presence becoming hungrier, their nature becoming more aligned with THE Prima Indifferentia itself.
And shockingly, as if they had gained an extremely sharp edge that cut through more than just physical matter...
ZING!
The tentacles and incorporeal beams of brilliance from THE Undivided One began to be caught up and sliced and broken down.
The seals weren’t just blocking anymore.
They were devouring!
They were undifferentiating!

Tentacles that touched the crimson-tinged petals found themselves being consumed, their undefined flesh feeding into the Infinite Hunger that now permeated every seal. Beams of annihilation that struck the gold-touched blossoms found themselves being destabilized, their undifferentiation turned back upon them by seals that now carried the quality of THE Prima Indifferentia itself.
|Combat Analysis - Updated|
|You have learned to infuse Infinite Hunger and Infinite Undifferentiated Fate into your attacks|
|Your seals now carry a quality of endlessly devouring|
|They also carry a quality that only those native to THE Prima Indifferentia possess|
|The quality to induce undifferentiation|
|Even though your Depth is insufficient to survive direct confrontation with THE Undivided One|
|You have thrown out an infinite number of seals that now have the capability to break down and undifferentiate everything thrown at you|
|Bazuman is experiencing attacks being consumed and undifferentiated by prey|
|This will not last|
|Take this brief respite and run before THE Undivided One decides to get truly serious|
|Run!|
BOOM!

The infinite seals continued to flood from his existence, creating a barrier of hungry, undifferentiating petals that bought him precious moments of distance. Behind him, Bazuman paused for the first time since the chase began, its million crimson eyes blinking in what might have been surprise as it watched its tentacles being devoured and its beams being destabilized.

And that novelty, that unprecedented experience, gave Noah the seconds he needed to push his proto-matter storm faster, to ride the currents of undefined potential deeper into THE Prima Indifferentia, to put distance between himself and something that could still absolutely destroy him if it chose to commit fully as...
BOOM!
He disappeared as if the storm of Proto-matter had reached a warping concentration, similar to what took him away from THE Primordial Paradox!
Behind him, the garden of infinite seals continued to bloom and devour and undifferentiate as the jaws of an Undivided One smiled devilishly with brutality, but his prey...was gone!

chapters.title: Chapter 4868: Jokul!
paragraphs: Truth be told, THE Primordial Paradox was a bit regretful.

How could he lose someone pivotal to his reemergence in the future? He had brought THE Youngest to THE Prima Indifferentia because he had a pretty good idea that this was where THE Entity was stemming from, and the pieces fit in his mind perfectly based on the nature of the infection and what it was currently doing to him.
THE Entity sought to undifferentiate.
THE Prima Indifferentia was the source of all undifferentiation.
The connection seemed obvious once he had examined it from the right angle.

What he couldn’t figure out was how someone as weak as Erwin had gotten his hands on something so powerful in the first place. How Erwin himself wasn’t affected by the very weapon he was wielding. And how he was utilizing it to the extent that even THE Primordial Paradox didn’t know when this attack on his Claim had actually started.

This trip to THE Prima Indifferentia was meant to illuminate things somewhat, to provide THE Tongue Whisperer with understanding that could be used against THE Entity in the future when it had fully emerged and threatened all of Observable Existence.
But...
"It’s a proper mess."

THE Primordial Paradox shook his head as his Immensity surged out once more, his voice carrying across the churning expanse of proto-matter with authority that forced the undefined substance to transmit his words further than they should have been able to travel.
"Jokul!"
HUUM!

He had been doing so for quite a long time now, and every time he called out, he was risking pulling in terrifying entities toward his position. His voice was a beacon in a place where beacons attracted predators, and THE Prima Indifferentia had no shortage of things that would be very interested in consuming one of THE Four.
Well, there were now two of THE Four here!
Oh!

He had actually already rebuffed an undifferentiated creature who sought to break down his paradoxical nature, his Apophasis turning the attack back on itself and sending the formless thing retreating into the proto-matter storms from whence it came.
If he continued doing this anymore, something worse would find him.
He just had this thought when in the next moment his eyes brightened, and he looked out toward his right with sudden alertness.
There, a humanoid visage of an entity with no discernible waves of power formed from the proto-matter itself.

He was adorned in an ancient white robe that seemed impossibly clean given the environment, the fabric untouched by the churning chaos that surrounded everything else in this place. Dark flowing hair fell past his shoulders, moving in currents that had nothing to do with the proto-matter storms. His eyes were filled with ancient Immensity that didn’t radiate outward but rather pulled inward, as if everything around him was being drawn toward a singularity of stillness that defied THE Prima Indifferentia’s constant motion.

Behind him was the illusion of an inverted mountain radiating immense coldness, its peak pointing downward into depths that couldn’t be perceived, its base spreading upward into skies that didn’t exist. The mountain wasn’t really there, but it was also more real than anything else in this region of undefined space.
The moment this being arrived, the proto-matter in the surroundings began freezing over.

Not freezing in the sense of becoming ice, but freezing in the sense of becoming still. The churning stopped. The undefined potential ceased its constant shifting. Everything achieved a state of stasis that shouldn’t have been possible in a place defined by perpetual change, and the silence that followed was so profound that it pressed against THE Primordial Paradox’s existence with weight that would have crushed lesser beings.
"Why have you been shouting my name?"

The words of this entity sounded heavy and filled with weight that could freeze even weaker Absolutes in their tracks. There was no hostility in his tone, but there was also no warmth, only the absolute certainty of something that had existed long enough to be utterly unimpressed by anything it might encounter.

THE Primordial Paradox looked at this being up and down in evaluation, his obsidian eyes taking in every detail of the entity before him while revealing nothing of his own assessment. His voice came out calm even as he processed what he was perceiving.
"I was told to scream your name to find you. I asked THE Creature for the assistance of a local in locating someone that I lost in this place."
He paused, his obsidian crown spinning slowly.
"I simply never expected him to have connections with something like you. I cannot pinpoint whether you are an Undivided One or a Formless Terror or something worse entirely."

His words were calm even as they came out, carrying the measured precision that defined all of his words. And the entity they were directed to also remained calm, his ancient eyes showing no reaction to being analyzed by one of THE Four as if such analysis was beneath his notice.
When he heard the name of THE Creature, his eyes flickered briefly, and he seemed to think for a moment before giving a light nod.
"Who are you looking for?"
THE Primordial Paradox smiled at the fact that his entire set of words were ignored except for the most important one.

"I am looking for someone whose existence is currently surrounded by the designation of THE Tongue Whisperer. He should have a flicker of the signature of The First Tongue burning brightly around him."

The entity opposite to THE Primordial Paradox simply nodded at these words as he turned around, apparently ready to begin the search without any further discussion. The frozen proto-matter remained still around him, held in stasis by his mere presence.
THE Primordial Paradox continued to look at him with curiosity that he didn’t bother to hide, and he couldn’t help but ask the question that pressed against his mind.
"Who are you, really?"

At these words, the figure of Jokul turned around and looked at THE Primordial Paradox with extremely calm eyes that held depths which even someone who had existed since before THE Infinite Unfurling couldn’t fully perceive.
"You have been calling my name this entire time."
His voice was flat, stating fact rather than expressing emotion.
"Jokul. Jokul Anaximander."
He paused, and the inverted mountain behind him seemed to grow larger for just a moment.
"But call me Jack. To you, I am simply a friend of THE Creature. Nothing more and nothing less."
His ancient eyes held no deception because there was nothing to deceive about, only the truth of what he was willing to share and the silence of everything he wasn’t.
"And as for the one that you lost..."

The frozen proto-matter in the surroundings began to churn and pulse with a heart-shaking brilliance that emanated from Jokul himself, his stillness somehow becoming motion without ever actually moving. The inverted mountain behind him blazed with light that was also darkness, with cold that was also presence.
"I know where THE Tongue Whisperer is."
WAA!
He said these words as if they were an affirmation or something that he was uttering to then be true.
The proto-matter responded by revealing pathways that hadn’t existed before, frozen currents that pointed toward a specific direction in a place where direction shouldn’t have been possible.
But an instant later, his eyes shone with piercing light as he nodded his head with what might have been interest.
"It seems like it will take some time, as an Undivided One is hunting him."
He paused.
"But I have found him. Let us go."
An Undivided One was hunting him?
Now THE Primordial Paradox was entirely surprised. The proto-matter around them seemed to darken in response to his sudden concern.
"An Undivided One is hunting him and he has not been undifferentiated or collapsed?"
Was THE Youngest so fearsome when he hadn’t even become an Absolute yet?

THE Primordial Paradox had brought THE Youngest here expecting challenges, yes, but he had also expected to be present to help navigate those challenges. For someone of Fundamental Depth to survive being hunted by an Undivided One, even for a short time, was unprecedented.
The visage of Jokul turned toward THE Primordial Paradox with a calm gaze that held neither concern nor reassurance.
"We can wait a little bit more for THE Formless Terrors or more Undivided Ones to find him, or for him to land in the gazes of THE Primordial Architects."
His voice was utterly flat.
"Then he will really be undifferentiated or collapsed. He will die. Shall we wait?"
THE Primordial Paradox looked at the deadpan expression of Jokul as his sharp eyes flashed with irritation. The proto-matter around them seemed to hold its breath, waiting for his response.
He took a step to appear beside this being, his obsidian form closing the distance instantaneously.
"Well, all of us will one day die, but...why say such horror-inducing things?"
His voice was serious.
"Let us go. I cannot afford to lose this one."

With such words, the visage of Jokul turned toward another direction entirely, one that the frozen pathways in the proto-matter hadn’t indicated, and disappeared into the churning expanse with movement that wasn’t movement.
His voice echoed out across the undefined space with weight that pressed against everything it touched.
"Keep up."

THE Primordial Paradox followed, his obsidian form cutting through the proto-matter as he pursued this enigmatic being called Jokul Anaximander, or really, Jack, toward THE Youngest who was somehow surviving being hunted by an Undivided One!

The moment this being arrived, the proto-matter in the surroundings began freezing over.
Not freezing in the sense of becoming ice, but freezing in the sense of becoming still.
The churning stopped.
The undefined potential ceased its constant shifting.

Everything achieved a state of stasis that shouldn’t have been possible in a place defined by perpetual change, and the silence that followed was so profound that it pressed against THE Primordial Paradox’s existence with weight that would have crushed lesser beings.
"Why have you been shouting my name?"
The words of this entity sounded heavy and filled with weight that could freeze even weaker Absolutes in their tracks.
There was no hostility in his tone, but there was also no warmth, only the absolute certainty of something that had existed long enough to be utterly unimpressed by anything it might encounter.
THE Primordial Paradox looked at this being up and down in evaluation, his obsidian eyes taking in every detail of the entity before him while revealing nothing of his own assessment.
His voice came out calm even as he processed what he was perceiving.
"I was told to scream your name to find you.
I asked THE Creature for the assistance of a local in locating someone that I lost in this place."
He paused, his obsidian crown spinning slowly.
"I simply never expected him to have connections with something like you.
I cannot pinpoint whether you are an Undivided One or a Formless Terror or something worse entirely."
His words were calm even as they came out, carrying the measured precision that defined all of his words.
And the entity they were directed to also remained calm, his ancient eyes showing no reaction to being analyzed by one of THE Four as if such analysis was beneath his notice.
When he heard the name of THE Creature, his eyes flickered briefly, and he seemed to think for a moment before giving a light nod.
"Who are you looking for?"
THE Primordial Paradox smiled at the fact that his entire set of words were ignored except for the most important one.
"I am looking for someone whose existence is currently surrounded by the designation of THE Tongue Whisperer.
He should have a flicker of the signature of The First Tongue burning brightly around him."
The entity opposite to THE Primordial Paradox simply nodded at these words as he turned around, apparently ready to begin the search without any further discussion.
The frozen proto-matter remained still around him, held in stasis by his mere presence.
THE Primordial Paradox continued to look at him with curiosity that he didn’t bother to hide, and he couldn’t help but ask the question that pressed against his mind.
"Who are you, really?"

At these words, the figure of Jokul turned around and looked at THE Primordial Paradox with extremely calm eyes that held depths which even someone who had existed since before THE Infinite Unfurling couldn’t fully perceive.
"You have been calling my name this entire time."
His voice was flat, stating fact rather than expressing emotion.
"Jokul.
Jokul Anaximander."
He paused, and the inverted mountain behind him seemed to grow larger for just a moment.
"But call me Jack.
To you, I am simply a friend of THE Creature.
Nothing more and nothing less."
His ancient eyes held no deception because there was nothing to deceive about, only the truth of what he was willing to share and the silence of everything he wasn’t.
"And as for the one that you lost..."

The frozen proto-matter in the surroundings began to churn and pulse with a heart-shaking brilliance that emanated from Jokul himself, his stillness somehow becoming motion without ever actually moving.
The inverted mountain behind him blazed with light that was also darkness, with cold that was also presence.
"I know where THE Tongue Whisperer is."
WAA!
He said these words as if they were an affirmation or something that he was uttering to then be true.
The proto-matter responded by revealing pathways that hadn’t existed before, frozen currents that pointed toward a specific direction in a place where direction shouldn’t have been possible.
But an instant later, his eyes shone with piercing light as he nodded his head with what might have been interest.
"It seems like it will take some time, as an Undivided One is hunting him."
He paused.
"But I have found him.
Let us go."
An Undivided One was hunting him?
Now THE Primordial Paradox was entirely surprised.
The proto-matter around them seemed to darken in response to his sudden concern.
"An Undivided One is hunting him and he has not been undifferentiated or collapsed?"
Was THE Youngest so fearsome when he hadn’t even become an Absolute yet?
THE Primordial Paradox had brought THE Youngest here expecting challenges, yes, but he had also expected to be present to help navigate those challenges.
For someone of Fundamental Depth to survive being hunted by an Undivided One, even for a short time, was unprecedented.
The visage of Jokul turned toward THE Primordial Paradox with a calm gaze that held neither concern nor reassurance.
"We can wait a little bit more for THE Formless Terrors or more Undivided Ones to find him, or for him to land in the gazes of THE Primordial Architects."
His voice was utterly flat.
"Then he will really be undifferentiated or collapsed.
He will die.
Shall we wait?"
THE Primordial Paradox looked at the deadpan expression of Jokul as his sharp eyes flashed with irritation.
The proto-matter around them seemed to hold its breath, waiting for his response.
He took a step to appear beside this being, his obsidian form closing the distance instantaneously.
"Well, all of us will one day die, but...why say such horror-inducing things?"
His voice was serious.
"Let us go.
I cannot afford to lose this one."

With such words, the visage of Jokul turned toward another direction entirely, one that the frozen pathways in the proto-matter hadn’t indicated, and disappeared into the churning expanse with movement that wasn’t movement.
His voice echoed out across the undefined space with weight that pressed against everything it touched.
"Keep up."

THE Primordial Paradox followed, his obsidian form cutting through the proto-matter as he pursued this enigmatic being called Jokul Anaximander, or really, Jack, toward THE Youngest who was somehow surviving being hunted by an Undivided One!

chapters.title: Chapter 4869: Infinite I
paragraphs: The proto-matter storm calmed around him as he appeared in an entirely different place.

Noah frowned as he looked around, his blue-gold form tense and ready for violence, almost as if he was expecting another monstrous thing to erupt at any moment and attempt to consume him. His eyes scanned the churning expanse with wariness that had been earned through far too many encounters where peace turned to peril in the span of a heartbeat.
That seemed to be his hardship and adversity across Existence, as he couldn’t even get a fucking moment to breathe.
But...

He only saw the forming and unforming landscapes of reality all around him, seas of proto-matter covering the nearby regions in waves of undefined potential that rose and fell without ever committing to any particular shape. Mountains that were also valleys. Rivers that were also skies. Ground that was also nothing at all.
No Undivided Ones hunting him.
No Formless Terrors seeking to drag him into their undefined existence.
No beams of annihilation or tentacles with jaws or million-eyed horrors screeching for a taste.
But Noah did not relax.

Instead, he released Absolute Seals of Darkness, Chaos, and Paradox that instantly bloomed around his form in swirling patterns that expanded outward with the infinity that now defined them. The seals multiplied endlessly as they reacted to the proto-matter surrounding him, their edges blurring as they took on the qualities of this place.
Moments later, everything transformed.

The seals became proto-matter themselves, as if they had undergone complete undifferentiation while somehow retaining their protective function. They wrapped around Noah’s existence and merged with the churning expanse until the distinction between his defenses and the environment became impossible to perceive.
When the storm of transformation calmed, Noah was nowhere to be seen.
But he was right there, mixed in with the calm movements of proto-matter.
Hidden in plain sight within a place where sight itself hadn’t fully differentiated.
In such a state of concealed existence, he finally turned his attention inward and breathed.
Just what had happened to him, really? The changes he had undergone since being separated from THE Primordial Paradox were so profound that he needed time to actually process them.
Time he hadn’t been given until now.
|Infinity Integration: Complete Existential Analysis|

|The core aspect of your existence was already infinite before entering THE Prima Indifferentia. Proto-matter attempted to undifferentiate it and failed because infinity cannot be made less than infinite. Instead of being eroded, your core aspect became the template that all other aspects of your existence are now being restructured to mirror.|
|This process is ongoing and will continue until full integration is achieved.|
The prompts flowed through his consciousness with weight, each piece of information landing with significance that demanded attention.

|THE Grimoire of Infinite Lexicons- Previous State: A repository of linguistic authority containing all acquired Phonemes, Logos, Philologies, and Archai. Current State: The Grimoire now containsinfinite pages, with each Phoneme existing in infinite variations and each Logos expressible in infinite permutations.|

|Each Philology and Archai can be structured in infinite arrangements that you have not yet explored. The Grimoire no longer merely stores The First Tongue but generates linguistic authority passively, with new combinations of existing Phonemes forming automatically within its infinite pages.|
|You will need to review these combinations when time permits. Some may be useful, some may be dangerous, and all of them are yours to claim or discard as you see fit.|

Noah felt THE Grimoire of Infinite Lexicons pulsing within his existence, its pages turning endlessly through combinations that his conscious mind couldn’t track. It was generating authority on its own now, creating linguistic structures that might take eons to fully catalogue!

|THE Organ of Civilization - Previous State: The core structure housing the authority of your Civilization and its derivatives. Current State: The Organ now pulses with infinite rhythm, its capacity for Derivative Civilizations no longer limited by conventional constraints.|

|The Organ can theoretically support infinite derivatives simultaneously, but the constraint has shifted from quantity to quality. You can have as many Derivative Civilizations as you desire, but each must still be cultivated through genuine development. Infinity provides space, but it does not provide substance, and that remains your responsibility.|

|Additionally, inside THE Organ of Civilization, THE Infinite Desmoterion has been bathed with a light of infinity. The prisoners held within are undergoing unknown alterations and mutations that your other self, Ozymandias, is currently overseeing and guiding in real-time and dilated time.|
The implications of that last prompt were heavy, but Noah filed them away for later consideration.

|27 Seals of Absolute Tongue - Previous State: 27 distinct Seals representing your mastery over The First Tongue. Current State: Each Seal is now infinitely reproducible, with throwing one Seal manifesting infinite Seals in response.|

|The number 27 remains significant as the base configuration, but each of the 27 can multiply without limit upon release. Additionally, your Seals now carry three distinct qualities that transform them from mere representations of authority into weapons of existential significance.|

|Quality One: Infinite durability through endless replacement. Quality Two: Infinite Hunger absorption from Derivative Civilization integration. Quality Three: Undifferentiation induction from Infinite Undifferentiated Fate integration. Your Seals have become both shield and weapon, both defense and consumption, both definition and undefinition.|

He had already witnessed those qualities in action against Bazuman, watching his seals devour and undifferentiate the attacks of an Undivided One. They had bought him time that shouldn’t have been possible to purchase.
But then the prompts reached something that made him pause.

|Depth and Immensity - Infinity seeks to permeate across your Depth, but the integration appears to be missing a critical component. The change required is too significant for passive integration alone.Active application of a catalyst is required to complete the transformation.|
Noah paused at these prompts.

Everything was getting bathed with a light of infinity, his Grimoire and his Organ and his Seals all transforming to reflect the boundless nature of his core aspect. But his Depth had not fully taken that step, as it seemed to be missing something that passive integration couldn’t provide.
And he felt like he knew exactly what was missing.

At this time, he turned his gaze to his Organ of Civilization where an unfathomably bright singularity of blue-gold light spun in lemniscate formations that twisted through dimensions that shouldn’t have existed within his existence. The light was hypnotic and terrifying and beautiful all at once, a resource of such profound significance that even looking at it directly made his foundations ache.
He was looking at his Infinite Everything.

chapters.title: Chapter 4870: Infinite II
paragraphs: |Infinite Everything - Classification and Application Parameters|

|An Infinite Everything can be applied to most resources, most authorities, and nearly all aspects of one’s Civilization. Upon application, that resource becomes infinite in quantity while retaining its original quality, transforming limited potential into boundless actuality.|

|The limitation is singular and absolute: an Infinite Everything can only be applied once. Once used, it cannot be recovered, cannot be replicated, and cannot be undone. The choice of application determines the trajectory of one’s existence for all time that follows.|

|Choose what becomes infinite with extreme care. The wrong choice creates infinite mediocrity, an endless supply of something that doesn’t matter. The right choice creates infinite transcendence, a foundation for growth that has no ceiling and no end.|

The definition was straightforward for the most part, but Noah also felt like something immense was missing from his understanding. The Infinite Everything spun within his Organ of Civilization with weight that pressed against his perception, demanding to be used while also warning him of the permanence of that use.

But while Noah felt the Immensity of his existence and his Depth, which was having a hard time taking the aspect of infinity through passive integration alone, he knew exactly where this Infinite Everything needed to go.
There was only one choice that made sense.

His thoughts were silent as they imposed themselves onto his existence, and a moment later he felt his newly born Infinite Everything surge toward the target he had selected. The area of THE Prima Indifferentia that had calmed around him with undifferentiated proto-matter instantly released a flash of blue-gold light that stretched out across the edges of perception, painting the undefined expanse in colors that shouldn’t have existed here.
BOOM!
He felt like something within him had broken.

Not broken in the sense of damage, but broken in the sense of liberation. A ceiling that would have always remained there, a glass container that would have forever limited how high he could build, shattered into fragments of conceptual constraint that dissolved into his foundations and disappeared.
|Infinite Everything Application Confirmed|
|Target: THE Formless Depth of your existence|
HUUM!
Immensity bloomed.
Gloru unfolded as his existence felt squeezed and then let free!

|Your Depth transforms to become THE Infinite Formless Depth.There is no longer any theoretical ceiling to your foundation at any level of existence. The constraints that would have limited your growth have been permanently removed.|

|THE Surface Depth, which was approaching the theoretical limit of 1000% comparative weight to THE Primordial Paradox at equivalent stage, no longer has this ceiling. It can be increased infinitely. THE Intermediate Depth, which was approaching the theoretical limit of 1000% comparative weight, no longer has this ceiling. It can be increased infinitely.|

|Your Fundamental Depth can be increased infinitely without ever reaching a point where further growth becomes impossible. Your Absolute Depth, when you eventually attain it, can have its foundation increased infinitely as well. The Vakochev Scales of Existence will need to be navigated regardless, but the weight you bring to those Scales has no upper bound.|

|While it may become more and more arduous to scale upward as the numbers grow larger, there is no theoretical ceiling to prevent continued growth. Hypothetically, you could continue elevating the weight of your Surface, Intermediate, and Fundamental Depths to become so grand that you could stand against Absolutes without ever fully grasping that designation yourself.|
|You have not become an Absolute. You have become something with the potential to exceed Absolutes while remaining at lower Depths. This configuration has no precedent in Observable Existence.|

|Additionally, the aspect of Infinity has now fully permeated your Depth. The integration that was stalled has been completed through active application of the Infinite Everything.All aspects of your existence now burn with the light of boundlessness.|
Utter majesty bloomed within Noah as he felt a sense of exuberance that transcended mere emotion.

Inside of his existence, the parts where it had felt like a ceiling existed, the invisible barriers that would have eventually stopped his growth, were now filled with Infinite Potential instead. There were no walls. No limits.
No points where someone could say "this far and no further" because infinity recognized no such constraints.
And for all his efforts, there were grand harvests being made.

Infinity wrapped around Perpetual Harvest and Cheating Architect as well, enhancing these aspects of his existence that had always been responsible for his accelerated growth. Currently, they were drawing in proto-matter from THE Prima Indifferentia and its undifferentiated quality, and proceeding to change it into differentiated harvest that steadily flowed into his foundations at rates that made his previous gains look like trickles compared to rivers.
He was becoming heavier and grander with every passing second throughout all his foundations.
Surface Depth growing.
Intermediate Depth growing.
Fundamental Depth growing!
All of it expanding without any ceiling to eventually halt the expansion.

It was surreal to see this as a result of his current temporal traversal, a journey that had begun with hiding a piece of THE Primordial Paradox and had transformed into something that reshaped the fundamental nature of his existence.
But one thing became abundantly clear as he floated within the concealment of undifferentiated proto-matter and felt his foundations expanding in real-time.
It looked like he would be building his foundation for a very, very long time.
Now, he basically had all the blueprints to infinite growth and Immensity.

What he had to do now was continue to flood his existence with infinite potential and resources that would continue to scale upward without any theoretical ceiling to halt his progress. Since there was no upper limit anymore, he could continue to pour resources into his weight and Immensity until he reached levels that rivaled or exceeded beings who had spent eons building their foundations.
But of course, even more resources were required the higher up he went.

The law of diminishing returns applied, with each subsequent increase demanding more investment than the last. Going from 100% to 200% comparative weight might require a certain amount of resources, but going from 200% to 300% would require even more, and the progression would continue to steepen as he climbed higher and higher into territory that had never been explored by someone at his Depth.

Absolutes were resources that were tasty and grand, and collapsing them through combat or through methods like the Rite of Paradoxical Inheritance had provided significant boosts to his foundations. But THE Prima Indifferentia should also hold unfathomable resources as just being here alone allowed him to take in and process proto-matter that was being turned into infinite potential, continuously and steadily pumped into his foundation through Perpetual Harvest and Cheating Architect.
He was growing passively simply by existing in this place.
But if he was to increase his weight and Immensity to be capable of getting close to those who had obtained the level of an Absolute, he had to do more than rely on passive growth!

chapters.title: Chapter 4871: The Evolutionary Dead End
paragraphs: THE Primordial Paradox had said there were boundless resources and treasures here, materials of incalculable value that could accelerate progression in ways that normal cultivation could never achieve.
Spark Fragments containing echoes of THE First Cause.
Contradiction Cores embodying paradoxes from before Paradox itself differentiated.
Pure Possibility granting access to Chaos in its most fundamental state.
All of these things existed somewhere in THE Prima Indifferentia, waiting to be claimed by those with the strength and fortune to find them.
"Oh, THE Primordial Paradox..."

In that invisible state of concealment within the proto-matter, Noah remembered the ancient Absolute and thought about where he might be right now. He had been separated from THE Primordial Paradox when the storms of proto-matter had reacted to his presence and swept him away, and he had no idea how much time had passed since then or how far he had traveled.

He didn’t have to worry about the safety of such a terrifying being as much as he had to worry about his own, given that THE Primordial Paradox was one of THE Four and had survived in THE Prima Indifferentia before. But Noah also couldn’t say for sure that he had lost the trail of that terrifying Undivided One, Bazuman, whose million crimson eyes had shown such interest in prey that could fight back.

For now, until he was potentially forced to end this temporal traversal early by having his body collapsed, he had to see what other opportunities were available in this region. Every moment he spent here was a moment of growth, but every moment was also a moment of danger.
And for him right now, it was actually easier to navigate the idea of looking for treasures and resources than it would have been for anyone else in Observable Existence.
Because at this moment, he held Infinite Undifferentiated Fate.

In this unique state of existence where his connection to destiny had become paradoxical and boundless, he pulled upon that Derivative Civilization with focused intent. A silent golden light emerged from his concealed form and spread out across the waves and seas of proto-matter like ripples in a pond, except these ripples carried the weight of fate itself seeking answers to questions he had yet to ask.
|Derivative Civilization of Infinite Undifferentiated Fate - Active Manifestation|

|The Derivative Civilization of Infinite Undifferentiated Fate exerts its Way across the surrounding existence. What is fated and destined are now infinitely amplified and capable of being chosen by the one wielding this Way, turning destiny from something that happens to you into something you actively shape and direct.|

|Your connection to fate has begun permeating across the surrounding regions of THE Prima Indifferentia. Destiny is not something that others make for you here, as you are infinitely making your own choices that inform different fates and different outcomes. The possibilities are endless, and you are selecting which possibilities become reality.|

|The fates of resources and treasures are being sought through this manifestation. Your existence has found potential links to three different directions from your current position, with each direction highlighted according to the proposed level of danger that accompanies the potential reward.|
|Direction One: Crimson designation indicating extreme danger. Potential reward: significant but path is guarded by forces that exceed current combat capability.|
|Direction Two: Crimson designation indicating extreme danger. Potential reward: significant but path is guarded by forces that exceed current combat capability.|

|Direction Three: Orange designation indicating high danger but potentially manageable. Potential reward: moderate to significant, with path containing hazards that fall within survivable parameters if approached with caution.|

Noah saw faint lines of golden light stretching out in three separate directions from where he currently was, the threads of fate made visible through his Derivative Civilization’s influence on the surrounding proto-matter.
Two of them were surrounded with a deep hue of crimson light that pulsed with warning, the color of blood and danger and almost certain death.
Only a single one shone bright orange.

The two shining with crimson light emanated a great level of danger for him, the kind of danger that even his newly infinite existence might not be able to survive. Perhaps Undivided Ones guarded those paths. Perhaps Formless Terrors lurked along their routes.

The one pulsing with orange light seemed to be potentially manageable but still very dangerous, the kind of danger that would test him without necessarily destroying him. The kind of hardship that Vakochev demanded for progression rather than the kind that simply ended existence.
But...
Everything in Existence was dangerous.
Hardship and adversity were a must for growth, weren’t they?

THE Primordial Paradox had said it himself when discussing the Vakochev Scales: if one’s foundation hadn’t weathered through waves of Immensity and hardship, if one’s Way hadn’t been established through genuine adversity, then the doorway to the second Scale would remain uncrossable regardless of how powerful one became.

So while feeling the immense growth and Immensity of his existence expanding with every passing moment, and seeking to grow it even more while he had the opportunity in this place, Noah began to move once more.
He took a step toward the orange-designated path.

And even though he did so, what actually moved was a swirling storm of proto-matter that concealed his existence within its undefined currents. The storm shot forward at speeds that made the proto-matter around it blur and distort, covering distances that should have taken considerable time in mere moments.
His speed was approaching the speed of his very good boy, Skoll.
His speed was approaching the speed of an Absolute.
He had grown so much in such a short time, and he was just getting started.

As he moved silently through THE Prima Indifferentia, his concealment holding even at these tremendous velocities, Noah thought about the words of THE Primordial Paradox and this place as potentially the origin of THE Entity.

The one thing that stuck with him was what THE Primordial Paradox had said about THE Formless Terrors and THE Undivided Ones, the entities that represented the greatest dangers within this undifferentiated expanse.

THE Formless Terrors especially haunted his thoughts, because they had lost all definition of their existence and now moved around seeking to attack anything that possessed definition. They wanted to make others like themselves, to drag differentiated beings down into the formless state they had been trapped in.
And the words that THE Primordial Paradox had spoken resonated with something he had heard before.
THE Primordial Paradox had said exactly:
"It is not malice. It is something more fundamental than malice. It is the natural behaviour of undifferentiated existence encountering differentiated existence."
It was not malice.

When THE Secretive Eon had talked with him, she had mentioned how she, or they, were not doing anything overly malicious. They were simply returning things to their truest nature, helping existence achieve a state that they believed was more fundamental and more pure. And the more that others joined them, the less conflict there would be, as they would collectively focus on moving across the Scales of Existence together.
THE Secretive Eon had been confident that the second Scale would be achieved rather rapidly once enough of Observable Existence had been unified under THE Entity’s influence.
The philosophy was almost seductive in its simplicity.
Join us. Become one with us. Stop fighting and start ascending together.
But now, with what Noah had just learned from THE Primordial Paradox, a fundamental flaw in that philosophy became abundantly clear.
The Vakochev Scales of Existence demanded hardship for progression.
They demanded adversity and conflict.
They demanded that foundations be built through genuine struggle.

So THE Entity seeking to infect everyone and have all of Existence collectively move toward the goal of elevation might truly be an evolutionary dead end. For those who had been unified under THE Entity’s influence, there would be no genuine adversity because they would all be working toward the same goal without opposition. There would be no hardship because hardship required something to struggle against, and when everyone was the same, struggle became meaningless.
THE Secretive Eon had spoken of ascending together.
But The Scales of Existence didn’t care about collective ascension.
The Scales of Existence cared about individual hardship woven into individual foundations.
The actions of THE Entity, if successful, would actually halt all progression across Observable Existence.
No one would reach the second Scale.
No one would advance beyond where they currently were.
Everyone would be unified, yes, but unified in stagnation rather than growth.

The thought was a heavy and deadly one as Noah moved across THE Prima Indifferentia, following the lead of his Derivative Civilization toward what should be a resource or treasure that also held a level of danger.
THE Entity might not even know about this flaw in its philosophy.
Or perhaps it did know and didn’t care.

Or perhaps the goal was never actually ascension but something else entirely, something that used the promise of collective growth as a lure while the true purpose remained hidden behind layers of infection!

chapters.title: Chapter 4872: Existence Is! I
paragraphs: Across eons of time.
Far from the weavings of THE Infinite Unfurling in a past that Noah was currently experiencing.
In the current era after THE Fallout.
In Alfheimr.

An unknown number of light years from the region where Noah had held an illusory consciousness meeting with THE Primordial Chaos, far from where THE Living Elemental and THE Living Emotive had met him and clashed with words that carried the weight of civilizations, there existed an abode that was sacred to the lifeforms of this Primordial Realm.

It sat atop a mountain peak that rose from clouds of luminescent mist, the summit reaching toward skies that burned with the twilight of Alfheimr. The mountain itself was ancient beyond measure, its slopes covered with forests of trees that had witnessed the differentiation of Observable Existence and continued to witness everything that came after.
At the peak stood a simple multicolored stone temple.

Not grand in the way that palaces were grand. Not imposing in the way that fortresses were imposing. It was simple in the way that truly sacred things were simple, its architecture speaking of purpose rather than ostentation. The stones that formed its walls held every color that light could produce, shifting and changing as the twilight touched them from different angles, and the air around it carried a weight that pressed against any existence that approached.
This was a place where THE Creature had once walked.
The figures of THE Living Origin and THE First Hunger appeared at the foot of the temple, their forms manifesting from spatial distortions.

Origin looked up at the temple with eyes that held memories stretching back to before The Earliest Folds, before her collapse, before everything had changed. Her milky white form seemed almost fragile in this moment despite the power she now held, her expression complex with emotions that she rarely allowed others to see.
She turned to Hunger.
"Can you wait for me down here?"
Her voice was soft, almost hesitant.
"I just... I need a moment. When I come down, I will have my answer."
She paused, her eyes meeting his.
"And you will have yours."

Her expression was complex as Hunger heard this and stayed still, his eyes heavy with understanding. His dark hair flowed past his shoulders, stirred by winds that carried the weight of Alfheimr’s twilight, and his crimson eyes held a light of defiance that never truly faded regardless of the circumstances.
Lesser beings would not ever think about competing against THE Creature for anything, let alone for the affection of one who had given THE Creature her Everything.
But not Hunger.
The light of all Inevitabilities burned within him as he sat down on the stone steps leading up to the temple, his posture relaxed but his attention sharp. He would wait. He would be patient!
And when Origin came down from that mountain, whatever answer she carried would determine everything that came next.
Origin went up the temple.

Her steps were light and measured as she continued up the ancient stones, her gaze reflecting memories of times when she had climbed these same steps with hope. She remembered when THE Creature had been everything to her. She remembered when his presence had been enough to make existence feel meaningful.
She remembered when she had given him her Everything, and he had accepted it without telling her what that acceptance would truly cost.

She continued until she entered the temple fully, passing through the simple archway into an interior that held no decorations, no ornaments, no displays of power. Just empty space and the weight of presence that had accumulated across eons of beings coming here to seek audience with THE Creature.
She came to stand close to the temple’s center, and there she saw it.
A white mat.

Not a grand throne or anything unfathomable that would befit one of THE Four. Just an empty mat where visitors would kneel, simple and unassuming in a way that almost seemed like mockery given the power of the being who would appear before it.
But Origin did not kneel.

She calmly proceeded to sit opposite to this mat, her legs folded beneath her and her back straight with dignity that refused to bow. Her expression seemed made up, her decision already finalized before she had even begun climbing those temple steps.
"I demand an answer."
BOOM!

Four words, but they were so heavy that the air itself seemed to compress around them. Before she even finished saying them, the area around the mat in front of her fluctuated with distortions that bent light and space simultaneously, and the illusory visage of an entity shrouded in multicolored flames appeared.
THE Creature!

His face could barely be observed as it was surrounded by multicolored flames that burned with every color that existence could produce, fires that didn’t consume but simply were. But one could see eyes of immensity and calmness looking out from within those flames, eyes that held depths which even Absolutes couldn’t fully perceive.
Eyes that looked at Origin with something that might have been regret.
Origin’s body trembled lightly as she looked at THE Creature, biting her lips as she heard his voice for what seemed like forever.
"I am sorry."
BOOM!
She had come demanding an answer, and the first thing she was told was this.

Two words that she had never expected to hear from someone who embodied Existence itself. Two words that confirmed everything she had feared and suspected since regaining consciousness after her collapse.

Her face paled and turned ashen as anger flashed in her eyes, bright and hot and barely contained! She looked defiantly at THE Creature with an expression that held none of the reverence that had once defined her interactions with him.
"I gave you my Everything."
Her voice trembled with emotion that she couldn’t fully suppress.
"The least I expected from you was honesty. I do not even care that I was collapsed. I just..."
She paused, gathering herself.

"It would have been nice to have had a level of honesty. To be looked at as a peer and not as someone lesser. You never told me what was really going on. You never looked at me as anything worth sharing your grand plans with."
BOOM!

She was venting out all her frustrations at this time, years of suppressed anger finally finding release in the presence of the one who had caused them. Her milky white form flickered with agitation that made the temple’s multicolored stones pulse in sympathy.
THE Creature took everything in without interruption, his multicolored flames burning steadily as he listened to accusations.
"I am not a perfect being."
His voice was booming yet calm, carrying the weight of Existence itself even as it acknowledged failure.
"Far from it. I make mistakes, and I made many mistakes that I can blame on the nature of my Existence. Existence is. Existence was. I became...too attuned with it."
The flames around him shifted through colors that spoke of memory and regret.
"I let things flow as they should without intervening when I should. As much as I can blame my nature on this, it was still my choice."
He paused.
"This was unfair to you, so I apologize."
