chapters.title: Chapter 4873: Existence Is! II
paragraphs: The words were unfathomably calm, and Origin found herself searching within them for emotion that matched her own. She wanted to see pain. She wanted to see remorse that burned as hot as her anger. She wanted to know that her suffering had meant something to him beyond mere acknowledgment!
But she couldn’t find it.
Not the emotion she wanted, anyway.

THE Creature’s apology was sincere, but it was also the apology of a being who existed on a level where individual suffering, no matter how profound, was just one thread in an infinite weaving. He meant his words, but he couldn’t feel them the way she needed him to feel them.
She breathed out and controlled her existence, forcing the trembling of her form to still as she asked the question that had haunted her since her reconstruction.
"Why did you allow me to be collapsed?"
Her voice was steadier now, colder.

"The more I think of it, the more I can see that Paradox shouldn’t have had the power he had. Even if he supposedly took your heart by using Anaximander, even if you were chained, you are powerful. You were powerful."
Her eyes narrowed.
"So really, why...did I have to be collapsed? Why did you allow it?"
There were many whys she wanted to ask, but this was the critical one. This was the question that would determine whether anything between them could ever be salvaged.

THE Creature looked at her with a gaze that truly wanted to portray how he felt, the multicolored flames parting slightly as if to allow her to see more of his expression. What she saw there was not cruelty. What she saw there was not indifference.
What she saw there was the certainty of someone who had made calculations that others couldn’t understand.
"At that time, I mistakenly believed that it was all...for the sake of adversity."
BOOM!
As he said this, his finger tapped out in a gesture that was almost casual, and in the next moment the aura around THE Living Origin exploded with power that she hadn’t fully realized she possessed.

While she was sitting down, milky white light erupted from her existence as an aura of Absolute radiated outward with intensity that made the temple’s stones tremble. A heavy aura filled with Immensity that spoke of foundations forged through genuine hardship, through genuine suffering, through genuine loss.
And it continued rising.
The power climbed nonsensically higher, revealing depths to her foundation that THE Creature’s gesture had unlocked or perhaps simply revealed with a tap!
From Half-Step Absolute to Absolute with a tap!
But even as she felt this Immensity, her eyes were those of anger as she wanted to rebuke THE Creature.
For adversity?
For adversity?!
"One of the many mistales I made. I should have communicated with you more clearly on it."
THE Creature’s voice remained calm despite her obvious rage.

"I should not have been passive. But the hardship you and many others went through forged a grand foundation for your existences. It made Absolute possible for beings who might otherwise have never reached it."
His multicolored flames pulsed with something that might have been pride in what she had become.
"And it altered your existences to allow THE Second Scale of Existence to be possible for many."
BOOM!

The words caused Origin to become even more ashen as her eyes grew cold with understanding that she didn’t want to have. The implications of what THE Creature was saying pressed against her mind with weight that threatened to crush everything she thought she knew about her own existence.
She looked at THE Creature with eyes that held ice rather than fire.
"THE Loom. THE Fallout. THE Living Paradox."
Her voice was quiet now, dangerously quiet.
"If you wanted, could you have stopped all of it?"
The question was a terrifying one, and the silence that followed was even more terrifying.
THE Creature did not answer.
And this alone caused the eyes of Origin to flash with Immensity as she understood that this non-answer was its own answer.
He could have stopped it! He could have prevented THE Fallout from ever occurring. He could have prevented the devastation that had reshaped Observable Existence!
But he had chosen not to.
For the sake of adversity.
"Haha..."
She couldn’t help but laugh, the sound hollow and bitter in the sacred space of the temple.

"Right. You are THE Creature. The entity that seemed so otherworldly and strong. I always found myself questioning how you could have been defeated by THE Living Paradox, how you could have been chained and had your heart stolen."
Her laughter died, replaced by a smile that held no warmth.
"It turned out you were playing games that us lesser minds didn’t even deserve to know about. How grand. How majestic you are, O Creature!"

Her words turned biting at the end as she rose from her seated position, her chest heaving with anger that she no longer tried to suppress. The Civilizational Authority around her trembled with agitation that made the temple’s multicolored stones flicker wildly, responding to her emotional state.
She looked straight into the eyes of THE Creature.

THE Creature looked back, and within the eyes of this entity shrouded by multicolored flames, there was a sense of true apology that went deeper than his earlier words had conveyed. He understood her anger. He accepted it as deserved. And yet he couldn’t fully regret his choices because those choices had led to outcomes that served purposes she couldn’t yet comprehend.
"Many things were done wrong, Ljósmóðir."
He used her ancient name, the name she had held before becoming THE Living Origin, and the familiarity of it made her chest tighten.
"We all live and learn. The ends do not always justify the means. I am trying to do things differently."
His voice, even though still grand, was earnest in a way that she hadn’t heard from him in eons.
"But know that what I did, while for myself, was also for you and many others."

Origin listened to his words as her chest stopped heaving, the anger slowly settling into something colder and more permanent. She smiled brilliantly, but the smile didn’t reach her eyes as she turned around from THE Creature.
"Did you get what you wanted?"
She asked this question without looking back at him.
"Do you have your Second Scale of Existence under your grand thumb?"

She wanted to see pain.
She wanted to see remorse that burned as hot as her anger.

But she couldn’t find it.
Not the emotion she wanted, anyway.
THE Creature’s apology was sincere, but it was also the apology of a being who existed on a level where individual suffering, no matter how profound, was just one thread in an infinite weaving.
He meant his words, but he couldn’t feel them the way she needed him to feel them.
She breathed out and controlled her existence, forcing the trembling of her form to still as she asked the question that had haunted her since her reconstruction.
"Why did you allow me to be collapsed?"
Her voice was steadier now, colder.
"The more I think of it, the more I can see that Paradox shouldn’t have had the power he had.

Her eyes narrowed.
"So really, why...did I have to be collapsed?
Why did you allow it?"

The power climbed nonsensically higher, revealing depths to her foundation that THE Creature’s gesture had unlocked or perhaps simply revealed with a tap!
From Half-Step Absolute to Absolute with a tap!

For adversity?!

BOOM!
The words caused Origin to become even more ashen as her eyes grew cold with understanding that she didn’t want to have.

chapters.title: Chapter 4874: Existence Is! III
paragraphs: This time around as well, THE Creature did not reply.
That also should have been its own answer.
Origin smiled at this non-answer as she began to walk away from the temple, her steps light despite the weight of everything that had been said.
"I am happy for you. I really am."
Her voice carried no happiness at all.
"I wish you the best, O Creature."
BOOM!
With such words, she walked away and did not look back.

The multicolored flames around THE Creature pulsed faintly as he looked out from the temple, watching her descend the steps toward where THE First Hunger waited. His eyes were filled with unknown Immensities and wonder, contemplating paths that only he could see and outcomes that only he could understand.
He had lost something today.
Whether that loss was worth what he had gained remained to be seen.

Origin left the temple with light steps, her form descending the ancient stones with grace that belied the emotional weight she had been carrying. Even though her body radiated terrifying waves of Absolute power that made the very air around her tremble with respect, her eyes felt light and her breathing felt free.
As if she had released a heavy weight that had been pressing against her shoulders since the moment she had been reconstructed.

She reached the bottom of the steps where she had left Hunger, and she found him exactly where she had asked him to wait. His dark hair still flowed past his shoulders. His crimson eyes still burned with the light of all Inevitabilities. His posture was still relaxed but attentive, ready for whatever came next.
He rose as she approached.
She reached out toward THE First Hunger, offering her hand.
He took it.

His fingers wrapped around hers with warmth that THE Creature’s apologies had lacked, with presence that felt immediate and real rather than distant and calculating. She had been given her answer by THE Creature, and in this gesture, in this offered hand, she gave her answer to Hunger.
THE First Hunger turned to stare at the distant visage of THE Creature still visible within the temple, his crimson eyes holding a murky gaze that contained depths of emotion he rarely displayed.
Then he pulled gently on her hand, and the two of them began to walk down the mountain together.
Not once had he believed he would lose against THE Creature.
Not once had he doubted that his patience would be rewarded.
And so far, it seemed like at least at this time, THE First Hunger had won.
He walked down a mountain holding the hand of an Absolute, and the twilight of Alfheimr seemed to burn brighter around them as they descended.
Far from Alfheimr.

In a region that could be considered within the spaces between spaces, where the boundaries of Observable Existence grew thin and the rules that governed reality became suggestions rather than laws, the figure of THE Creature was situated back to back with the figure of Anaximander.

The two of them floated in void that wasn’t quite void, surrounded by currents of authority that flowed from THE Creature’s multicolored flames like rivers of pure being. Anaximander’s scholarly robes drifted in winds that had no source, his ancient eyes contemplating equations and theories that only he could perceive.
They had been here for some time.
Immense waves of Existence were spinning around them in patterns, and at this moment, between THE Creature and Anaximander, a flash of colorless light shone and erupted far above them.
The light climbed higher and higher until it reached a point where space itself seemed to object to its presence, and then it carved outward with force that made both beings look up with attention.
An unimaginable crack formed in the fabric of reality.
A Crack of Observable Existence.
It was a rare and impossible thing to find as only a few places had it, but what was impossible for THE Creature?

The moment this crack formed, Anaximander looked up with marvel and curiosity that burned brighter than any scientific discovery he had ever made. His ancient eyes studied the fracture with the intensity of someone who had dedicated eons to understanding the nature of reality, and he couldn’t help but ask THE Creature what he was witnessing.
"What is this?"

THE Creature looked up at the crack with eyes that held knowledge stretching back to before THE Infinite Unfurling, his multicolored flames pulsing with rhythms that seemed to sync with the crack’s formation.
"It would be much easier to explain in a few seconds."
The moment his words were done, the Crack of Observable Existence above them opened fully.

From within that crack, a storm of proto-matter instantly surged out like a pillar of undefined potential, descending with purpose that transcended random occurrence. The storm didn’t spread across the space between spaces. It didn’t dissipate into the void around them.
It landed directly onto the figure of Anaximander.

The proto-matter covered his existence entirely, wrapping around his scholarly form with churning chaos that should have undifferentiated anything it touched. But Anaximander didn’t dissolve. He didn’t blur at the edges. Instead, while surrounded by the storm, his eyes burned with curiosity that held no fear as he raised his hand and twirled strands of proto-matter between his fingers.
He was familiar with this substance.
He was comfortable with its presence.

The storm pulsed once, twice, and then shockingly entered his body as if returning to a home it had been separated from for far too long. Anaximander began to tremble as an unfathomable Immensity was released from within him, power that had been dormant awakening with force that made THE Creature’s multicolored flames flicker in response.
Instantly, in this entire region, everything froze over.
Not frozen in the sense of ice, but frozen in the sense of absolute stillness. The currents of authority stopped flowing. The void stopped being void. Everything achieved a state of stasis!

Anaximander looked like he had a dazed expression as the storm died down around him, waves of proto-matter flowing serenely across his figure like loyal attendants welcoming a returning master. But his expression didn’t show triumph or satisfaction.
It showed a sense of loss.
Almost as if he did not want this.
Almost as if the memories now flooding back into his existence were memories he had been happy to forget.
Yet THE Creature looked down toward him with eyes that held ancient knowing, his multicolored flames burning with warmth that seemed almost paternal.
"Hello, Jack. It has been quite some time."

chapters.title: Chapter 4875: Last Gamble! I
paragraphs: Jack.
Jokul.

These names felt foreign in Anaximander’s mind, labels that belonged to someone else, designations that carried weight he had spent eons trying to escape. He shook his head as if he did not want them, as if he did not recognize them, as if the being they referred to was a stranger wearing his face!
THE Creature’s gaze softened at this response, understanding filling his multicolored eyes as he continued speaking with the patience of someone who had all the time in Existence.
"Your experiment in defining yourself was a grand one. You lived a life of hardship as the scientist and explorer Anaximander, without any of your memories, without any of your knowledge."
He paused, letting the words settle.
"But your existence is filled with weavings of undifferentiation. Your existence, by nature, is undefined."

At such words, Anaximander became utterly still and serious, the proto-matter around him ceasing its serene flow as his attention focused entirely on the being before him. His ancient eyes held defiance that burned brighter than the frost he had just released.
"My existence may be undefined."
His voice was steady despite the turmoil that must have been raging within him.
"But my Way, my self, it is defined. I like Anaximander. I like who I have become."
He straightened, his scholarly robes settling around him with dignity that transcended his undefined nature.
"Sometimes one has to take a step and say who they are. To define themselves and remain what they are, fully and truly."
His eyes met THE Creature’s without flinching.
"And I am an explorer. I am Anaximander."
BOOM!

As he said this, the frost in this region receded and disappeared as if acknowledging his declaration. He tapped out with authority that made space itself respond, and the Crack of Observable Existence above them shook with resonance!

Immense seas of proto-matter, more than ten times grander than before, gushed out from the crack and landed on Anaximander with force that would have annihilated lesser beings. But he absorbed it all without faltering, his existence drinking in the undefined potential while his definition remained firmly in place.
He had made a choice, like many in Existence made their choices.
To be what he wanted to be rather than what he had been born as.
To define himself rather than accept the undefined nature of his origins.

THE Creature had also made his own choices across the eons, some right and some wrong, some that he regretted and some that he stood by despite the consequences. He looked at the most recent choice of his friend with a smile that held genuine warmth.
Every choice was a path taken.
And every path was a river of endless possibilities.

As he thought of this, THE Creature couldn’t help but look out in a different direction entirely, his gaze piercing through the spaces between spaces toward destinations that only he could perceive. His booming voice echoed out as it spoke to no one in particular.
"What choice will you make?"

It was a simple question, and it was unknown whether it was aimed at THE Living Paradox who held a Claim through methods that many didn’t fully understand, or THE Secretive Eon who sought to unite all of Observable Existence, or THE Primordial Chaos who watched everything from his corner of reality, or perhaps someone else entirely that THE Creature was thinking about right now.
Eons passed and eons gone.
Far in THE Infinite Unfurling, past a Crack of Observable Existence, inside THE Prima Indifferentia.
In a region where proto-matter had taken on properties that shouldn’t have been possible even for undefined substance, an ancient creature made its home among formations that defied description.

The proto-matter here was molten, shining crimson-gold with heat that had nothing to do with temperature and everything to do with concentrated potential. It curved in millions of Mobius strips that twisted through dimensions that hadn’t fully differentiated, creating an environment of endless loops where beginning and end lost all meaning.

The ancient creature itself was something between a serpent and a concept, its form stretching across hundreds of miles while simultaneously occupying a single point in space. Scales that shifted through every possible color covered its body, and eyes that numbered in the thousands dotted its length, each one watching a different aspect of the molten landscape it called home.
It had been here since before THE Infinite Unfurling.
It would likely be here long after.
And right now, it was watching a small crimson-gold seed that spun perpetually in the middle of this place with happiness that radiated from every one of its countless eyes.

The seed was no larger than a fist, but it burned with authority that made the surrounding Mobius strips of proto-matter bend toward it in reverence. Routinely, the seed would release a flash of light that carried the quality of undifferentiation, pure potential in its most concentrated form, and the ancient creature would absorb this light as it made its existence feel that much richer.
It had enjoyed this sensation for cycles.

Sometimes, the continued sensation something brought was grander than consuming it in a single gulp. The creature had learned this lesson long ago, and so it had been content to simply bask in the seed’s emissions rather than devour it entirely.
So the creature continued to enjoy the sensation this seed granted, its countless eyes blinking with contentment that spoke of simple pleasures appreciated across unfathomable spans of time.
Unbeknownst to it...
HUUM!

A storm of proto-matter arrived nearby, settling into the molten landscape as if it belonged there. The storm had been measuring this situation for several seconds, observing the ancient creature and its treasure with attention that went beyond mere curiosity.
The storm of proto-matter was naturally Noah, and his gaze was sharp as he looked at the terrifying scene ahead of him from within his concealment.
|Environmental Analysis - High Value Target Detected|

|You are observing an ancient entity designated as a Primordial Serpent of Undifferentiated Coils. Its power should rival or exceed weaker Absolutes, though its combat methodology would be fundamentally different from differentiated beings.|
|More significantly, you are observing the object it is benefiting from.|
|Object Classification: Spark Fragment of THE First Cause|

|This is a fragment that contains mere echoes of THE First Cause that initiated differentiation, but it is a fragment nonetheless. Consuming or integrating this Spark Fragment would provide tremendous advancement to your foundations, potentially accelerating your growth by factors that cannot be accurately calculated.|
|The Primordial Serpent has been passively absorbing emissions from this Spark Fragment for eons rather than consuming it directly.|
|You could potentially integrate it where the Serpent could not.|
|However, acquiring it would require either defeating the Serpent or stealing the Fragment without detection.|
|Neither option carries favorable odds given current power differentials.|
A Spark Fragment of THE First Cause.

The very thing that THE Primordial Paradox had mentioned when describing the resources of incalculable value that could be found in THE Prima Indifferentia. Not the full First Cause, of course, that would be something beyond even Absolutes to claim, but a fragment containing echoes of the moment when differentiation began.

Noah’s foundations trembled with hunger that had nothing to do with his Derivative Civilization of Infinite Hunger. This was pure desire, the recognition of something that could elevate his existence in ways that normal resources could never achieve.
And at this moment, as he was thinking about how he might acquire it...
|Critical Alert - Threat Approaching|

|Infinite Undifferentiated Fate has sensed the fate of collapse drawing closer from a specific direction. THE Undivided One, Bazuman, continues to track your existence through methods that your concealment cannot fully prevent. That relentless fucker is coming, and its arrival is estimated...soon?Soon.|
|You have limited time to make a decision.|
|Attempt acquisition of the Spark Fragment and risk confrontation with both the Primordial Serpent and Bazuman.|
|Or...well, there isn’t truly another viable option.|
He had never escaped the attention of an Undivided One that continued to chase him across THE Prima Indifferentia with persistence that bordered on obsession.

And a treasure lay right before him that could help cement his power even more, continuing to allow him to build a foundation that might just allow him to go against Absolutes even without having become one himself.
The Spark Fragment pulsed with another emission of undifferentiated light, and the Primordial Serpent’s countless eyes blinked with contentment as it absorbed the offering.
Behind him, somewhere in the churning expanse of THE Prima Indifferentia, Bazuman was approaching with million crimson eyes and endless jaws.

So when it came to this pivotal moment, Noah knew that his time in this temporal traversal might be nearing an end. He had already gained so much, had already transformed in ways that he couldn’t have anticipated, had already become something that had no precedent in Observable Existence.
But he was also greedy.
And greed, properly directed, was just another word for ambition.
"In for a penny, in for a pound."
He moved!

It had been here since before THE Infinite Unfurling.
It would likely be here long after.
And right now, it was watching a small crimson-gold seed that spun perpetually in the middle of this place with happiness that radiated from every one of its countless eyes.
The seed was no larger than a fist, but it burned with authority that made the surrounding Mobius strips of proto-matter bend toward it in reverence.

Routinely, the seed would release a flash of light that carried the quality of undifferentiation, pure potential in its most concentrated form, and the ancient creature would absorb this light as it made its existence feel that much richer.
It had enjoyed this sensation for cycles.
Sometimes, the continued sensation something brought was grander than consuming it in a single gulp.
The creature had learned this lesson long ago, and so it had been content to simply bask in the seed’s emissions rather than devour it entirely.
So the creature continued to enjoy the sensation this seed granted, its countless eyes blinking with contentment that spoke of simple pleasures appreciated across unfathomable spans of time.
Unbeknownst to it...
HUUM!
A storm of proto-matter arrived nearby, settling into the molten landscape as if it belonged there.
The storm had been measuring this situation for several seconds, observing the ancient creature and its treasure with attention that went beyond mere curiosity.
The storm of proto-matter was naturally Noah, and his gaze was sharp as he looked at the terrifying scene ahead of him from within his concealment.
|Environmental Analysis - High Value Target Detected|
|You are observing an ancient entity designated as a Primordial Serpent of Undifferentiated Coils.
Its power should rival or exceed weaker Absolutes, though its combat methodology would be fundamentally different from differentiated beings.|
|More significantly, you are observing the object it is benefiting from.|
|Object Classification: Spark Fragment of THE First Cause|
|This is a fragment that contains mere echoes of THE First Cause that initiated differentiation, but it is a fragment nonetheless.
Consuming or integrating this Spark Fragment would provide tremendous advancement to your foundations, potentially accelerating your growth by factors that cannot be accurately calculated.|
|The Primordial Serpent has been passively absorbing emissions from this Spark Fragment for eons rather than consuming it directly.|
|You could potentially integrate it where the Serpent could not.|
|However, acquiring it would require either defeating the Serpent or stealing the Fragment without detection.|
|Neither option carries favorable odds given current power differentials.|
A Spark Fragment of THE First Cause.
The very thing that THE Primordial Paradox had mentioned when describing the resources of incalculable value that could be found in THE Prima Indifferentia.
Not the full First Cause, of course, that would be something beyond even Absolutes to claim, but a fragment containing echoes of the moment when differentiation began.
Noah’s foundations trembled with hunger that had nothing to do with his Derivative Civilization of Infinite Hunger.
This was pure desire, the recognition of something that could elevate his existence in ways that normal resources could never achieve.
And at this moment, as he was thinking about how he might acquire it...
|Critical Alert - Threat Approaching|
|Infinite Undifferentiated Fate has sensed the fate of collapse drawing closer from a specific direction.
THE Undivided One, Bazuman, continues to track your existence through methods that your concealment cannot fully prevent.
That relentless fucker is coming, and its arrival is estimated...soon?Soon.|
|You have limited time to make a decision.|
|Attempt acquisition of the Spark Fragment and risk confrontation with both the Primordial Serpent and Bazuman.|
|Or...well, there isn’t truly another viable option.|
He had never escaped the attention of an Undivided One that continued to chase him across THE Prima Indifferentia with persistence that bordered on obsession.

And a treasure lay right before him that could help cement his power even more, continuing to allow him to build a foundation that might just allow him to go against Absolutes even without having become one himself.
The Spark Fragment pulsed with another emission of undifferentiated light, and the Primordial Serpent’s countless eyes blinked with contentment as it absorbed the offering.
Behind him, somewhere in the churning expanse of THE Prima Indifferentia, Bazuman was approaching with million crimson eyes and endless jaws.
So when it came to this pivotal moment, Noah knew that his time in this temporal traversal might be nearing an end.
He had already gained so much, had already transformed in ways that he couldn’t have anticipated, had already become something that had no precedent in Observable Existence.
But he was also greedy.
And greed, properly directed, was just another word for ambition.
"In for a penny, in for a pound."
He moved!

chapters.title: Chapter 4876: Last Gamble! II
paragraphs: The Primordial Serpent was moving languidly and basking in the glow of undifferentiation brought about by the Spark Fragment of THE First Cause.

Its power was mighty and its being was heavy to the point that its senses perceived all the countless changes occurring across this region of molten proto-matter. Every shift in the Mobius strips that curved around its domain registered against its awareness. Every fluctuation in the undefined potential that comprised its home was catalogued and assessed.
Nothing escaped its notice.
Nothing had escaped its notice for eons!
And at this moment, it felt like the proto-matter in the surroundings felt distinctly different.

The undefined substance that should have flowed in familiar patterns was behaving strangely, its currents shifting in ways that spoke of external influence rather than natural variation. Something was here that shouldn’t be here. Something was approaching that didn’t belong in this place.
But the moment it felt this, the moment its countless eyes began to turn toward the anomaly with attention that had ended the existence of many intruders across the ages...
BOOM!
Blue-gold light exploded across its domain.

Radiant seals erupted like a field of beautiful flowers blooming in impossible synchronization, each one manifesting from the proto-matter storm that had been concealing Noah’s existence. They spread outward in waves that multiplied infinitely, their petals burning with the devouring light of Infinite Hunger and the destabilizing quality of undifferentiation that this place had taught them to carry!

The devouring light of Infinite Hunger reached toward the Primordial Serpent with appetite that transcended normal consumption, seeking to break down its ancient existence into fuel for Noah’s ever-growing foundations. The undifferentiation quality pressed against the Serpent’s defined form with pressure that made even this native of THE Prima Indifferentia recoil in shock.
The Primordial Serpent was pushed back!

Its countless eyes widened with surprise that it hadn’t felt in eons, its massive form retreating from the field of infinite flowers that burned with authority it couldn’t immediately counter. For a single moment, its attention was entirely focused on the seals rather than what the seals were concealing.
And in that moment, the humanoid visage of Noah appeared right before the Spark Fragment of THE First Cause.

Something that a native of THE Prima Indifferentia had been holding onto and enjoying its constant boon for years beyond counting now had a thief standing before it, blue-gold light burning around a figure whose wings spread wide with infinity blazing through every feather.
What would Noah do to it?

Without even a delay, time seemed to slow as Noah flung his body forward with movement that committed everything to this single action. His jaws opened wide, wider than should have been possible for a humanoid form, stretching to accommodate what he was about to consume. His mouth wrapped around the entire area where the grain-sized Spark Fragment of THE First Cause spun in perpetual rotation.
And it disappeared down his throat!
Consumed in a single gulp after the Primordial Serpent had spent eons savoring its emissions rather than devouring it whole.
The Primordial Serpent saw this scene.
Its countless eyes, which had been watching with shock just moments before, now melted with sheer rage and lividity!

This was the fury of something that had just witnessed its most treasured possession, its companion across eons of existence, its source of joy and enrichment, eaten right in front of it by an intruder who had no right to be here.
As if an intruder had stripped his lover and taken them whole right before his eyes!
How dare he? How dare he?!
BOOM!
The molten proto-matter around them responded to its rage by churning with violence that made the Mobius strips shatter and reform in patterns of pure chaos.
A crimson pillar of undifferentiation erupted from the Primordial Serpent’s form.

The pillar wasn’t an attack in the conventional sense but rather a release of everything this ancient creature was, its full Depth and Immensity manifesting as a column of authority that made Noah’s infinite seals seem like flowers before a hurricane. The Serpent charged forward through the field of blue-gold petals, and where lesser beings would have been consumed by the Infinite Hunger quality or destabilized by the undifferentiation, the Primordial Serpent used its pure Depth to simply push through.
The infinite seals multiplied to replace those destroyed.
The Serpent destroyed them faster than they could multiply.
Its Depth was simply too immense, its existence too heavy, its rage too absolute!
The seals that could devour and undifferentiate attacks were being swept aside like leaves in a storm, pushed sideways by authority that had been accumulating since before THE Infinite Unfurling!
The Primordial Serpent appeared before Noah in an instant.

Its tail, a appendage that stretched for hundreds of miles and contained the concentrated weight of an existence older than the Earliest Folds itself, smashed into him with force that should have ended his temporal traversal immediately.
But Noah’s visage was valiant as he waited for this strike.
He didn’t try to dodge. He didn’t try to block. He used the force of the impact and his own Immensity to accomplish something that pure defense could never achieve.
He flung himself far back.

The tail strike that should have destroyed him instead became a catapult, launching his existence away from the enraged Serpent at speeds that turned him into a streak of blue-gold light. His velocity fuly attained the speed of Absolutes as he rocketed away from the molten region, away from the creature whose treasure he had just stolen, away from a fight he couldn’t possibly win!
He was making a run for it like any good thief should.
But at such a time...
"Found you, slippery thing."
WAA!
The voice came from everywhere and nowhere simultaneously, formed from concepts that hadn’t fully differentiated into sound.
"Come here."
BOOM!
Bazuman materialized in the space between Noah and freedom.

THE Undivided One’s entry was heralded by the cessation of all normal motion in the region, reality itself pausing to acknowledge the arrival of something that predated reality’s existence. Its form had shifted since their last encounter, now appearing as a mass of flesh and undefined potential that stretched across miles of space, but its million crimson eyes remained constant.
Those eyes were all focused on Noah.
The rageful Primordial Serpent, which had been charging forward with murderous intent toward the thief who had stolen its treasure, froze in place.
It was scared shitless.
But terror didn’t stop the situation from escalating.

Bazuman stood still, its million crimson eyes opening fully as every single one of them released a terrifying suctioning force that pulled everything in the nearby light years toward its position. The molten proto-matter that comprised this region began flowing toward the Undivided One like water toward a drain. The Mobius strips that had been curving through undefined space straightened as they were drawn toward that central point of consumption.
All proto-matter was being pulled in.
All things were being pulled in.

Even the Primordial Serpent was included in this gravitational nightmare, its massive form being dragged toward Bazuman despite its attempts to resist. Its rage and madness returned as it realized it was now caught between the thief who had stolen its treasure and another Undivided One who would consume them both without discrimination.
It roared toward Bazuman with fury born of desperation.
But its hateful gaze remained fixed on Noah, who was currently being pulled back toward The Undivided One alongside everything else in this region of THE Prima Indifferentia.
He couldn’t run.

The suctioning force was too strong, too absolute, too fundamental to resist through conventional means. His streak of blue-gold light was being dragged backward despite his velocity of Absolute speeds, the pull of Bazuman’s million eyes overwhelming everything he threw against it.
And by all means, he should be scared shitless right now.

He should be terrified like the Primordial Serpent was terrified, facing an enemy that could consume Absolutes without effort and had been hunting him across THE Prima Indifferentia with persistence that bordered on obsession.
But...
DUM!
What he had just swallowed was making his existence pulse with excitement and Immensity that he couldn’t explain.

The Spark Fragment of THE First Cause was dissolving into his foundations, and the echoes of the moment when differentiation began were flooding through his existence with authority that made everything else seem small.
He felt...he felt...! Fuck, he couldn’t even explain how he felt!
He wanted to howl.
He wanted to roar.
He wanted to release the joy and exhilaration of having consumed something that most beings in Observable Existence would never even see, let alone integrate into their foundations.
But... well, he needed to run.
So while gazing at the terrifying Undivided One that he couldn’t beat even if he attained the power of an Absolute, Noah’s existence pulsed as he began to speak...
Gibberish.
The gibberish required to open The Interstices.

The undefined Phoneme that would create a doorway to the spaces between spaces, the routes that could carry him away from this place and back toward safety as he would utilize Temporal Traversal to return.
But as he did...
"Youngest, don’t!"
HUUM!

From a far distance, cutting through even the suctioning force of Bazuman’s million eyes, Noah saw the materialization of THE Primordial Paradox. The ancient Absolute’s obsidian form had appeared at the edge of this region, his expression one of solemnity and alarm as if Noah had done something he absolutely shouldn’t have.
But Noah had already committed.

He sent a message rapidly through waves of undifferentiation that carried his intent across the distance between them, his thoughts pressing into THE Primordial Paradox’s perception with urgency that couldn’t be delayed.
"I will see you soon. Not here, but eons from now."
And as Noah looked over toward THE Primordial Paradox, completing the gibberish that would open The Interstices, he also saw that beside the ancient Absolute there was someone else.
Someone who looked oddly familiar.
Someone whose features seemed to shift between a scholarly explorer and something far older, far more powerful, far more connected to THE Prima Indifferentia than any visitor should be.
Noah blinked as if his eyes were playing tricks on him.
But he had already spoken the gibberish.
The undefined Phoneme had already left his existence.
And in the next moment...
CRACK!
A Crack of Observable Existence appeared where Noah was, tearing through the fabric of THE Prima Indifferentia with force that made even Bazuman’s suctioning eyes pause in surprise.
Noah disappeared into it.
But moments before he vanished entirely, he realized what THE Primordial Paradox had been referring to when he said "don’t."
They had entered THE Prima Indifferentia through the Crack of Observable Existence, not through The Interstices.
It seemed there was a reason for this.
THE Prima Indifferentia couldn’t be reached through The Interstices because it existed in a state that predated the spaces between spaces.
So if one sought to open The Interstices while inside of THE Prima Indifferentia...
"Oh."

Noah only had this thought of understanding before everything disappeared around him, the crack swallowing his existence and carrying him toward a destination that he hadn’t chosen and couldn’t predict.
What was left behind in THE Prima Indifferentia was chaos of a different kind.

The Primordial Serpent roared with madness that had lost its target, its countless eyes searching for the thief who had stolen its treasure and finding nothing but the crack that was already closing. Its rage had nowhere to go, its fury had no outlet, and the loss of its Spark Fragment pressed against its ancient existence with weight that would take eons to process.
Bazuman stood silent!
THE Undivided One’s million crimson eyes had stopped their suctioning force the moment the crack appeared, its attention entirely focused on the anomaly that had just occurred.
And at the edge of this region, THE Primordial Paradox and Jack stood together, with the former looking toward Bazuman with a sharp gaze.
THE Primordial Paradox’s obsidian eyes held irritation that burned cold.

This Undivided One had been chasing THE Youngest across THE Prima Indifferentia, had forced him into increasingly desperate measures, had caused him to make a choice that opened a crack that shouldn’t have been opened from this side!
And now THE Youngest was gone.

THE Primordial Paradox stared at Bazuman with eyes that held the promise of consequences, but...who knew how this encounter unfolded and finished as at this moment, a thief was either given a recompense to breathe and enjoy his boon, or he may have just neen extinguished entirely!

chapters.title: Chapter 4877: Echoes! I
paragraphs: Noah had eaten a lot of things across his life.
Some good, some bad, some tantalizing beyond description.
Some things he ate on a regular basis as he never stopped. He had consumed Absolute Everythings and Weavings of collapsed entities and treasures that entire civilizations would have gone to war over.
The Spark Fragment of THE First Cause instantly shot up to the number one spot of things he would love to be eating every day.

As ludicrous as it was to mention it, the sensation flooding through his existence made everything else he had ever consumed feel like pale imitations of what food should actually be. Every aspect of his being was amplified, every fiber of his foundations singing with pleasure.
He imagined this was the type of high that drug addicts felt, the kind that kept them going back even if they were destroying their lives in the process!
Because damn.
The things he would do for this sensation.
He would fight Bazuman again. He would steal from a thousand Primordial Serpents! He would challenge THE Undivided Ones themselves if it meant experiencing this feeling one more time.
But...
HUUM!

His existence buzzed with Immensity as he forced himself not to be lost in the sensation, pulling his consciousness back from the edge of euphoria in order to truly understand what was happening to his existence. The pleasure was seductive, yes, but pleasure without understanding was just distraction from the truth of what he was becoming.
And...
And...?
"Hmm?"
He wasn’t seeing any immense and unfathomable changes that he expected.

Yes, his foundation was rising rapidly across Surface, Intermediate, and Fundamental Depths. He could feel the weight of his existence growing heavier with every passing moment, his Immensity scaling upward at rates that should have been impossible.
But... he felt like this shouldn’t be it.
He was looking for something truly grand.

A Spark Fragment of THE First Cause, a piece of the very moment when differentiation began, and all it was doing was making his foundation heavier? That seemed almost anticlimactic given what he had risked to acquire it!
He had stolen from an ancient Primordial Serpent, had been chased by an Undivided One, had opened The Interstices in a place where The Interstices should never have been opened.
For foundation growth?
He frowned as he didn’t understand, but this moment of reflection allowed him to focus as he looked around him.

He had attempted to enter The Interstices when he apparently should not have, and right now he was somewhere that defied easy description. The space around him wasn’t differentiated in the way that Observable Existence was differentiated, but it also wasn’t undifferentiated in the way that THE Prima Indifferentia was undifferentiated.
It was somewhere in between.
Somewhere that shouldn’t exist.
|Critical Navigation Error - Existential Analysis|

|Accessing the spaces between spaces while within a region of undifferentiation would normally result in the collapse of even Absolutes. The combination of differentiated pathways and undifferentiated origin creates paradoxical weavings that trap existence in endless loops between definition and undefinition.|

|However, the weavings of your Infinities paired with the consumption of the Spark Fragment of THE First Cause are funneling your existence across these treacherous pathways without collapse. You are surviving what should not be survivable.|
|The issue is navigation rather than survival.|

|To define yourself at a certain time and location, existential coordinates would need to be viable and established within the weavings you are currently crossing. You would need to specify where you wish to emerge and when you wish to emerge there.|

|But due to the weavings of unclear and chaotic definition and undefinition surrounding everything in this space, no known coordinates of locations or times are currently viable for selection. The pathways cannot distinguish between differentiated destinations because they themselves are not fully and stably differentiated.|
|In simpler terms: you cannot choose where to go because the paths cannot understand what "where" means.|

The prompts may have been hard to understand at first, but Noah’s eyes turned sharp as he realized they were basically saying that he was funneling across regions that had no clear stable definition. And because these regions had no clear definition, he couldn’t give them clear coordinates of where to go.
So he couldn’t leave.
So...was he just lost here endlessly, trapped in spaces between spaces that would carry him forever without ever depositing him anywhere real?
He shook his head at such a thought as the one thing he could appreciate about this place being both defined and undefined was that time didn’t seem to be a factor here.
And he loved having a moment to breathe.

For the first time since entering THE Prima Indifferentia, he actually had space to think without being chased by Undivided Ones or threatened by Formless Terrors or forced to make split-second decisions that determined whether his temporal traversal continued or ended.
Right now, he wanted to figure out exactly what was going on with the weavings of THE First Cause.

Surely the boons of something so grand would not be as disappointing as his foundations simply being elevated, right? There had to be more. There had to be something that justified the significance of what he had consumed!

He looked deep within himself where the grain-sized object spun rapidly at the center of his Organ of Civilization, his Infinities breaking down its authority with appetite. What was being broken down was scaling his foundation upward with speed that made his previous growth look glacial by comparison.

|The Immensity of your Fundamental Depth has undergone the most significant transformation.|
|Your Fundamental Depth has now reached the same level as THE Primordial Paradox and THE Creature before they took their steps to become Absolutes.|
|It is untested and purely theoretical, but as of right now, your collective Immensity may be arriving at the level of weak Absolutes, even without having attained this stage yourself.|
|Your Depth remains at Infinite Formless, but your weight may rival those who have transcended to Absolute. Weak Absolute. It cannot be stressed enough- hypothetically weak Absolutes.|
|This configuration has no precedent and requires verification through actual combat to confirm.|

sentences.text: Noah had eaten a lot of things across his life.
Some good, some bad, some tantalizing beyond description.
Some things he ate on a regular basis as he never stopped.
He had consumed Absolute Everythings and Weavings of collapsed entities and treasures that entire civilizations would have gone to war over.
The Spark Fragment of THE First Cause instantly shot up to the number one spot of things he would love to be eating every day.
As ludicrous as it was to mention it, the sensation flooding through his existence made everything else he had ever consumed feel like pale imitations of what food should actually be.
Every aspect of his being was amplified, every fiber of his foundations singing with pleasure.
He imagined this was the type of high that drug addicts felt, the kind that kept them going back even if they were destroying their lives in the process!
Because damn.
The things he would do for this sensation.
He would fight Bazuman again.
He would steal from a thousand Primordial Serpents!
He would challenge THE Undivided Ones themselves if it meant experiencing this feeling one more time.
But...
HUUM!

His existence buzzed with Immensity as he forced himself not to be lost in the sensation, pulling his consciousness back from the edge of euphoria in order to truly understand what was happening to his existence.
The pleasure was seductive, yes, but pleasure without understanding was just distraction from the truth of what he was becoming.
And...
And...?
"Hmm?"
He wasn’t seeing any immense and unfathomable changes that he expected.
Yes, his foundation was rising rapidly across Surface, Intermediate, and Fundamental Depths.
He could feel the weight of his existence growing heavier with every passing moment, his Immensity scaling upward at rates that should have been impossible.
But... he felt like this shouldn’t be it.
He was looking for something truly grand.
A Spark Fragment of THE First Cause, a piece of the very moment when differentiation began, and all it was doing was making his foundation heavier?
That seemed almost anticlimactic given what he had risked to acquire it!
He had stolen from an ancient Primordial Serpent, had been chased by an Undivided One, had opened The Interstices in a place where The Interstices should never have been opened.
For foundation growth?
He frowned as he didn’t understand, but this moment of reflection allowed him to focus as he looked around him.
He had attempted to enter The Interstices when he apparently should not have, and right now he was somewhere that defied easy description.
The space around him wasn’t differentiated in the way that Observable Existence was differentiated, but it also wasn’t undifferentiated in the way that THE Prima Indifferentia was undifferentiated.
It was somewhere in between.
Somewhere that shouldn’t exist.

|The issue is navigation rather than survival.|

chapters.title: Chapter 4878: Echoes! II
paragraphs: So his foundation was reaching tremendous levels!

His Fundamental Depth, which had been so hard to raise and which represented the truest measurement of his potential before grasping Absolute, had now reached the level of THE Creature and THE Primordial Paradox before they became what they became.

After his movements across THE Prima Indifferentia, after the passive absorption of proto-matter through his Infinities, after swallowing the Spark Fragment of THE First Cause, his foundation had been elevated enough to rival what the greatest Absolutes had forged before their ascension.
It was all grand.
It was all impressive beyond what he could have hoped for when he first entered THE Prima Indifferentia.
But still, Noah felt like something was missing.

The harvest and potential of the Spark Fragment of THE First Cause continued to fill his existence, but it felt like only a portion was actually going to his foundation. The vast majority seemed to be suffusing into every nook and cranny of something else entirely.
His Infinities.
His Mind.
His Civilization.
Parts of his existence that weren’t measured by foundation weight alone.

His existence began to buzz as he focused on himself truly and fully, setting aside the distraction of his growing weight to observe the subtler changes occurring within. As he barreled across weavings of definition and undefinition, carried by currents that had no destination, something else began to make itself known.
HUUM!
He felt like he began to hear...a voice.

A grand voice that felt like his own voice but filled with an unfathomable weaving of majesty that transcended anything he had ever produced. It was him speaking to himself across time, or perhaps it was something older than him using his voice as a vessel for communication.
Echoes of differentiation’s birth flooded through his existence, and a voice that was not a voice spoke words that were not words into his consciousness.
THE First Cause.
He felt like he... was touching that moment through the Spark Fragment.
He was experiencing echoes of what had occurred when differentiation began.

And with it, he felt like he could glimpse musings of things he knew and things he didn’t know, of future possibilities that may or may not happen, of paths that branched infinitely from the crossroads of his current existence.
To the point that as he spun across existence, carried by weavings that had no name, he heard it.
A booming voice that felt like it was his and not his.
"When the Youngest walks where the Oldest slumber, Existence shall tremble and the Weave shall fray. He who holds infinity in mortal palms shall stand at the crossroads where all rivers end.

The Paradox shall fall before the Paradox rises. The father consumed by the son, the son consumed by the purpose, the purpose consumed by the question that birthed all questions. Three collapses for the price of one, and in the third collapse, the door shall crack.

Beware the Unity that wears the face of peace. Beware the Legion that marches without banners. They shall come as whispers in the foundation, as cracks in the certainty, as the gentle erosion that unmakes mountains. Where they pass, definition dies. Where they gather, possibility ends.

The Shroud of Endless Blue shall fall upon Observable Existence. It shall be both salvation and damnation, both the key and the lock, both the bridge and the chasm. Under its weight, the doors of the Scales shall open or the doors of the Scales shall shatter. There is no third path. There is no middle ground. There is only the choice that is not a choice.

When Chaos speaks with the tongue of Order, when Existence questions its own being, when the Tongue falls silent and the Paradox emerges, then shall the Era of Undifferentiation begin. Absolutes shall be unleashed. The First shall become the Last. The Many shall become the One. The One shall become the None.
Yet in the None, a spark remains.

The adversity that breaks all others shall forge him. The hardship that ends all paths shall begin his. The Scales demand what the Scales demand, and he shall pay in currencies that have not yet been minted.He shall pay the price he deems.
Three times shall he face the mirror of undoing. Three times shall he choose between becoming and unbecoming. Three times shall the answer be the same, and three times shall the answer be different.
In the end, which is also the beginning, the Infinite shall stand before the Undefined. And one side shall remain to tell the tale that no one shall hear.
This is an Echo of First Cause.
This is what shall come to pass, for it has already passed, and it shall pass again.
The wheel turns. The river flows. The question echoes.
He shall be the answer, or he shall be nothing.
Or he shall be the question that ends all answers."
BOOM!

Noah’s existence was dazed as he heard what was deemed an Echo of THE First Cause repeating itself in his mind, the words burning into his consciousness with weight that made his foundations tremble despite their newly elevated state.
There were some heavy words in the Echoes Noah had heard!

Even the first line was heavy as Noah thought about it, the words burning in his consciousness with weight that refused to fade even as the euphoria of consumption continued to flood through his existence.
"When the Youngest walks where the Oldest slumber, Existence shall tremble and the Weave shall fray. He who holds infinity in mortal palms shall stand at the crossroads where all rivers end."

This should be fully referring to him as THE Youngest. And the Oldest slumber, was that... referring to THE Prima Indifferentia itself where THE Undivided Ones existed in states of perpetual non-differentiation? Or was it referring to the spaces he was currently barreling across, these weavings between definition and undefinition that seemed to exist outside of normal reality? Or...Chaos, since Chaos was supposedly the oldest?
And the crossroads where all rivers end...
His eyes shone brightly as he thought about what all of this could mean, what future events the prophecy was pointing toward, what choices awaited him at destinations he couldn’t yet perceive.
But the next set of words were even heavier.

"The Paradox shall fall before the Paradox rises. The father consumed by the son, the son consumed by the purpose, the purpose consumed by the question that birthed all questions. Three collapses for the price of one, and in the third collapse, the door shall crack."
Now this one painted future possibilities of what would happen very soon in ways that made his foundations pulse with the weight of foreknowledge.
The first part should relate to THE Primordial Paradox and THE Living Paradox, with the ancient master being consumed by his disciple. The father consumed by the son was clear enough.
But the son consumed by the purpose?
And the purpose consumed by the question that birthed all questions...
Three collapses for the price of one.
In the third collapse, the door shall crack.

Noah thought about all the possibilities as the prophecy continued to echo in the depths of his consciousness, each line carrying weight that demanded analysis and interpretation. There was so much to unpack, so much to understand, and he was currently tumbling through spaces that had no reference points for time or distance!

chapters.title: Chapter 4879: THE Civilizational Instinctus! I
paragraphs: "Decipher as much as you can, and let me know your theories on what it could all mean later."
He gave this command to RUINATION as he continued to funnel across existence, trusting her to work through the prophecy’s meanings while he focused on more immediate concerns.
|Understood, Master|
|I will compile comprehensive analysis of the Echo of First Cause and present theories when you have time to review them|
Her affirmation came as Noah continued to focus on himself.

The echoes he heard were grand, but they were still not the main thing that he was getting from devouring that Spark Fragment. The prophecy was important, yes, but it was information about the future rather than power in the present.
As the Spark Fragment continued to permeate Immensity across his existence, he felt like he could see.
Not in the same manner as Lens of Civilization.
Not even as THE Weaver of Existence.
He felt like all of these were being taken to another level entirely.

Not simply being able to see, but he could feel so much that it was truly hard to explain. His entire existence was overwhelmed with sensory sensations as information seemed to be coming in from all around, data flooding into his consciousness from angles that shouldn’t have existed and perspectives that transcended everything.
BOOM!
Around his body, blue-gold billowing flames rose and shone brilliantly as the overflow of information formed into prompts that crystallized the chaos into understanding he could actually process.
|The echoes of THE First Cause have finished permeating across your existence|
|The moment when differentiation began has left its imprint upon your foundations, granting you perspective that only those who have touched the origin of all things can possess|
|You now see existence not as it appears, but as it truly is|
Noah felt the truth of these words resonating through every aspect of his being, the fundamental shift in perception that the Spark Fragment had catalyzed now reaching its completion.
|New Existential Capability Unlocked|
|Designation: THE Civilizational Instinctus|
|Also known as: THE Gnosis Ruinae, or THE Praescientia Civitatis|

|This capability is only attained by those whose foundations have grown heavy enough to approach the threshold of THE Second Scale of Existence. It represents a fundamental shift in how you perceive and interact with the Civilizations of others, granting you instinctive understanding of structural foundations.|
BOOM!
So this was what the Spark Fragment’s true boon was!
Okay.
Okay!
Not just foundation elevation, though that alone would have been worth the risks he had taken, but a fundamental transformation in how he perceived reality itself!
|Primary Function: Autonomous Existential Response|

|Your existence now reacts to threats and opportunities before your conscious mind processes them. Your Civilization moves with purpose that transcends thought, your Seals manifesting and your Infinities flaring in response to dangers you have not yet perceived with your awareness. This is not prediction or foresight but rather your existence acting on knowledge that bypasses the delay of conscious processing.|
|You do not think and then move. You simply respond, and the thinking catches up afterward.|

|Against opponents of equivalent or lesser Depth, your existence will automatically position itself in optimal configurations for both offense and defense. Against opponents of greater Depth, this autonomous response will buy you precious moments that conscious reaction could never provide.|
Noah’s eyes shone with understanding as he processed this first function.
His body would move before his mind commanded it to move!
|Secondary Function: Manifestation Observation|

|When you focus your attention upon any entity possessing a Civilization, you now perceive something that was previously invisible. Behind their physical form, surrounding their existence like a second body made of pure authority, you observe the Manifestation of their Civilization in its entirety.|

|This Manifestation appears as an architectural construct unique to each entity. For some, it may appear as a towering citadel with walls representing their defenses and towers representing their offensive capabilities. For others, it may appear as a vast network of roots and branches, or as a constellation of orbiting structures, or as something that defies conventional description entirely.|

|The form of the Manifestation reflects the nature of the Civilization it represents. A Civilization built on conquest will appear martial and aggressive. A Civilization built on knowledge will appear scholarly and layered. A Civilization built on paradox will appear contradictory and shifting.|
This was even grander than the first function!
|Tertiary Function: Structural Analysis|

|Within each observed Manifestation, you perceive points of vulnerability that the entity themselves may not even be aware of. These appear as cracks in walls, as rotting foundations, as pillars that bear too much weight, as connections that are fraying under strain. Every Civilization, no matter how grand, possesses weaknesses born from the choices made during its construction.|
|The clearer you perceive an entity, the more vulnerabilities you identify. Proximity, duration of observation, and relative Depth all influence the clarity of your analysis.|
So not only could he see Civilizations, but he could see their weaknesses!
|Quaternary Function: Targeted Undifferentiation|

|Having identified vulnerabilities within a Manifestation, you may now direct your attacks specifically toward those weak points. Your Authority of Infinite Undifferentiated Fate, when launched at identified vulnerabilities, carries additional effectiveness. A strike against a weakness does not simply damage. It undifferentiates.|

|The targeted aspect of their Civilization begins to blur, to lose definition, to revert toward the proto-state that existed before differentiation. A pillar struck at its stress point doesn’t merely crack but begins to forget that it was ever a pillar. A wall attacked at its weakest section doesn’t merely crumble but starts questioning whether it was ever meant to be a wall.|

|Repeated strikes against the same vulnerability compound this effect. What begins as minor instability grows into structural failure. What starts as a hairline crack expands into a chasm that threatens the entire Manifestation.|
Noah felt his existence trembling with the implications of this function.
THE Prima Indifferentia had taught him well, and now he could bring those lessons to bear against anyone who stood in his way!
